items.title: Leilão do pré-sal negocia 7 áreas para Petrobras, Prio, Equinor, Galp, Sinopec e CNOOC
items.author: Marta Nogueira, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.creator: Marta Nogueira, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.summary: Sete blocos exploratórios de petróleo e gás no pré-sal foram arrematados nesta quarta-feira por empresas como Petrobras, Prio Forte, Equinor, Galp, Sinopec e CNOOC, em leilão que não registrou disputas, de acordo com resultados apresentados pela Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP).
items.body:
Sete blocos exploratórios de petróleo e gás no pré-sal foram arrematados nesta quarta-feira por empresas como Petrobras, Prio Forte, Equinor, Galp, Sinopec e CNOOC, em leilão que não registrou disputas, de acordo com resultados apresentados pela Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP).
Seis blocos ofertados, contudo, não tiveram interesse, já que o mercado considera que grande parte dos blocos do pré-sal com potenciais maiores já foi comercializada pelo governo brasileiro.
O leilão resultou em uma arrecadação de R$530,47 milhões em bônus fixos de assinatura à União, que também levou dos arrematantes o direito de parte do petróleo a ser produzido no futuro.
O investimento exploratório previsto nas áreas somou R$778,43 milhões, de acordo com o balanço apresentado pela ANP.
A Petrobras (PETR3.SA) arrematou os blocos Azurita, na Bacia de Campos, e Cruzeiro do Sul, na Bacia de Santos, oferecendo percentuais de excedente em óleo de 30,0% e 15,27%, respectivamente.
Os ágios em relação ao excedente mínimo de óleo alcançaram 139,81% em Azurita e 8,07% em Cruzeiro do Sul, segundo dados da ANP.
A operação com maior ágio da rodada foi registrada no bloco Rodocrosita, na Bacia de Santos, arrematado por consórcio formado pela norueguesa Equinor e a portuguesa Galp. O lance vencedor ofereceu excedente em óleo de 15,52% para a União, um ágio de 494,64% ante o percentual mínimo previsto.
A brasileira Prio foi a vencedora dos blocos Magnetita e Hematita, ambos na Bacia de Campos. Em Magnetita, a empresa ofertou excedente em óleo de 32,8% para a União, com ágio de 132,79%, enquanto em Hematita apresentou proposta de 7,18%, equivalente a ágio de 315,03%.
O bloco Jade foi vencido pelo consórcio formado pelas chinesas CNOOC e Sinopec, com oferta de 18,2% de excedente em óleo para a União, representando ágio de 65,76%.
Já o bloco Rubi foi arrematado pela Equinor Brasil, com oferta de 25,02% de excedente em óleo e ágio de 91,72%.
Os blocos Turmalina, Larimar, Aragonita, Opala, Granada e Cerussita não receberam oferta.

items.title: Brazil Stocks Lure Record $2 Billion Inflow on Election Surprise
items.author: Giovanna Serafim
items.creator: Giovanna Serafim
items.summary: Foreign investors poured a record net 10.06 billion reais ($2.01 billion) into Brazilian stocks listed in Sao Paulo on Oct. 5, the highest single-day inflow on record, amid increased hopes that opposition presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro would address the country’s mounting fiscal problems and pave the way for interest-rate cuts if he is elected. The data was released by Brazilian exchange B3 SA on Wednesday.

items.title: Exportação de carne de frango do Brasil cresce em setembro com antecipação de cargas para UE
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: As exportações brasileiras de carne de frango totalizaram 500,3 mil toneladas em setembro, alta de 3,7% sobre o mesmo mês de 2025, com uma antecipação de maiores fluxos para a União Europeia, que proibiu a produção nacional certificada após o dia 3, afirmou a Associação Brasileira de Proteína Animal (ABPA) nesta quarta-feira.
items.body:
As exportações brasileiras de carne de frango totalizaram 500,3 mil toneladas em setembro, alta de 3,7% sobre o mesmo mês de 2025, com uma antecipação de maiores fluxos para a União Europeia, que proibiu a produção nacional certificada após o dia 3, afirmou a Associação Brasileira de Proteína Animal (ABPA) nesta quarta-feira.
A receita alcançou US$984,2 milhões, avanço de 14,7% na mesma comparação.
A União Europeia foi o segundo principal destino da carne de frango brasileira em setembro, com 43,5 mil toneladas, ante apenas 3,9 mil toneladas no mesmo período do ano passado.
O aumento se deve a uma antecipação de embarques, mas também a uma pequena base de comparação --no mesmo período do ano passado, os embarques ainda eram pressionados por embargos sanitários decorrentes de um caso de gripe aviária em granja comercial.
No caso da União Europeia, o resultado de setembro de 2026 inclui cargas produzidas e certificadas até 2 de setembro, explicou o presidente da ABPA, Ricardo Santin, em nota.
A suspensão temporária da emissão de novos certificados para a UE entrou em vigor no dia 3, sem impedir o embarque dos produtos que já haviam cumprido essa etapa, acrescentou ele.
A antecipação de volumes por exportadores e importadores também contribuiu para reduzir os efeitos imediatos da medida, disse Santin.
A União Europeia retirou o Brasil da lista de países autorizados a exportar depois que considerou que o país não cumpriu normas sobre antimicrobianos.
Os Emirados Árabes Unidos foram o principal destino da carne de frango brasileira em setembro, com 45,9 mil toneladas, volume 23,3% superior na comparação anual.
Já a China importou 40,9 mil toneladas, ante somente 51 toneladas em setembro de 2025 -- os chineses levaram mais tempo para retomar compras do produto brasileiro, após o caso de gripe aviária em maio do ano passado.
No acumulado de janeiro a setembro, os embarques do maior exportador global de carne de frango chegaram a 4,4 milhões de toneladas, crescimento de 14% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. A receita acumulada atingiu US$8,7 bilhões, avanço de 21%, segundo a ABPA.

items.title: Wildfire ash turns Spanish mountain river black, contaminating water supply
items.author: Susana Vera
items.creator: Susana Vera
items.summary: A river running through a town in central Spain has turned black from wildfire ash and debris, contaminating the local drinking water and forcing residents to rely on emergency supplies.
items.body:
A river running through a town in central Spain has turned black from wildfire ash and debris, contaminating the local drinking water and forcing residents to rely on emergency supplies.
In the town of Casavieja in Avila province, where fast mountain streams flow into the Tietar River, the churning waters were inky black from ash-laden runoff. Residents queued at fountains and tanker trucks to fill canisters with clear drinking water, and authorities distributed water in bottles.
"To drink, to cook, for the bathroom, for everything. Water: you only realize how much you need it once you don't have it anymore," said resident Miguel Angel Perez Sanchez.
Casavieja Mayor Vanessa Muñoz said torrential rains had compounded the damage caused by the fires, washing away bridges and carrying runoff into a reservoir that serves as a backup water source for the town.
"It affected us mainly because it entered the reservoir, which was our water supply and our emergency plan when the first rains arrived," she told the regional broadcaster Castilla y Leon TV.
Santiago M. Barajas, an agronomist and co-founder of environmental group Ecologistas en Accion, wrote on X: "The impacts of the fires continue after they have been extinguished."
"After torrential rains, the water barely filters into the soil without vegetation and rushes away muddy at great speed, as if the ashes had made it impermeable."
In the nearby town of Piedralaves, authorities and water utility Aqualia were working to restore normal supplies after ash washed into water catchments following recent rains, prompting officials to declare tap water unfit for consumption.
The affected area lies downstream from the Burgohondo wildfire in Avila, one of Spain's largest blazes this year, which burned 33,943 hectares (83,875 acres), accounting for more than 15% of the total area destroyed by wildfires nationwide, according to Environment Ministry data.
Jose Maria Manso, mayor of nearby El Barraco, said ash and sediment could eventually reach the El Burguillo reservoir, a key source of drinking water for surrounding communities.

items.title: US SEC will not pursue charges against climate group, warns of disclosure obligations
items.author: Chris Prentice, Ross Kerber
items.creator: Chris Prentice, Ross Kerber
items.summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission disclosed in a report on Wednesday that it had investigated the actions of a climate group in connection with a May 2021 ExxonMobil shareholder meeting and has chosen not to pursue charges against it.
items.body:
The US Securities and Exchange Commission disclosed in a report on Wednesday that it had investigated the actions of a climate group in connection with a May 2021 ExxonMobil shareholder meeting and has chosen not to pursue charges against it.
But the SEC warned that it had concerns about actions by the group, known as Climate Action 100+, and said that ahead of the 2027 proxy season, large shareholders need to understand their regulatory obligations.
Climate Action 100+ and ExxonMobil did not respond immediately to a request for comment.
Exxon's shareholder meeting in 2021 became a flashpoint in a broader debate about how much investors -- and Corporate America -- should take account of nontraditional factors, such as climate change issues, in their decision-making.
At the meeting, major investment firms including BlackRock, Vanguard and State Street backed some dissident directors from a slate put forward by activist hedge fund Engine No. 1, which argued the Texas company needed to focus on the energy transition.
Since then, various Republican politicians, often from energy-producing states, have harshly criticized asset managers over their environmental and social stances, saying their attention could violate antitrust laws.

items.title: Colômbia revoga decreto que limitava investimentos de fundos de pensão no exterior
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O governo recém-empossado da Colômbia revogou um decreto que limitava os investimentos de fundos de pensão privados no exterior a 30%, afirmou o ministro da Fazenda, Miguel Gomez, nesta quarta-feira.
items.body:
O governo recém-empossado da Colômbia revogou um decreto que limitava os investimentos de fundos de pensão privados no exterior a 30%, afirmou o ministro da Fazenda, Miguel Gomez, nesta quarta-feira.
O decreto anterior, emitido em abril passado pelo governo do ex-presidente Gustavo Petro, tinha como objetivo obrigar os fundos de pensão a repatriar capital para impulsionar investimentos em infraestrutura e projetos econômicos nacionais.
“Ao remover essa restrição, os fundos poderão diversificar melhor suas carteiras, acessar mais mercados e buscar retornos mais elevados”, disse Gomez em uma mensagem gravada.
A associação setorial Asofondos informou que as gestoras de fundos privados da Colômbia, entre as quais se incluem Porvenir, Proteccion, Colfondos e Old Mutual, administram uma carteira combinada de aproximadamente 579 trilhões de pesos (US$179 bilhões) em nome de quase 20 milhões de participantes.
A regra anterior exigia a repatriação gradual de mais de 100 trilhões de pesos (US$30,9 bilhões) para a economia colombiana, segundo a Asofondos. Atualmente, os investimentos estrangeiros representam aproximadamente 48% da carteira total dos fundos, o que equivale a quase 278 trilhões de pesos (US$85,8 bilhões).
O decreto anterior corria o risco de provocar uma forte valorização do peso em relação ao dólar e elevar artificialmente os preços dos ativos domésticos.
“Estamos corrigindo essa política antes que ela entre em vigor e tenha qualquer impacto significativo”, acrescentou Gomez.
(Reportagem de Carlos Vargas e Nelson Bocanegra)

items.title: Retaining key LIV players an 'achievable hurdle' for new investors
items.author: Alan Baldwin
items.creator: Alan Baldwin
items.summary: LIV Golf faces a challenge to retain key players as the professional men's league restructures under Chapter 11 protection but it is a 'very achievable hurdle in a short period of time", the head of new investors BC Partners Credit said on Wednesday.
items.body:
LIV Golf faces a challenge to retain key players as the professional men's league restructures under Chapter 11 protection but it is a 'very achievable hurdle in a short period of time", the head of new investors BC Partners Credit said on Wednesday.
With financial backing from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) drying up, LIV last month started a [USN:L4N4501MD TEXT:"court-supervised restructuring process"] that it hopes to complete in early 2027.
BC Partners Credit [USN:L4N45R1JI TEXT:"announced on Monday"] an initial committed investment and said it planned to provide up to $300 million in financing.
Ted Goldthorpe, partner and head of BC Partners Credit, told the Leaders Week London sports business conference that he saw LIV as a great opportunity.
"Every layer of the onion that we peel back on this thing, the more excited we are about the investment," he said.
"The thing that's really fun about this one is in all of our other leagues, the players are on the other side of the table. In this situation, the players are our partners. The players own the teams with us... you're 100% aligned with the talent. That is really rare in sports."
LIV Golf launched in 2022 and lured leading players from the PGA Tour with lucrative contracts. The next phase envisages players becoming equity owners of both the league and its teams.
Several of those stars, including Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson and Cameron Smith, are listed in the Chapter 11 filing as creditors still owed millions in unsecured claims.
"If we can show people that this is a sustainable business and league, those teams have tonnes of value. My guess is, over time, this will begin to look a lot more like Formula One or other leagues that are analogous to what we're trying to do," said Goldthorpe.
LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil likened it to "a rocket ship, waiting to take off", with LIV playing on five continents last year and aiming for five or six next year.
He said relationships with television partners remained strong, with Fox "holding windows for us".
Goldthorpe said every CEO in the world and major sponsors wanted to be involved with golf, and sounded bullish about the future.
"When we emerge from bankruptcy, you'll be surprised at the calibre and quality of people who invest alongside of us. It's all sports owners, billionaires, people who understand what we're trying to do," he said.
He said BC Partners would "lean on Scott and his team to run the league, and our job is to help with strategy, media and also we have this holding company that we're going to build assets around. So, we can use LIV to help monetise other things... media brands, consumer products.
"There's a lot of cross-selling sponsors. So, really, what I'm going to be focused on is more like the holding company and creating value for our players and ourselves."

LONDON, Oct 7 : LIV Golf faces a challenge to retain key players as the professional men's league restructures under Chapter 11 protection but it is a 'very achievable hurdle in a short period of time", the head of new investors BC Partners Credit said on Wednesday.
With financial backing from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) drying up, LIV last month started a court-supervised restructuring process that it hopes to complete in early 2027.
BC Partners Credit announced on Monday an initial committed investment and said it planned to provide up to $300 million in financing.
Ted Goldthorpe, partner and head of BC Partners Credit, told the Leaders Week London sports business conference that he saw LIV as a great opportunity.

"Every layer of the onion that we peel back on this thing, the more excited we are about the investment," he said.
"The thing that's really fun about this one is in all of our other leagues, the players are on the other side of the table. In this situation, the players are our partners. The players own the teams with us... you're 100 per cent aligned with the talent. That is really rare in sports."
LIV Golf launched in 2022 and lured leading players from the PGA Tour with lucrative contracts. The next phase envisages players becoming equity owners of both the league and its teams.
Several of those stars, including Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson and Cameron Smith, are listed in the Chapter 11 filing as creditors still owed millions in unsecured claims.
"If we can show people that this is a sustainable business and league, those teams have tonnes of value. My guess is, over time, this will begin to look a lot more like Formula One or other leagues that are analogous to what we're trying to do," said Goldthorpe.
LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil likened it to "a rocket ship, waiting to take off", with LIV playing on five continents last year and aiming for five or six next year.
He said relationships with television partners remained strong, with Fox "holding windows for us".  
Goldthorpe said every CEO in the world and major sponsors wanted to be involved with golf, and sounded bullish about the future.
"When we emerge from bankruptcy, you'll be surprised at the calibre and quality of people who invest alongside of us. It's all sports owners, billionaires, people who understand what we're trying to do," he said.
He said BC Partners would "lean on Scott and his team to run the league, and our job is to help with strategy, media and also we have this holding company that we're going to build assets around. So, we can use LIV to help monetise other things... media brands, consumer products.
"There's a lot of cross-selling sponsors. So, really, what I'm going to be focused on is more like the holding company and creating value for our players and ourselves."

items.title: Tin rides the AI investment wave to a new price dimension
items.author: Andy Home
items.creator: Andy Home
items.summary: Tin is the metal that refuses to fall back to earth.
items.body:
Tin is the metal that refuses to fall back to earth.
Tin prices have more than doubled over the last three years, outperforming the rest of the London Metal Exchange pack, even much-hyped copper.
LME three-month tin has been trading above the $50,000-per-metric-ton level since June. Prior to this year the brief all-time high of $51,000 per ton was recorded in March 2022, just after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The new pricing paradigm speaks to the quiet revolution that has unfolded in tin usage over the last few decades.
A metal associated with the humble tin can has woven its way into the fabric of the internet in the form of circuit-board soldering.
Tin-plate packaging now accounts for just around 11% of usage, while solders represent more than half of global demand.
From smart phones to drones, if it's got wiring in, it's also got tin.
And artificial intelligence data centers have a lot of wiring in them.
COMPUTATIONAL POWER The surge of investment into AI infrastructure is [USN:L6N45N0Q6 TEXT:"unprecedented"], eclipsing the railroad boom in the 19th century and the dotcom boom in the 20th century even after adjusting for inflation.
Analysts at research house BMI estimate capital expenditure will reach $785 billion this year.
Cumulative spending globally on data centers alone could top $30 trillion by 2050, according to a projection by PwC.
The competition for ever greater computing power is translating into explosive growth in semiconductor sales.
Global billings have risen for 18 straight months, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association.
Sales in August were $160 billion, up 8% month-on-month and 144% year-on-year. The US is registering the fastest rate of growth, closely followed by China and the rest of Asia.
Wherever all those semiconductors end up, they'll need a tiny drop of tin to glue them to the circuit board.
TIN BRIDGE Every gigawatt of installed AI data center capacity needs around 1,200-1,500 tons of tin, more than three times that used in a traditional data center, according to research from Shanghai Metals Market.
This is a structural change.
Traditional servers consume about 500 kg of tin per unit, while AI servers need up to 4-5 tons of tin.
A 10,000-card AI computing center requires 2.5-3.2 tons of printed circuit board solder alone.
The more complex the data center architecture, the more tin it needs to bind everything together.
Tin is, for now at least, the essential electrical and physical bridge to increased computing power.
The electronics sector has spent years trying to use less tin, leaving little wriggle room for further thrifting.
The only real threat on the horizon is hybrid bonding, but SMM doesn't expect that to make a tangible impact until the next decade.
NEW HEIGHTS While copper bulls wax lyrical about that metal's enhanced demand prospects from the AI boom, tin is already feeling the force.
It's also being helped by [USN:L8N45A111 TEXT:"accelerating sales"] of electric vehicles just about everywhere outside of the US. EVs have a lot more wiring than traditional internal combustion vehicles, which of course means more tin soldering.
These new demand drivers help explain why tin is now trading in what until this year was literally uncharted territory.
The other part of the equation is tin's problematic supply chain, which is heavily concentrated on a limited number of operators, several in higher-risk jurisdictions such as the Democratic Republic of Congo and the autonomous Wa state in Myanmar.
Production has been relatively smooth this year by tin's highly variable standards, but visible inventory has still been quietly sliding away.
Combined stocks registered with the LME, including off-warrant metal, and the Shanghai Futures Exchange have fallen from a February peak of 22,600 tons to 13,100 tons.
LME time-spreads have started to react. Cash tin was trading at a wide discount of more than $400 per ton to three-month metal at times in July. The discount has since contracted to $105 per ton.
As the market tightens, we'll see just how far further into the unknown tin can travel.
(The opinions expressed here are those of Andy Home , a columnist for Reuters.)

items.title: La UE pretende reducir el déficit comercial con China en las negociaciones con Pekín
items.author: Philip Blenkinsop
items.creator: Philip Blenkinsop
items.summary: El comisario europeo de Comercio, Maros Sefcovic, viajará el miércoles a Pekín para mantener conversaciones clave destinadas a reducir el creciente déficit comercial de la Unión Europea con China, que amenaza con destruir la industria de la UE y muchos miles de puestos de trabajo.
items.body:
El comisario europeo de Comercio, Maros Sefcovic, viajará el miércoles a Pekín para mantener conversaciones clave destinadas a reducir el creciente déficit comercial de la Unión Europea con China, que amenaza con destruir la industria de la UE y muchos miles de puestos de trabajo.
Sefcovic se reunirá con el ministro de Comercio chino, Wang Wentao, el jueves y el viernes, tras tres meses de debates sobre el déficit comercial de la UE en el sector de los bienes, que supera los 1.000 millones de euros (1.120 millones de dólares) al día, y sobre las restricciones chinas a las exportaciones de tierras raras y otros minerales críticos.
El responsable de Comercio de la UE ha afirmado que quiere "resultados tangibles" para octubre y algún tipo de compromiso que pueda presentarse a los líderes de la UE reunidos en Bruselas los días 15 y 16 de octubre. La gestión de las relaciones comerciales con China ocupa un lugar prioritario en la agenda de la cumbre.
La presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, dijo ante el Parlamento Europeo el mes pasado que el desequilibrio comercial había alcanzado un punto de inflexión y que Europa utilizaría todas las herramientas a su alcance para reequilibrar la relación.
Los ministros de Economía y Finanzas del G-20, excepto el de China, acordaron en septiembre actuar contra las distorsiones "ajenas al mercado" que agravan los desequilibrios. Pekín sostiene que dar demasiada importancia a cuestiones como los desequilibrios económicos y el exceso de capacidad es una forma de proteccionismo destinada a ejercer presión sobre China y a restringirla.
Los responsables de comercio de la UE quieren que China aplique medidas para abrir más su mercado a las empresas de la UE, pero señalan que esta medida por sí sola no será suficiente. La Comisión está presionando para que China establezca un límite máximo a algunas de sus exportaciones.
El responsable de la aplicación de la normativa comercial de la Comisión dijo la semana pasada que casi una cuarta parte de todas las importaciones estaban aumentando a un ritmo preocupante, con incrementos anómalos en maquinaria, textiles, metales básicos y productos químicos.
No está claro qué importaciones podría aceptar China restringir.
A los responsables de la UE les preocupa especialmente el fuerte aumento de las importaciones de automóviles procedentes de China. Las importaciones de híbridos enchufables a la UE han aumentado un 86% en el año hasta septiembre, con una caída de los precios del 20%, mientras que las importaciones de vehículos eléctricos de batería (BEV) han subido un 40%.
Más de la mitad de todos estos vehículos proceden de China, a pesar de los aranceles de la UE sobre las importaciones de BEV fabricados en ese país.
(1 dólar = 0,8935 euros)

items.title: Postura hawkish do Fed provoca saídas de capital de mercados emergentes em setembro
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Os investidores estrangeiros retiraram US$26,3 bilhões de ações e títulos de mercados emergentes em setembro, a primeira saída mensal desde junho, à medida que a postura hawkish (dura com a inflação) do Federal Reserve impulsionou os rendimentos dos Treasuries e a valorização do dólar, segundo relatório do Instituto de Finanças Internacionais (IIF).
items.body:
Os investidores estrangeiros retiraram US$26,3 bilhões de ações e títulos de mercados emergentes em setembro, a primeira saída mensal desde junho, à medida que a postura hawkish (dura com a inflação) do Federal Reserve impulsionou os rendimentos dos Treasuries e a valorização do dólar, segundo relatório do Instituto de Finanças Internacionais (IIF).
Os investidores não residentes retiraram US$7 bilhões dos ativos de renda fixa dos mercados emergentes no mês passado, a primeira saída líquida desde março, quando a escalada do conflito no Oriente Médio abalou os mercados globais.
Os mercados emergentes ficaram sob pressão em setembro depois que o Fed, sob o comando de Kevin Warsh, elevou as taxas de juros pela primeira vez desde 2023 e sinalizou que a inflação continuava sendo uma preocupação. A medida fez com que os rendimentos dos Treasuries subissem acentuadamente, impulsionou o dólar e levou os investidores a se afastarem de alguns ativos de maior risco.
“A pressão se intensificou na segunda metade do mês, à medida que os fundos de títulos em moeda forte passaram a registrar saídas na semana da decisão do Fomc e os spreads de crédito em dólares dos mercados emergentes se ampliaram”, constatou o relatório.
“Olhando para o futuro, um Fed de Warsh com postura hawkish que projeta novos aumentos, um BoJ (Banco do Japão) com sua taxa básica de juros no maior nível desde 1995 e um aperto monetário generalizado nas economias avançadas aumentam os obstáculos para o carry trade dos mercados emergentes no quarto trimestre”, acrescentou.
Enquanto isso, as fortes vendas estrangeiras de ações sul-coreanas geraram uma saída de US$19,2 bilhões das ações de mercados emergentes em setembro, segundo o IIF.

items.title: NSE cautions investors over pricey overseas ETFs as demand surges
items.author: Jayshree Pyasi
items.creator: Jayshree Pyasi
items.summary: The NSE on Wednesday cautioned investors against rising risks of investing in international exchange traded funds (ETFs).
items.body:
The NSE on Wednesday cautioned investors against rising risks of investing in international exchange traded funds (ETFs).
It said several of these funds were trading at significant premiums to their underlying net asset values (NAVs), implying that investors were essentially buying international ETFs at elevated prices. Here are the key details.
Prices of some ETFs investing in overseas securities have surged even as the NAVs of their underlying overseas holdings have remained broadly stable, NSE said.
Premiums have widened sharply in recent weeks, with some ETFs trading roughly 65%-80% above the value of their underlying holdings at various points in September, according to publicly available market data.
NSE attributed the divergence to supply constraints and regulatory changes. It said that Indian mutual funds have exhausted regulatory overseas investment limits, which has restricted the creation of fresh ETF units.
The regulatory changes, which mandate that ETF price bands be linked to the previous day's NAV from April 1, 2027, could impact how such products trade relative to their underlying assets.
Investors purchasing such units at steep premiums may be exposed to the risk of an abrupt fall in prices, unrelated to movements in the underlying securities, NSE said, urging investors to exercise caution.
Assets in mutual fund schemes investing abroad rose nearly 55% year-on-year to about 485 billion rupees in August 2026, while investor folios increased more than 40%, according to AMFI data.
The demand has been buoyed by the performance gap between Indian and overseas markets. Over the past year, the Nifty 50 has fallen about 8% and the Sensex about 9%, while the Nasdaq-100 has gained roughly 24%.

items.title: Clip generado con IA se comparte falsamente como registro del huracán Polo
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Un clip que muestra un huracán visto desde la ventana de un avión fue generado con inteligencia artificial, pero se comparte erróneamente en redes sociales como un video auténtico del huracán Polo, que golpeó los estados mexicanos de Sonora y Baja California Sur en septiembre de 2026.
items.body:
Un clip que muestra un huracán visto desde la ventana de un avión fue generado con inteligencia artificial, pero se comparte erróneamente en redes sociales como un video auténtico del huracán Polo, que golpeó los estados mexicanos de Sonora y Baja California Sur en septiembre de 2026.
Estos son los detalles clave:
Algunos ejemplos dicen que el clip muestra el ojo del huracán Polo a 33,000 pies (10,058 metros) y lo atribuyen a la Administración Nacional Oceánica y Atmosférica de Estados Unidos (NOAA).
El video no figura entre las imágenes del huracán que difundió la agencia.
El usuario de Instagram @earthimpacts25, quien no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios, lo publicó en octubre de 2025 con una descripción y una etiqueta que indican que fue generado con IA.
La cuenta y su imagen de perfil dicen que el contenido que comparte es creado con IA.
La herramienta de detección de IA de Google, SynthID, concluyó que el clip fue creado utilizando uno de los modelos generativos de IA de la compañía tecnológica.
SynthID detecta todas o partes de marcas de agua imperceptibles que se encuentran presentes en los contenidos generados por los modelos de IA de Google.
En respuesta a un correo de Reuters, NOAA no comentó sobre el video, pero remitió a imágenes del huracán de la agencia.
Polo, que permaneció varios [USN:L8N45L0P6 TEXT:"días"] frente a la costa del Pacífico mexicano, se disipó el 29 de septiembre.
Veredicto: Contenido artificial. El clip fue publicado en 2025 por una cuenta que comparte contenido generado con IA, y SynthID determinó que fue creado con uno de los modelos generativos de Google.
Reuters Fact Check ofrece información confiable mediante su canal de WhatsApp para México . Envíenos un mensaje con el contenido en español que desea que verifiquemos.
Este artículo fue realizado por el equipo de Reuters Fact Check. Lea más sobre nuestro trabajo de verificación de afirmaciones en las redes sociales.

items.title: Farage's Reform UK admits failings over donations but denies breaking law
items.author: William James
items.creator: William James
items.summary: Nigel Farage's Reform UK on Wednesday acknowledged failings in the way the party had handled prospective donations and pledged to tighten its rules on dealing with donors, but it said allegations it had broken electoral law were unfounded.
items.body:
Nigel Farage's Reform UK on Wednesday acknowledged failings in the way the party had handled prospective donations and pledged to tighten its rules on dealing with donors, but it said allegations it had broken electoral law were unfounded.
Reform UK published the results of an internal investigation into allegations, [USN:L1N44W097 TEXT:"aired in an undercover documentary"], that officials had arranged for a foreign donor to pay for political polling and also discussed arranging a large donation with a man they believed to be a foreign national.
[USN:L8N4511I5 TEXT:"Police are still investigating"] those allegations, including whether Reform breached laws which ban accepting money from foreign sources. Police are also looking at [USN:L8N4511I5 TEXT:"other accusations"] about the party's finances, all of which Reform denies.
Reform's investigation concluded that no laws were broken in relation to the footage — consistent with the party's original response to the documentary, which was aired on the eve of its annual conference in September.
But the report said it had "found conduct which deserves criticism", referring to the way potential donations had been described, whether those soliciting them had been truthful, and the failure to provide full information to party officials.
The investigation also said it had "found weaknesses in the party’s arrangements which allowed a sustained deception to reach the top of the party without anyone asking the questions that would have exposed it, and it has set out how those weaknesses are to be closed."
TIGHTER PARTY RULES NEEDED, REFORM SAYS Reform has fallen behind the governing Labour Party in recent opinion polls. The country's next election is due in 2029.
But with Labour struggling to improve living standards and stop illegal migration, Reform's leader Farage is still seen as a possible future prime minister promising anti-immigration policies and sweeping economic change.
Shortly after the original allegations, which were broadcast by Channel 4 and compiled by investigative group Verbatim, head of policy James Orr and Farage's right-hand man Dan Jukes stood down pending the results of the investigation.
Wednesday's report said Jukes had been acting independently in his capacity as a contractor with several other clients when he commissioned the polling.
It also said the separate larger donation had not happened and no arrangement was made with the man, who was an actor posing as a wealthy US donor.
Nevertheless, on the commissioning of polls it recommended contractors should adhere to formal transparency requirements and tighter record-keeping requirements in order to separate their party work from other work.
On the broader donation process, it promised to impose stricter rules on disclosing potential donations to the party treasurer and on the distribution of written guidance on how to properly court donors.
The report said that guidance should include: "That no arrangement is to be described as discreet, off the record, or outside public view; that the regulator is not to be disparaged; that the party’s procedures for checking donors are to be described to every prospective donor at the outset."

items.title: Halozyme wins court order to block Merck's injected Keytruda in select European markets
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Biopharma company Halozyme said on Wednesday that a Dutch patent court ruled in its favor against Merck , ordering the drugmaker to halt the manufacture and sale of injectable Keytruda in eight European markets.
items.body:
Biopharma company Halozyme (HALO.O) said on Wednesday that a Dutch patent court ruled in its favor against Merck (MRK.N) , ordering the drugmaker to halt the manufacture and sale of injectable Keytruda in eight European markets.
Here are some details:
Halozyme said a specialized Dutch patent court in The Hague found that Merck had infringed one of its patents covering MDASE, Halozyme's technology for rapid, high-volume under-the-skin drug delivery.
The court ordered Merck to stop the production and sale of injectable Keytruda in Belgium, Denmark, France, Ireland, Italy, Sweden, Switzerland and the Netherlands.
The drugmaker has been counting on the simpler-to-use subcutaneous version of the drug, known as Keytruda SC, to help drive growth as key patents on its original intravenous version expire later in the decade.
Merck did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.
"We're very pleased the Dutch court recognized the validity and infringement of Halozyme's MDASE patent," said Mark Snyder, the company's chief legal officer.
Halozyme has also sued Merck for patent infringement in the US, alleging the under-the-skin formulation of Keytruda infringes 15 patents that Halozyme has filed since 2011.
The company sued Merck in Germany and was granted a preliminary injunction last year, stopping Merck's launch of Keytruda SC in Germany.

items.title: Canada's Weston family buys UK pharmacy chain Boots for $8.9 billion
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The holding company of Canada's Weston family has agreed to buy British health and beauty retailer Boots from private equity firm Sycamore Partners and the Pessina family for $8.9 billion, including debt, it said on Wednesday.
items.body:
The holding company of Canada's Weston family has agreed to buy British health and beauty retailer Boots from private equity firm Sycamore Partners and the Pessina family for $8.9 billion, including debt, it said on Wednesday.
Wittington Investments, Limited will acquire Boots' retail operations in the UK and Ireland, Boots Opticians, No7 Beauty Company and its Thailand and franchised businesses.
The Weston group owns Canadian grocer Loblaw and Shoppers Drug Mart, Canada's largest pharmacy, health and beauty business and previously owned London department store Selfridges from 2003 to 2021.
Wittington is partnering with Fairfax Financial Holdings, a Toronto-based holding company, on the deal, with Wittington having operational control.
It said its plans for Boots include investing in stores and online and expanding healthcare services.
Galen Weston, Wittington's chair, will become Boots' chair.
"Boots is one of Britain's most enduring businesses, with a rich heritage, a trusted name and a vital role in everyday life across the UK and Ireland," he said.
"We see a meaningful opportunity to make a great business even better."
Sycamore, in partnership with Stefano Pessina and his family, will retain ownership of The Boots Group's other interests in Farmacias Benavides and Alliance Healthcare Deutschland.
Sycamore took Boots' then parent Walgreens Boots Alliance for $10 billion last year.

items.title: Russian supermarket staff applaud Germany's Schroeder in new board role
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder, who recently joined the supervisory board of Russian supermarket chain Hyperglobus, visited one of its Moscow stores on Wednesday and was greeted with applause from employees, Russian TV footage showed.
items.body:
Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder, who [USN:L1N45O0BK TEXT:"recently joined"] the supervisory board of Russian supermarket chain Hyperglobus, visited one of its Moscow stores on Wednesday and was greeted with applause from employees, Russian TV footage showed.
Schroeder has faced criticism, notably in Germany, over his links to Russian business and President Vladimir Putin , ties that have persisted despite Moscow's 2022 invasion of Ukraine and subsequent waves of Western sanctions.
Hyperglobus was spun off Germany's Globus Holding last year. It announced Schroeder's board appointment last week.
The former chancellor smiled broadly as staff broke into sustained applause after he entered the store, the footage from Russian TV channel RBC showed.
"I’m very pleased to be here, to see this wonderful hypermarket, to see the results of your work and to meet you, my wonderful colleagues," RBC quoted him as saying.
The Russian retailer confirmed Schroeder visited a supermarket on the western outskirts of Moscow.
Schroeder formed a close relationship with Putin while serving as German chancellor from 1998 to 2005, and he later worked for Russian state companies.
His appointment to the Hyperglobus board comes as Russia singles out European firms in a [USN:L1N45L0FF TEXT:"fresh drive"] to strip foreign owners of the right to manage their Russian assets.

items.title: Bezos quip, Ive design shaped Ferrari's Luce EV, Elkann says
items.author: Giulio Piovaccari
items.creator: Giulio Piovaccari
items.summary: When John Elkann first started thinking seriously about an electric Ferrari a decade ago, the prompt came from an unlikely source: a walk with Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, the Ferrari chairman said on Wednesday.
items.body:
When John Elkann first started thinking seriously about an electric Ferrari a decade ago, the prompt came from an unlikely source: a walk with Amazon (AMZN.O) founder Jeff Bezos, the Ferrari (RACE.MI) chairman said on Wednesday.
That conversation eventually led to the Ferrari Luce, the luxury carmaker's first fully electric model, [USN:L8N41M044 TEXT:"unveiled in May"] and created in partnership with former Apple (AAPL.O) design chief Jony Ive and his LoveFrom team.
But the result was also a car that sparked fierce debate, prompting [USN:L1N4230MY TEXT:"social media mockery and criticism"] for its unconventional styling, while some investors questioned Ferrari's gamble on electrification.
"This is something that we believe is important for the future of Ferrari ... not to just recycle history, but to create the future," Ive said of the project as he joined Elkann at a panel discussion at the Wave technology conference in Turin.
Ive described a project that began not with sketches but with understanding Ferrari itself.
"We spent really the best part of a year researching and trying to learn," he said, explaining that LoveFrom immersed itself in Ferrari's history and culture before starting work on the vehicle. Teams in California and at Ferrari's Maranello headquarters in northern Italy then spent five years developing the project together.
With Luce, Ive, who helped create some of Apple's most iconic products, sought to reject some industry trends, including the predominance of touchscreens and digital controls.
"Touch, as the primary interface, shouldn't be in a car," he said. "There's a price you pay ... you're disconnected as a physical being from the object."
The Luce relies heavily on physical controls and tactile feedback designed to create a more direct relationship between driver and machine.
SEEING IS BELIEVING "We weren't in any way intending to do a controversial Ferrari," Elkann said at the conference, organised by Vento, the venture capital arm of Agnelli family holding group Exor (EXOR.AS) , which controls Ferrari.
"What is important is how much that touches your conviction. What it did is that it made our conviction very strong."
But both Ive and Elkann, who is also Exor CEO, said seeing the Luce in person often changed perceptions compared with the initial response to images.
"I've never known such a massive change that seems to occur when you see it," Ive said.
With a Luce on display at Wednesday's event, drawing long queues of visitors eager to judge Ferrari's most debated new model for themselves, Elkann recalled that a July 2016 conversation with Bezos helped convince him Ferrari needed to think seriously about electric vehicles.
Bezos told him: "I don't know anything about cars, but I really know a lot about innovation. And I think that you need to really think hard about building an electric vehicle," Elkann said.
items.raw_description: When John Elkann first started thinking seriously about an electric Ferrari a decade ago, the prompt came from an unlikely source: a walk with Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, the Ferrari chairman said on Wednesday.

items.title: Países do Pacífico insistem que mundo precisa intensificar esforços para cumprir limite do aquecimento global
items.author: Peter Hobson
items.creator: Peter Hobson
items.summary: Os governos de todo o mundo precisam intensificar os esforços para reduzir as emissões, pois o planeta está “ultrapassando rapidamente” uma meta crítica de temperatura que conteria a elevação do nível do mar e os fenômenos climáticos extremos, afirmaram na quarta-feira delegados de uma importante conferência climática em Fiji.
items.body:
Os governos de todo o mundo precisam intensificar os esforços para reduzir as emissões, pois o planeta está “ultrapassando rapidamente” uma meta crítica de temperatura que conteria a elevação do nível do mar e os fenômenos climáticos extremos, afirmaram na quarta-feira delegados de uma importante conferência climática em Fiji.
Os países do Pacífico, que estão entre os mais vulneráveis às mudanças climáticas no mundo, estão tentando garantir que suas prioridades sejam incluídas nas negociações globais sobre o clima na reunião ministerial em Fiji, um evento preparatório para o fórum COP31, que ocorrerá na Turquia em novembro.
Entre essas prioridades estão garantir melhor acesso ao financiamento climático, proteger os oceanos e assegurar que a meta de limitar o aquecimento a 1,5 grau Celsius acima dos níveis pré-industriais seja cumprida, apesar das projeções da ONU de que ela será ultrapassada em breve.
“Estamos ultrapassando rapidamente o limite de temperatura de 1,5 grau”, disse a ministra do Clima de Fiji, Lynda Tabuya, a representantes de mais de 50 países no início das negociações ministeriais pré-COP.
Os dados simplesmente confirmam o que as nações do Pacífico podem ver, disse ela: “A maré que chega às nossas casas, o recife desbotado que nossas avós já não reconhecem, as vilas que já tivemos que realojar.”
“Ultrapassar (a meta) não é um veredicto que aceitamos passivamente... manter a meta de 1,5 vivo é a principal obrigação legal e o dever que viemos aqui defender.”
Representantes de cerca de 30 nações se reuniram na terça-feira em Fiji após uma visita à vulnerável nação atol de Tuvalu e adotaram uma declaração exigindo “reduções profundas, rápidas e sustentadas das emissões”.
A delegação, que inclui líderes das ilhas do Pacífico e representantes de países como França, Índia e Emirados Árabes Unidos, viu máquinas pesadas escavando areia e criando novos terrenos capazes de resistir à elevação do nível do mar.
“Cada fração de grau de aquecimento acelera os impactos das mudanças climáticas e aumenta o risco de perdas e danos irreversíveis”, afirma a declaração, cujo título, Taku Pakasoa, é o conceito tuvaluano da força encontrada na união e na ação coletiva.
A Turquia sedia a COP31 na cidade litorânea de Antália, e a Austrália está liderando as negociações.
Os eventos pré-COP em Fiji e Tuvalu nesta semana definirão o que será possível na COP31, afirmou o ministro australiano do Clima, Chris Bowen.
“Esta região abriga algumas das vozes mais influentes do mundo em questões climáticas”, disse ele, acrescentando que a defesa da causa pelo Pacífico foi vital para a adoção da meta de 1,5 grau na COP21, em Paris, em 2015. “Ela também está sofrendo os impactos mais diretos.”
O ministro do Meio Ambiente da Turquia, Murat Kurum, que é presidente da COP31, disse que limitar o desvio em relação à meta é o objetivo comum claro da cúpula. “Acredito nisso de todo o coração”, declarou ele.

items.body:
Mais de 200 mil pessoas foram deslocadas de suas casas desde o início dos combates no Iêmen nas últimas semanas, de acordo com dados divulgados nesta quarta-feira pela Organização Internacional para as Migrações (OIM) das Nações Unidas.
A OIM descreveu como alarmante a crise provocada pela retomada dos combates entre o grupo houthi, apoiado pelo Irã, e as forças governamentais apoiadas pela Arábia Saudita no Iêmen, com os números de deslocados subindo de 76 mil em meados de setembro para mais de 200 mil até esta quarta-feira — quase todos os quais fugiram desde o início dos combates, no início de setembro.
(Reportagem de Olivia Le Poidevin)

items.title: Pfizer conferma 330 esuberi e chiusura reparto penicilline a Catania - sindacati
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: La multinazionale farmaceutica Pfizer ha confermato la chiusura definitiva del reparto penicilline e l'avvio dei licenziamenti collettivi per circa 330 lavoratori su un organico di 550 dipendenti nello stabilimento di Catania.
items.body:
La multinazionale farmaceutica Pfizer (PFE.N) ha confermato la chiusura definitiva del reparto penicilline e l'avvio dei licenziamenti collettivi per circa 330 lavoratori su un organico di 550 dipendenti nello stabilimento di Catania.
E' quanto rendono noto i sindacati Filctem Cgil, Femca Cisl e Uiltec in una nota dopo che ieri l'incontro presso il ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy "si è concluso con un esito negativo", sottolineano.
L'azienda ha inoltre escluso nuovi investimenti di sviluppo per riassorbire il personale, limitando gli interventi alla sola manutenzione e digitalizzazione della linea sterile, aggiungono i sindacati.
In una nota il Mimit conferma "l’annuncio da parte della multinazionale della farmaceutica della dismissione definitiva di due linee di produzione del sito, con conseguenti effetti sul piano occupazionale".
Il ministero aggiunge, tuttavia, che "nel corso dell’incontro, l’azienda ha comunicato che sta proseguendo la ricerca di una soluzione industriale e occupazionale. Pfizer ha inoltre ribadito di considerare strategico lo stabilimento etneo, confermando l’intenzione di proseguire gli investimenti sul sito".
"Abbiamo apprezzato la contrarietà del Mimit che ha rifiutato la gestione passiva degli esuberi e ha chiesto di estendere la procedura a 12 mesi per cercare soluzioni industriali alternative, mettendo a disposizione gli strumenti di sostegno statale e pretendendo massima trasparenza sulle trattative di vendita e sull'Advisor incaricato", sottolineano Filctem Cgil, Femca Cisl e Uiltec Uil.
Il 23 ottobre a Catania è prevista la visita del ministro Adolfo Urso allo stabilimento del gruppo e l’incontro con i vertici della società biofarmaceutica.

items.title: Former German top spy placed under formal arrest
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A judge of Germany's Federal Court of Justice issued a formal arrest warrant against a former spy chief accused of buying secret documents and using them in an analysis for a foreign intelligence service, the Office of the Federal Prosecutor said on Wednesday.
items.body:
A judge of Germany's Federal Court of Justice issued a formal arrest warrant against a former spy chief accused of buying secret documents and using them in an analysis for a foreign intelligence service, the Office of the Federal Prosecutor said on Wednesday.
The case of 80-year-old August Hanning, [USN:L8N45S0GQ TEXT:"detained on Tuesday"] over suspected espionage and attempted treason, has shocked the German intelligence community and lawmakers, and could emerge as one of the biggest leaks of classified documents in Germany since the end of the Cold War.
It has also raised concerns that foreign intelligence agencies could cut Germany off from important information.
Federal prosecutors have not identified the foreign intelligence service, and it is unclear whether Hanning's alleged analysis reached its intended recipient.
Der Spiegel news magazine reported late on Tuesday that investigators were pursuing a possible connection to Azerbaijan. It reported Hanning had been in contact with an agent from the country. Azerbaijan on Wednesday denied any connection.
Hanning on Tuesday did not respond to a request for comment.
"While it is true that he was in possession of confidential documents, the allegation that he passed on information contained therein to the detriment of Germany, let alone for payment, is incorrect," his lawyer told German newspaper Die Welt on Wednesday.
A judge at the Federal Court of Justice in the southwestern city of Karlsruhe issued the arrest warrant, federal prosecutors said.
The official warrant allows authorities to keep Hanning in custody.
Azerbaijan's Media and Broadcasting Council issued a statement saying the allegations were groundless disinformation.
"The malicious intent of the forces behind this disinformation operation is to damage Azerbaijan-Germany relations," the council said.
A senior Azerbaijani government official told Reuters that Baku had contacted German intelligence services through official channels and had been told that the case had no connection to Azerbaijani intelligence.
CHIEF OF STAFF IN CUSTODY Hanning was head of the BND, Germany's foreign intelligence service, from 1998 to 2005.
Prosecutors allege that in 2010 Hanning agreed to pay for confidential information from an official identified as Manfred D, who served as chief of staff to successive BND heads prior to his retirement in March this year.
His position potentially gave him access to some of Germany's most current intelligence at the time that prosecutors say documents were being siphoned from the service.
Manfred D. was detained on Tuesday and also placed under formal arrest on Wednesday.
Prosecutors on Tuesday said that the investigation centered on suspicion that Hanning received approximately 2,000 documents from D. through June 2022. "Some of these documents were classified," a spokesperson for the prosecution service said.
It is still unclear what level of secrecy the potentially leaked documents had.
Marc Henrichmann, head of the parliamentary committee that oversees the intelligence services, said he was "pretty stunned" by the case.
But he downplayed comparisons to the 1970s case of East German spy Guenther Guillaume, secretary of Chancellor Willy Brandt, who eventually stepped down over the affair.
"I find (that comparison) a bit of a stretch at the moment, because we don't even know exactly what happened there yet," Henrichmann told public broadcaster Deutschlandfunk.

items.title: Thailand at 'last paragraph' of US trade agreement, PM says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Thailand is at "the last paragraph" of a trade agreement with the United States, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Wednesday.
items.body:
Thailand is at "the last paragraph" of a trade agreement with the United States, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Wednesday.
Speaking at a forum in Singapore, Anutin said he expected to sign the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade during President Donald Trump's next visit to Asia, likely in November in Manila or Shenzhen when Trump attends ASEAN meetings.
Anutin said that he received a letter from Trump last week confirming the deal is at its final stage. "He told me that I was to make sure that my people and the United States Trade Representative would write up the final clause."
In July, the US imposed a tariff of 12.5% on imports from Thailand.
The United States is Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24% of the southeast Asian country's total exports so far this year.

items.title: Lineker laments Ronaldo's career finale compared to Messi's
items.author: Christian Radnedge
items.creator: Christian Radnedge
items.summary: It is sad that Cristiano Ronaldo's international career looks to have ended in acrimony, former England striker Gary Lineker said on Wednesday, adding that the Portuguese great should have enjoyed similar scenes to Lionel Messi's uplifting Argentina finale.
items.body:
It is sad that Cristiano Ronaldo's international career looks to have ended in acrimony, former England striker Gary Lineker said on Wednesday, adding that the Portuguese great should have enjoyed similar scenes to Lionel Messi's uplifting Argentina finale.
Ronaldo, 41, released a [USN:L6N45S178 TEXT:"lengthy statement on Tuesday"] to explain his sudden departure from the Portugal camp last week, accusing coach Jorge Jesus of breaking promises, while Messi scored one goal and set up two in a 3-0 friendly win over Benin.
It was the 39-year-old's final match in the famous blue and white and he was given an [USN:L1N45T01C TEXT:"emotional ovation in Buenos Aires"] - scenes that Lineker said would have been fitting for Portugal's all-time leading goalscorer (146) Ronaldo too.
"I think it's a bit sad because he's been so great. And ultimately in five years, 10 years' time, no one will remember this. We'll just remember how great he was," Lineker told reporters at the Leaders Week sports industry conference at Stamford Bridge.
"But I think if you look at Messi's farewell, it was so beautiful. And I think Cristiano deserves the same."
Ronaldo and Messi have battled for the title of greatest living player for much of their illustrious careers. Messi has won the Ballon d'Or eight times to Ronaldo's five, but neither are among the favourites for this year's award.
One player who is, however, is Lineker's compatriot Harry Kane. The England captain equalled his country's international appearance record of 125 on Tuesday against the Czech Republic, level with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, and extended his leading scoring tally to 91 goals in the 3-0 win.
Lineker, who scored 48 goals for England, hailed Kane as one of the greatest players in the country's history, echoing [USN:L8N45S1RB TEXT:"comments from midfielder Jude Bellingham"].
"I think he'd have to be in that conversation. Probably along with Bobby Charlton and maybe even Bobby Moore. I mean, look at his record, he's incredible," Lineker said.
"He's not just a goalscorer either, he's not just a box player like I was. He's way more than that. He can drop deep, he sprays passes everywhere, he scores all sorts of goals, both feet, head, he's got everything," he added.

LONDON, Oct 7 : It is sad that Cristiano Ronaldo's international career looks to have ended in acrimony, former England striker Gary Lineker said on Wednesday, adding that the Portuguese great should have enjoyed similar scenes to Lionel Messi's uplifting Argentina finale.
Ronaldo, 41, released a lengthy statement on Tuesday to explain his sudden departure from the Portugal camp last week, accusing coach Jorge Jesus of breaking promises, while Messi scored one goal and set up two in a 3-0 friendly win over Benin.
It was the 39-year-old's final match in the famous blue and white and he was given an emotional ovation in Buenos Aires - cenes that Lineker said would have been fitting for Portugal's all-time leading goalscorer (146) Ronaldo too.
"I think it's a bit sad because he's been so great. And ultimately in five years, 10 years' time, no one will remember this. We'll just remember how great he was," Lineker told reporters at the Leaders Week sports industry conference at Stamford Bridge.

items.title: Palestinian killed in Israeli settler attack during olive harvest, officials say
items.author: Mohammed Torokman
items.creator: Mohammed Torokman
items.summary: A Palestinian was killed on Wednesday during an Israeli settler attack while Palestinians were harvesting olives near the village of Burqa in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, the Palestinian health ministry said.
items.body:
A Palestinian was killed on Wednesday during an Israeli settler attack while Palestinians were harvesting olives near the village of Burqa in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, the Palestinian health ministry said.
The attack came amid mounting violence from militant Israeli settlers during the Palestinian olive harvest, which has seen settlers fire live ammunition at farmers, attack journalists, and damage the trees.
The Israeli military said both soldiers and settlers had opened fire in Wednesday's incident. It said soldiers were responding to a report of a Palestinian throwing a rock at a settler but did not say why the settlers were in the area.
Reuters journalists have witnessed several incidents in the past two weeks in which the Israeli military and settlers have prevented Palestinians from accessing their olive groves.
The Palestinian health ministry identified the dead man as 44-year-old Ali Hassan Yusor al-Bazzari. It was not immediately clear whether the Israeli military or settlers had killed him.
At the funeral following the attack, al-Bazzari's son Danial, 12, wept over his father's body, which was later draped in a Palestinian flag.
'FOR US, THE OLIVE TREE IS LIFE' The olive harvest, which runs from October to November, has come amid a surge of violence in the West Bank, where Israeli settlers have killed at least 30 Palestinians this year, according to the Palestinian Authority.
It has also reported that more than 45,000 trees, including more than 26,000 olive trees, were cut down or damaged across the West Bank during the first half of 2026.
The olive trees bear great significance for Palestinians, representing their connection to the land as well as providing a vital source of income, amid mounting economic pressures.
"For us, the olive tree is life," said Tayseer Al-Sheikh, a 64-year-old Palestinian farmer, from the outskirts of Rantis village, northwest of Ramallah.
Fear of settler violence prevented him from accessing and tending to his olives for a year. He was only able to access them this harvest while accompanied by activists providing a protective presence.
For Al-Sheikh, the loss is not measured merely by the number of trees or the quantity of oil produced, but also by the changing relationship of people to their land.
"In the past, everyone used to come to the olives, young and old. Today, many people are afraid to reach their lands," he told Reuters.

items.title: French lawmakers spare pensioners from cuts as budget review begins
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The rejection of the measure straight out of the blocks sets the stage for a rocky ride in parliament for the minority government trying to push through its €43 billion savings package.
items.body:
French lawmakers began their review of the government's 2027 budget on Wednesday, scrapping in one of their first moves a planned reduction in a tax break benefiting pensioners.
The rejection of the measure straight out of the blocks sets the stage for a rocky ride in parliament for the minority government trying to push through its €43 billion ($48 billion) [USN:L1N45N0A3 TEXT:"savings package"].
With France [USN:L8N45S1P0 TEXT:"at the centre"] of a global bond market selloff over its weak public finances, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is seeking to cut the budget deficit from 5.4% of economic output this year to 5% next year.
Lawmakers have been hardening their positions as parties try to build political momentum ahead of next year's presidential election, which polls suggest far-right leader [USN:L1N45S0C4 TEXT:"Marine Le Pen"] could win.
The finance committee in the lower house rejected a government proposal to lower the effective ceiling on the 10% pension allowance, from €4,439 to €3,000 for retirement pensions. The measure is ostensibly to cover "professional expenses" even though most retirees do not have any.
The proposal could be revived in a later stage of the legislative process, though it could be shot down again given the broad rejection among parties in the finance committee.
"We oppose that the consolidation of the public accounts is done on the backs of retirees," said lawmaker Claire Marais-Beuil with the far-right National Rally (RN) during the debate.
Many politicians have long been reluctant to pass any measures that would hurt pensioners' purchasing power since older voters turn out in higher numbers than other age groups.
Pensions are by far France's single biggest public expense, reaching €436 billion next year, or 14% of economic output.
As part of its savings measures, the government also wants to raise pensions less than the rate of inflation for all but those on the lowest incomes, which it expects would save €4.1 billion.
($1 = 0.8941 euros)

items.title: Moody's turns positive on sub-Saharan African countries
items.author: Colleen Goko
items.creator: Colleen Goko
items.summary: Moody's raised its outlook for sub-Saharan African countries to positive on Wednesday, saying reforms had helped them weather inflationary pressures, while strong commodity prices and easier access to financing had improved their fiscal positions.
items.body:
Moody's raised its outlook for sub-Saharan African countries to positive on Wednesday, saying reforms had helped them weather inflationary pressures, while strong commodity prices and easier access to financing had improved their fiscal positions.
Moody's made the following observations:
Cautions that heavy debt repayment burdens, limited government income and risks from climate change and regional security threats remain major weak spots
Expects the region's economies to grow 4.3% in both 2026 and 2027, measured as a weighted average across countries.
Forecasts the amount governments need to borrow each year, to cover deficits and repay maturing debt, will decline to 11.2% of GDP in 2027 from a peak of 12.3% in 2025
Predicts total government debt will level off at 56.6% of GDP in 2027, down from 62.4% in 2025.
Expects Zambia and Ethiopia to see the biggest drops in debt. Botswana, hit by weak diamond demand, and Gabon, which is struggling to rein in spending, will see the sharpest rises
Kenya and Zambia will each spend about 35% of their government revenue just on interest payments in 2027, more than any other country in the region.
Warns a prolonged surge in inflation, severe weather events or a sudden investor pullback from the region's bond markets could darken the picture
Only two of the 25 countries it rates in the region, Botswana and Mauritius, are investment grade, meaning it considers them relatively low-risk borrowers
Of the 25, eight have positive outlooks — South Africa, Namibia, Angola, Nigeria, Togo, Ghana, Republic of Congo and Zambia — 13 are stable and four are negative: Mauritius, Gabon, Mali and Senegal

items.title: Maioria dos eleitores nos EUA diz que Trump e Congresso não levam a sério riscos da IA, aponta Reuters/Ipsos
items.author: Courtney Rozen, Jason Lange
items.creator: Courtney Rozen, Jason Lange
items.summary: A maioria dos eleitores norte-americanos acredita que o governo do presidente Donald Trump e o Congresso não estão levando os riscos da IA a sério o suficiente e quer que o governo elabore novas regulamentações para a tecnologia, de acordo com uma nova pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos.
items.body:
A maioria dos eleitores norte-americanos acredita que o governo do presidente Donald Trump e o Congresso não estão levando os riscos da IA a sério o suficiente e quer que o governo elabore novas regulamentações para a tecnologia, de acordo com uma nova pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos.
A pesquisa, realizada durante seis dias e encerrada na segunda-feira, mostrou que grande parte do eleitorado vê a IA como uma grande ameaça aos empregos nos Estados Unidos, ressaltando o ceticismo crescente em relação à tecnologia por parte de eleitores de todo o espectro político.
A tecnologia, que avança rapidamente, tornou-se um assunto de grande interesse nacional em meio a relatos de agentes de IA agindo descontroladamente e invadindo redes de computadores corporativas, além de alertas de pesquisadores renomados de que ela poderia, um dia, representar uma ameaça existencial à humanidade. Centros de dados barulhentos e que consomem muita energia — responsáveis por alimentar a IA — também representam um incômodo cada vez maior quando surgem próximos a bairros, ao mesmo tempo em que elevam as contas de serviços públicos.
Cerca de 57% dos eleitores registrados na pesquisa — incluindo um terço dos que se identificam como republicanos — afirmaram que o governo Trump não leva os riscos da IA a sério o suficiente, ou nem mesmo os leva em conta. Cerca de 54% disseram o mesmo sobre o Congresso.
A inteligência artificial tornou-se um tema de campanha significativo às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato em 3 de novembro, quando o controle do Congresso estará em jogo. Cerca de 62% dos eleitores na pesquisa afirmaram que a tecnologia pode sair do controle e colocar em risco o futuro da humanidade — aproximadamente a mesma porcentagem de eleitores com essa opinião em uma pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos realizada em agosto do ano passado.
Trump tem manifestado repetidamente apoio incondicional à IA e à construção de centros de dados, argumentando que eles são vitais para a competitividade dos EUA, mesmo com o aumento das críticas bipartidárias à tecnologia. Ele costuma dizer que o setor de tecnologia dos EUA ficará para trás em relação aos seus equivalentes chineses quando questionado sobre por que seu governo não estabeleceu limites para o uso e o desenvolvimento da tecnologia — um argumento que, segundo defensores da segurança da IA, é equivocado.
“Essa é uma preocupação importante, mas não é a principal preocupação da maioria dos norte-americanos, nem deveria ser”, disse Daniel Kokotajlo, ex-funcionário da OpenAI que se demitiu em 2024 por acreditar que a empresa não estava agindo de forma responsável.
A preocupação mais urgente é que a IA possa custar empregos às pessoas ou ameaçar a saúde e a segurança humana, afirmou ele.
Em uma declaração à Reuters sobre a forma como o presidente lida com a IA, um funcionário da Casa Branca destacou a nova força-tarefa de Trump, que, segundo ele, é responsável por garantir que “os Estados Unidos continuem liderando o mundo” nessa tecnologia.
“A prioridade do governo Trump é garantir que haja uma economia em expansão, para que os trabalhadores tenham muitas oportunidades e sofram pouca instabilidade decorrente de quaisquer perturbações de curto prazo”, disse o funcionário quando questionado sobre os temores dos eleitores em relação ao emprego no contexto da IA.
A nova pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos revelou que 84% dos eleitores veem a IA como uma ameaça aos trabalhadores norte-americanos. Em comparação, 60% veem a imigração ilegal como uma ameaça aos trabalhadores norte-americanos, enquanto 74% consideram a concorrência de trabalhadores estrangeiros dessa forma e 73% dizem o mesmo sobre as grandes corporações.
Uma maioria bipartidária de eleitores — incluindo 80% dos democratas e 61% dos republicanos — afirmou apoiar uma regulamentação governamental mais rigorosa sobre a IA.
A pesquisa da Reuters/Ipsos, realizada online e em todo o país, reuniu respostas de 4.506 adultos norte-americanos, incluindo 3.526 eleitores registrados. A pesquisa tem uma margem de erro de 2 pontos percentuais.

items.title: Hawkish Fed triggers emerging market outflows in September
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Foreign investors pulled $26.3 billion out of emerging market stocks and bonds in September, the first monthly outflow since June, as a hawkish US Federal Reserve drove up yields and the dollar, a report by the Institute of International Finance showed.
items.body:
Foreign investors pulled $26.3 billion out of emerging market stocks and bonds in September, the first monthly outflow since June, as a hawkish US Federal Reserve drove up yields and the dollar, a report by the Institute of International Finance showed.
Non-resident investors pulled $7 billion from emerging market fixed income last month, the first net outflows since March when the escalating Middle East conflict roiled global markets.
Emerging markets came under pressure in September after the Fed under President Kevin Warsh raised rates for the first time since 2023 and signalled inflation remained a concern. The move sent US Treasury yields sharply higher, lifted the dollar and saw investors pull back from some riskier assets.
"The pressure built in the second half of the month, as hard currency bond funds turned to outflows in the week of the FOMC decision and EM dollar credit spreads widened," the report found.
"Looking ahead, a hawkish Warsh Fed that projects further hikes, a BoJ (Bank of Japan) at its highest policy rate since 1995 and broad tightening across advanced economies all raise the hurdle for EM carry into the fourth quarter," it added.
Meanwhile heavy foreign selling of South Korean stocks drove a $19.2 billion outflow from emerging market equities in September, the IIF found.

Oct 7 : The US government and tech heavyweights Meta Platforms and Google parent Alphabet are joining nonprofit Biohub to build open datasets to train AI models for biological reasearch, bringing total investment in the effort to $1.8 billion, Biohub said on Wednesday.
Meta, Google DeepMind and drug discovery startup Isomorphic Labs are jointly investing $300 million. The Department of Energy will invest more than $500 million over five years in laboratory measurement, modeling and computation. The National Institutes of Health will coordinate datasets and repositories built with more than $500 million in earlier federal funding, which Biohub will standardize for AI training.
The commitments follow the $500 million that Biohub — a philanthropic venture of Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Dr. Priscilla Chan — put into the project in April.
The investments fund the Virtual Biology Initiative, which aims to measure how cells respond to changes across far more conditions than scientists have so far studied, and use that data to build predictive models that could compress drug development timelines that currently take years.

"Biology has been just sort of a clever discovery-based science until this point," Chan said in an interview. "We have always held this as a community asset, not just for one group, so that it can build upon itself over time.” 
The datasets will eventually be released publicly, but companies that fund them get a head start, according to Biohub's head of science Alex Rives.
"With commercial funders we have embargo periods where there's a period of time where the groups can work on the data, and then it becomes available as a public scientific resource," Rives said. 
The arrangement is how Biohub is drawing private money into a project it describes as open science. Rives said the government-funded work running in parallel will carry no such restrictions, and that Biohub plans to approach pharmaceutical companies and philanthropies next.
Current cell datasets run to hundreds of millions of cells, Rives said, while an accurate predictive model will require billions and eventually trillions. Biohub's goal is to close that gap.
"We need to capture the language of biology, we need to capture the language of the cell. And that doesn't exist today," he said.
The data will come from techniques including spatial transcriptomics, which maps molecular activity inside intact tissue, and screens that record how cells respond to changes in environment. Much of it has never been generated in a coordinated way.
Rives said the work would normally take decades and that the partners aim to compress it into five years, with a first dataset ready in about a year. He expects accurate predictive models within five years.
Other AI labs are pursuing similar initiatives. Anthropic doubled down on its biology efforts with a wet lab, while the OpenAI Foundation started a more than $125 million grant program to fund biological and medical datasets for AI research.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Iranian official says 'illegal routes' in Strait of Hormuz to soon be blocked
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Despite growing oil flows in September, Iranian attacks on tankers have persisted.
items.body:
Transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz deemed illegal by Iran will soon be closed, an adviser to the Revolutionary Guards' Commander told the semi-official Fars News Agency on Wednesday, referring to the southern pathway hugging Oman's coast.
Mohammadreza Naqdi said these "few routes" had been created by blasting and damaging some of the rocky passages in the strategic waterway and were used by "small boats smuggling oil and transferring it to tankers", challenging the narrative that Gulf oil exports are [USN:L1N45R04U TEXT:"regaining pre-war levels."]
"The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran have full control over it. This situation will continue until Iran’s legitimate demands are met,” he added.
A seven-day moving average for crude exports from the region was 18.3 million barrels per day on September 30, provisional data from Kpler showed, with volumes topping pre-war levels on 14 days in September.
That included Gulf oil sent via Hormuz, the Red Sea, and from terminals and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman.
The IRGC has consistently denied that seaborne crude flows in the strait are rebounding thanks to US Navy help, with another IRGC adviser Majid Mirahmadi saying on Thursday that a daily average of 10 ships transit the waterway against an average of 125 before the war which started on February 28, when the US and Israel killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in a Tehran airstrike.
Despite growing oil flows in September, Iranian attacks on tankers and logistical constraints have persisted and call into question whether higher flows can be sustained durably.
