items.title: US government, Google join Zuckerberg-backed Biohub in $1.8 billion push for AI biology data
items.author: Krystal Hu
items.creator: Krystal Hu
items.summary: The US government and tech heavyweights Meta Platforms and Google parent Alphabet are joining nonprofit Biohub to build open datasets to train AI models for biological reasearch, bringing total investment in the effort to $1.8 billion, Biohub said on Wednesday.
items.body:
The US government and tech heavyweights Meta Platforms (META.O) and Google parent Alphabet are joining nonprofit Biohub to build open datasets to train AI models for biological reasearch, bringing total investment in the effort to $1.8 billion, Biohub said on Wednesday.
Meta, Google DeepMind and drug discovery startup Isomorphic Labs are jointly investing $300 million. The Department of Energy will invest more than $500 million over five years in laboratory measurement, modeling and computation. The National Institutes of Health will coordinate datasets and repositories built with more than $500 million in earlier federal funding, which Biohub will standardize for AI training.
The commitments follow the $500 million that Biohub — a philanthropic venture of Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Dr. Priscilla Chan — put into the project in April.
The investments fund the Virtual Biology Initiative, which aims to measure how cells respond to changes across far more conditions than scientists have so far studied, and use that data to build predictive models that could compress drug development timelines that currently take years.
"Biology has been just sort of a clever discovery-based science until this point," Chan said in an interview. "We have always held this as a community asset, not just for one group, so that it can build upon itself over time.”
The datasets will eventually be released publicly, but companies that fund them get a head start, according to Biohub's head of science Alex Rives.
"With commercial funders we have embargo periods where there's a period of time where the groups can work on the data, and then it becomes available as a public scientific resource," Rives said.
The arrangement is how Biohub is drawing private money into a project it describes as open science. Rives said the government-funded work running in parallel will carry no such restrictions, and that Biohub plans to approach pharmaceutical companies and philanthropies next.
Current cell datasets run to hundreds of millions of cells, Rives said, while an accurate predictive model will require billions and eventually trillions. Biohub's goal is to close that gap.
"We need to capture the language of biology, we need to capture the language of the cell. And that doesn't exist today," he said.
The data will come from techniques including spatial transcriptomics, which maps molecular activity inside intact tissue, and screens that record how cells respond to changes in environment. Much of it has never been generated in a coordinated way.
Rives said the work would normally take decades and that the partners aim to compress it into five years, with a first dataset ready in about a year. He expects accurate predictive models within five years.
Other AI labs are pursuing similar initiatives. Anthropic doubled down on its biology efforts [USN:L6N45814Q TEXT:"with a wet lab"], while the OpenAI Foundation started a more than $125 million grant program to fund biological and medical datasets for AI research.

items.title: Bochum fans banned from jumping for joy
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Germany's VfL Bochum have banned their fans from jumping up and down in unison in part of their stadium as the tribune movement makes some spectators feel unwell, the second division club said on Wednesday.
items.body:
Germany's VfL Bochum have banned their fans from jumping up and down in unison in part of their stadium as the tribune movement makes some spectators feel unwell, the second division club said on Wednesday.
Engineers investigated the structure as part of a Ruhrstadion upgrade plan and cleared its load-carrying capacity.
Their report, however, also highlighted the fact that the synchronised jumping of fans during matches created what they called a trampoline effect in the tribune that could trigger discomfort among those people who are not used to it.
The club said from October 11 any synchronised movement in the East Stand's standing area would be banned. The stadium has a capacity of about 26,000.
"VfL regrets the unavoidable measures but is relieved that the East Stand can be used at full capacity, provided the ban on jumping is observed," the club said.
The ban is expected to last until 2028.
"Fortunately, the renovation of the East Stand is already part of the modernisation project, meaning a lengthy planning process can be avoided and the ban on jumping lifted upon completion of the scheduled renovation work in 2028," Bochum said.

items.title: Japon-Les soldats US soumis à un couvre-feu à Okinawa après une affaire de meurtre
items.author: John Geddie
items.creator: John Geddie
items.summary: Les soldats américains stationnés à Okinawa, au Japon, se sont vu imposer un couvre-feu d'un mois et un stage de discipline, suspendant les opérations militaires sur place, après qu'un marine a été accusé d’avoir assassiné et dérobé une femme de la région.
items.body:
Les soldats américains stationnés à Okinawa, au Japon, se sont vu imposer un couvre-feu d'un mois et un stage de discipline, suspendant les opérations militaires sur place, après qu'un marine a été accusé d’avoir assassiné et dérobé une femme de la région.
Le caporal suppléant Devin Jacob Ballard, âgé de 20 ans, est soupçonné d'avoir tué samedi dernier Anna Yagi, 39 ans, et de lui avoir volé son portefeuille et son sac à dos.
Les faits se seraient déroulés dans un hôtel de Naha, la capitale de la préfecture d'Okinawa, un archipel situé à l'extrême sud-ouest du Japon.
Devin Jacob Ballard nie les accusations, selon la police.
Cette affaire vient s'ajouter à une série d'incidents survenus ces dernières années qui contribuent au malaise de la population locale face à l’importante présence militaire américaine sur l'archipel, situé près de Taïwan et de la Chine.
Les responsables américains ont averti que l'affaire pourrait compromettre des liens essentiels à la sécurité en Asie de l'Est.
"Chaque interaction avec nos voisins renforce ou sape la confiance qui est essentielle à notre équipe. Lorsque cette confiance est ébranlée, cela affecte la solidité de notre alliance et la sécurité de cette région", a déclaré mardi le lieutenant général américain Benjamin Watson dans un communiqué ordonnant ces mesures.
Toutes les opérations militaires américaines à Okinawa seront suspendues pendant 48 heures, le temps que les troupes suivent une formation sur les normes et la discipline, a ajouté Benjamin Watson.
Les militaires sont par ailleurs soumis à une interdiction de consommer de l'alcool.
"BRUTAL ET ODIEUX" La Première ministre japonaise Sanae Takaichi a qualifié le meurtre survenu samedi dernier d'"extrêmement brutal et odieux". Elle a déclaré avoir vivement protesté auprès des États-Unis et exigé que des mesures soient prises pour empêcher que de tels incidents ne se reproduisent à l'avenir.
Anna Yagi est morte par asphyxie après que Devin Jacob Ballard lui aurait "appuyé sur le cou", a précisé la police au journal militaire américain Stars and Stripes.
Le personnel de l'hôtel a retrouvé la femme inconsciente dans sa chambre aux premières heures de samedi, alors qu’elle n’avait pas réglé sa note.
Environ 200 agents ont participé aux recherches pour retrouver l'homme, qui avait été filmé par des caméras de vidéosurveillance alors qu'il entrait dans l’hôtel avec la victime, ont rapporté les médias locaux.
Lors d'une rencontre à Tokyo avec Genta Koja, le gouverneur d’Okinawa, Sanae Takaichi a déclaré que le Japon et les États-Unis continueraient à se concerter sur des mesures efficaces pour empêcher que de tels incidents ne se reproduisent. Cet incident a déclenché des manifestations à Naha et à Tokyo/
Le Japon accueille le plus grand contingent de forces armées américaines à l’étranger au monde. La plupart des 18.000 marines basés au Japon sont stationnés à Okinawa, que les États-Unis ont occupée de la fin de la Seconde Guerre mondiale jusqu'en 1972.
Cette présence a suscité à plusieurs reprises le ressentiment des habitants, notamment en raison de problèmes liés au bruit, aux accidents d'avion et au comportement du personnel.
Le viol, en 1995, d'une fillette d’Okinawa âgée de 12 ans par trois militaires américains avait déclenché des manifestations de grande ampleur.
Le meurtre de samedi pourrait compliquer les efforts de Sanae Takaichi visant à transférer une partie des marines de la base aérienne très fréquentée de Futenma vers une installation plus isolée à Henoko. Les opposants souhaitent que les troupes quittent la préfecture.
Okinawa, située à 100 kilomètres de Taïwan à son point le plus proche, est considérée par Tokyo et Washington comme un élément clé pour dissuader toute agression militaire potentielle de la part de la Chine.

items.title: El dólar sube a la espera de las minutas de la Fed; el euro cae hacia mínimos de 17 meses
items.author: Medha Singh, Rocky Swift
items.creator: Medha Singh, Rocky Swift
items.summary: El dólar subía frente a las principales divisas el miércoles, impulsado por el alza de los precios del petróleo, mientras los inversores esperan las minutas de la última reunión de la Reserva Federal y declaraciones de las autoridades monetarias en busca de indicios sobre un posible aumento de las tasas de interés.
items.body:
El dólar subía frente a las principales divisas el miércoles, impulsado por el alza de los precios del petróleo, mientras los inversores esperan las minutas de la última reunión de la Reserva Federal y declaraciones de las autoridades monetarias en busca de indicios sobre un posible aumento de las tasas de interés.
* El euro perdía un 0,83%, a 1,1166 dólares, cerca de los mínimos de 17 meses registrados la semana pasada, mientras los bonos franceses se veían sometidos a nuevas presiones debido a las preocupaciones fiscales.
* El yen cedía un 0,09%, a 158,265 unidades por dólar, incluso después de que una integrante del consejo del Banco de Japón, de postura moderada, afirmara que apoyará las alzas de tasas.
* "Para que el par euro-dólar caiga por debajo de 1,10 habría que descontar más subidas de tasas de la Fed de las que se descuentan actualmente, y ese no es nuestro escenario base", afirmó Adarsh Sinha, de BofA Global.
* La Fed tiene previsto publicar más tarde en el día las minutas de su reunión de política monetaria de septiembre, en la que elevó las tasas por primera vez desde 2023 para hacer frente a la inflación.
* El índice dólar ganaba un 0,64%, a 102,49 unidades, tras ceder un 0,27% en la víspera, al beneficiarse de la demanda de activos de refugio, ya que las preocupaciones sobre el suministro en Oriente Medio impulsaban los futuros del Brent de nuevo por encima de los 100 dólares el barril.
* "Llevamos varias semanas manteniendo esa perspectiva alcista sobre el dólar. Ha funcionado bastante bien. Pero creo que hay un elemento de impulso que está empezando a ralentizarse", dijo Dominic Bunning, de Nomura, añadiendo que el alza de los precios del petróleo está proporcionando un apoyo a corto plazo al billete verde.
* La libra esterlina restaba un 0,62% frente a su par estadounidense, a 1,3195 dólares.

items.title: Can Wall Street keep partying while bond markets burn?
items.author: Jamie McGeever
items.creator: Jamie McGeever
items.summary: There is a conundrum at the heart of US financial markets right now, it seems. Bond market fears are reaching fever pitch, catapulting Treasury yields to their highest levels in at least 20 years, yet the Nasdaq and S&P 500 are hitting record peaks. What gives?
items.body:
There is a conundrum at the heart of US financial markets right now, it seems. Bond market fears are reaching fever pitch, catapulting Treasury yields to their highest levels in at least 20 years, yet the Nasdaq and S&P 500 are hitting record peaks. What gives?
Investors could be forgiven for doing a double take. Boosted by the frenzied optimism around the AI-driven corporate profit outlook, the S&P 500 is up around 15% and the Nasdaq is up almost 20% this calendar year, even though the benchmark 10-year yield has spiked 120 basis points and the yield on ultra-long US bonds is at a 24-year high.
Soaring borrowing costs and a higher discount rate are typically red flags for stocks. Indeed, history shows that the rising cost of money almost always plays a significant role in severe economic and financial downturns, recessions, and market crashes. So equity investors have reason to be very cautious, especially given the market's historic concentration in a handful of artificial intelligence and tech stocks.
THE ‘WHY’ MATTERS But it's important to ask why bond yields are spiking.
The last time yields moved this much was in 2022 when the Federal Reserve cranked up interest rates aggressively to tackle the post-lockdown inflation whoosh that was then amplified by Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The 10-year yield leaped an eye-popping 235 basis points that year, and the S&P 500 slumped 20%.
Back then, sky-high inflation was the big concern.
That doesn’t appear to be the case this time around, although inflation is still above target. If Treasuries were being trounced primarily because of inflation indignation or even fiscal fears, one might expect to see a steeper yield curve and a spike in market-based inflation expectations. Neither has materialized. Breakeven inflation rates on five- and 10-year Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) are comfortably below their peaks from May, and the difference between short- and longer-dated yields has shrunk across most parts of the curve this year.
Instead, the primary driver of the rise in bond yields appears to be inflation-adjusted "real" yields, a sign that investors are pricing in strong real growth.
As Cullen Roche, founder and CIO at Discipline Funds, put it, "The bond vigilantes keep showing up expecting a funeral, but it turns out they walked into a growth party.”
And if bond yields continue to remain elevated because of robust growth projections and not spiking inflation expectations or other risks, Wall Street could keep on dancing.
WATCH THE TERM PREMIUM The divergence between Wall Street and Treasuries is so extreme that many fund managers say it is time to buy bonds. According to Bank of America, the 10-year rolling return for Treasuries with a maturity of 15 years or more fell to negative 2% last month. That's the worst return in more than a century.
And right now, investors can lock in real, inflation-adjusted yields of nearly 3% over the next decade, and 3.5% over the next three decades. These are generationally high, essentially guaranteed rates of return.
Will this pull capital away from equities? Perhaps, but investors seeking to build a more balanced portfolio may not have better opportunities to do so.
One major threat remains for both bonds and stocks: the term premium. That’s the amorphous degree of extra risk compensation bond buyers demand for buying longer-term debt instead of short-term paper. Sharp, upward spikes in the term premium suggest factors other than growth and inflation, such as doubts around central bank credibility or debt debasement fears, are driving yields higher.
The 10-year US term premium this week has snapped to a new 12-year high of 96 basis points, according to the New York Fed's closely watched Adrian, Crump, and Moench (ACM) model.
It's never clear what is driving the term premium at any particular time, or the ripple effect it will have across markets. But if it continues rising, Wall Street’s party could soon be over.
(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

items.title: IEA to meet Wednesday over proposed release of oil, diesel stocks, two EU diplomats say
items.author: Reuters Staff
items.summary: The International Energy Agency will hold an informal meeting on Wednesday to discuss a proposed release of oil and diesel stocks, two EU diplomats said, as details regarding the exact volume and ...
items.body: BRUSSELS -- The International Energy Agency will hold an informal meeting on Wednesday to discuss a proposed release of oil and diesel stocks, two EU diplomats said, as details regarding the exact volume and composition under the plan remained unclear. Record-high diesel prices have turned the fuel, which underpins trucking, agriculture and industry, into a global political and economic concern. The Group of 7 countries agreed last week to the new 100 million barrel release after U.S. President Donald Trump warned some European nations that the U.S. would ban diesel exports if they did not put more of the fuel into the market. The Paris-based IEA’s governing board was due to meet at 1300 local time (1100 GMT), the diplomats said. The G7 includes the U.S., U.K., Japan and Canada, along with European Union members France, Germany and Italy. The representatives of EU nations had already discussed the proposed release at a meeting on Wednesday morning, the diplomats added. Polish Energy Minister Milosz Motyka said on Wednesday that Poland was ready to release oil and diesel stocks if a consensus is reached, but he did not expect an IEA decision on this on Wednesday. The IEA’s board is expected to decide the details of the stocks release at an October 14-15 board meeting, two people close to the matter said on Tuesday. Extent of new volume not clear The IEA advises industrialized countries and coordinates their emergency oil stocks for use during major supply disruptions. In March, it agreed to release a record 400 million barrels of oil from strategic stockpiles to combat the spike in crude prices and supply losses that followed the start of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. Of this, about 325 million barrels have so far been released, the IEA said on Friday. It was not immediately clear on Wednesday if the G7 agreement would simply release the remaining share of the 400 million barrels, or add extra volumes on top of this, and how much would be diesel. Germany’s economy ministry said it was working on the approval of the release of energy reserves without mentioning any new amount. “Germany will participate in the further release of the volume already determined by the IEA in March,” the ministry said in a statement. As well as the war in Iran, the conflict in Ukraine has damaged oil refineries, helping to drive the rise in diesel prices. (Reporting by Kate Abnett and Holger Hansen; Additional reporting by Marek Strzelecki in Warsaw; Writing by Nina Chestney and Alex Lawler; Editing by Sudip Kar-Gupta, Jan Harvey and Joe Bavier)

items.title: Kenya infrastructure fund begins deploying $2.6 billion seed capital by buying bonds
items.author: Duncan Miriri
items.creator: Duncan Miriri
items.summary: Kenya's new National Infrastructure Fund has begun deploying its 340 billion shilling ($2.62 billion) seed capital by buying domestic government bonds, its chief executive said, in the first public disclosure of how it plans to finance projects.
items.body:
Kenya's new National Infrastructure Fund has begun deploying its 340 billion shilling ($2.62 billion) seed capital by buying domestic government bonds, its chief executive said, in the first public disclosure of how it plans to finance projects.
President William Ruto announced the fund [USN:L5N3VN08R TEXT:"last October"] to finance infrastructure projects without placing additional strain on public finances.
The fund's CEO James Mworia told Reuters that he expects the bond purchases to free up bank liquidity for private-sector lending.
Commercial banks are among the largest holders of the more than $50 billion of outstanding domestic government securities, often preferring them to riskier private-sector lending.
Burdened by high debt and annual repayments that consume 40% of government revenue, Ruto's administration has sought new ways to fund infrastructure.
"We have a high debt service level relative to our income, we have high social needs and we have a limit to which you can tax Kenyans," Mworia said, explaining the rationale behind the creation of the fund.
"But on the other hand, we have an infrastructure deficit."
Kenya's domestic bond market is the government's main source of financing.
Mworia said the fund began buying bonds in July, without saying how much has been invested.
"It will give a liquidity boost to the rest of the market," Mworia said, arguing banks would likely lend more to businesses and households.
INFRASTRUCTURE PLANS Mworia expects the fund to invest all its capital by the end of the financial year in June 2027.
At 340 billion shillings, the planned investment is equivalent to roughly a third of Kenya's domestic borrowing target for the fiscal year ending June 2027, Mworia said.
The bond portfolio is expected to generate about 42 billion shillings a year, helping the fund mobilise its targeted 3.6 trillion shillings over the next decade through co-investments and debt, Mworia said.
The fund will invest in commercially viable projects in energy, transport and logistics, information and communications technology, water and farm sectors.
The government capitalised the fund with proceeds from the [USN:L8N3ZS0PR TEXT:"privatisation"] of the Kenya Pipeline Company and the [USN:L8N3X927N TEXT:"sale"] of some of its shares in telecoms operator Safaricom.
Through the fund, Kenya plans to take a stake in a [USN:L1N45M098 TEXT:"refinery"] under development by Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote in the coastal county of Lamu, Mworia said, without disclosing the size of the investment.
The fund is also assessing other projects, he said.
"We have a lot of interest from other investors who would like to co-invest alongside the National Infrastructure Fund," Mworia said, adding that co-investors will come from Kenya and abroad.
($1 = 129.8000 Kenyan shillings)

Oct 7 : Core Stack, Lazzari Group's digital infrastructure business, and Green Arrow Capital will invest more than €1 billion ($1.12 billion) over the next four years to build 13 mid-size data centres in Italy, the two companies said on Wednesday.  
• The medium-sized data centres will be powered by renewable energy generated on-site.
• The companies said they expect to receive the required permits for the first two sites in the provinces of Cremona and Verona by the end of 2027 with operations due to launch in the first quarter of 2028.
• Following the more advanced projects in Italy's north and northeast, focus will move to the centre-south, the companies said.

Oct 7 : MotoGP's sprint races will have their own qualifying session from the 2027 season, resulting in a separate grid for the shorter high-intensity races, the motorcycle racing organisation announced on Wednesday.
• The sprints, which take place on Saturdays and offer 12 championship points for the winners, currently do not have their own qualifying sessions, and use the same grid positions as the Grand Prix races on Sunday.
• MotoGP will shorten the second practice session to 30 minutes, making way for a new 15-minute sprint qualifying session every Friday, to determine the starting positions for the shorter races.
• "The new format balances an incredible spectacle for fans and new stakes in each session," MotoGP said in a statement.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Analistas ajustan al alza pronóstico para el dólar en México y ven sin cambios tasa de interés
items.author: Zenyazen Flores
items.summary: El consenso de los analistas consultados para la Encuesta Citi de Expectativas espera que el tipo de cambio se ubique en MXN$18 al cierre de 2026.
items.body: Ciudad de México — Analistas ajustaron al alza su pronóstico para el dólar en México para cierre de 2026 mientras prevén que Banco de México (Banxico) mantenga la tasa de interés sin cambios este año y el próximo. La Encuesta Citi de Expectativas, publicada este 6 de octubre, mostró que las perspectivas para el peso mexicano se debilitaron respecto de la encuesta anterior de hace dos semanas, en medio de la erosión del atractivo del peso por el desacoplamiento de Banxico respecto de la Reserva Federal (Fed). El consenso de los analistas espera que el tipo de cambio se ubique en MXN$18 al cierre de 2026, desde los MXN$17,50 en la encuesta anterior, con expectativas que oscilan entre los MXN$16,80 y MXN$18,80. Ver más: Diputados aprueban Ley Aduanera con embargo precautorio en subvaluación de mercancías Para el cierre de 2027, el consenso espera que el tipo de cambio se sitúe en MXN$18,50, desde MXN$18 hace 15 días, con expectativas que van de MXN$17 a MXN$19,80. Al mismo tiempo, la visión de consenso se mantiene en que Banxico conservará la tasa de política monetaria en 6,50% hasta finales de 2027, con pocos participantes anticipando algún movimiento. La estimación mediana para el próximo movimiento en la tasa de política monetaria es de sin cambio hasta finales de 2026, de hecho, de los 37 analistas consultados, 25 no esperan movimiento alguno para 2027. El pronóstico mediano para la tasa de política monetaria al cierre de 2026 se mantiene sin cambio en 6,50% y para cierre de 2027 la expectativa mediana es de 6,50%, con estimaciones que van desde 7,25% hasta 6%. Ver más: ¿Qué países de América Latina sufren más por las tasas de EE.UU.? Estos son los más expuestos En su última decisión monetaria del 24 de septiembre, Banxico estableció en su comunicado que, dado que las condiciones macroeconómicas en México son distintas a las de Estados Unidos, la política monetaria no tendría que reaccionar de manera mecánica ante los ajustes previstos a la tasa de la Fed. Luego de registrar una tendencia a la baja entre julio y agosto, el dólar se ha apreciado desde septiembre de este año, con una apreciación en semanas recientes a medida que el mercado descuenta un incremento de tasa en la postura monetaria de la Fed, dijo Paulina Anciola, subdirectora de Estudios Económicos Banamex, en una nota de análisis. Esto se acentuó tras la primera alza que se llevó a cabo en septiembre, junto con un dot-plot que apunta a un aumento adicional este año, en línea con nuestras expectativas. En el caso particular de México, ni la retórica de Trump, el choque petrolero, el cierre del diferencial de tasas de interés en mínimos históricos, los ajustes a la perspectiva de la calificación soberana ni el escenario de revisiones anuales del T- MEC se habían reflejado en el mercado cambiario en la primera parte del año, lo que había mantenido apreciada a la moneda mexicana. Ver más: Banxico puede trazar la trayectoria de tasas de interés con independencia de la Fed: gobernadora Además, había predominado un mayor apetito global por activos de mercados emergentes, y el peso también se vio apoyado por el atractivo del diferencial de tasas de interés de largo plazo frente al resto del mundo, pero ahora se debilita el carry trade que había favorecido al peso mexicano. Anciola señala que el giro hacia mayores expectativas de aumentos en la Fed, aunado al desacoplamiento explícito de Banxico con respecto a ese banco central, ha llevado a una fuerte depreciación del peso mexicano hacia MXN$18,1-MXN$18,3 por dólar en lo que va de octubre, lo que implica una pérdida acumulada en el año de 0,6%. Derivado de lo anterior, Banamex ahora ve un nivel del tipo de cambio para de cierre del año en MXN$18,1 por dólar (desde MXN$17,6 estimado previamente), mientras que para 2027 proyecta el tipo de cambio en MXN$18,5 (MXN$18 anteriormente), si bien no se descartan periodos de volatilidad adicionales. Ver más: Diputados aprueban Ley de Economía Digital para reducir el uso de efectivo en México La Secretaría de Hacienda proyectó en el Paquete Económico que el tipo de cambio cerrará este año en MXN$17,8 por dólar y para fin de 2027 registrará un nivel de MXN$18 por billete verde. El 28 de septiembre, el peso mexicano cotizó en la barrera de los MXN$18 por cada dólar estadounidense, un nivel no visto desde marzo de este año, presionado por la política monetaria de Estados Unidos y México, la fortaleza de la moneda norteamericana y una mayor aversión al riesgo por la guerra en Medio Oriente. Días después, el 1 de octubre, el peso mexicano cayó casi 6%, al pasar de MXN$17 a MXN$18,07 por dólar, alcanzando un máximo intradía de MXN$18,43 por dólar y ubicándose como la divisa con peor desempeño dentro de las divisas de economías emergentes. Este movimiento representó su mayor caída mensual desde junio de 2024, de acuerdo con un análisis semanal de Banorte.

items.title: UK Conservative leader pledges to abolish inheritance tax on family homes
items.author: Hannah McKay
items.creator: Hannah McKay
items.summary: The leader of Britain's opposition Conservatives, Kemi Badenoch, pledged on Wednesday to abolish inheritance tax on family homes and let couples pass on an additional £1 million ($1.3 million) without incurring the levy if the party wins power.
items.body:
The leader of Britain's opposition Conservatives, [USN:S8N3UD03A TEXT:"Kemi Badenoch"], pledged on Wednesday to abolish inheritance tax on family homes and let couples pass on an additional £1 million ($1.3 million) without incurring the levy if the party wins power.
The Conservative Party, which has spent more time governing Britain than any other party, now sits third in opinion polls after [USN:L1N42U0AD TEXT:"years of political chaos"] and infighting in the aftermath of the [USN:L1N45M0A5 TEXT:"2016 vote to leave"] the European Union.
On the final day of the Conservative Party conference, Badenoch put tax cuts and growing the economy at the heart of her speech, framing the next election as a "battle for the soul of this nation" and contrasting her economic vision with that of the [USN:L8N45L1RD TEXT:"governing Labour Party"].
Badenoch said she would like to abolish inheritance tax entirely when the British government can afford it, which is currently 40% of an estate's value over £325,000, or above £500,000 if a home is given to a direct descendant.
"I believe the people who work hard and save should be rewarded for that effort," Badenoch said.
BADENOCH SAYS WORK TO DO TO RESTORE TRUST Polling suggests a cut in or abolition of inheritance tax would be broadly popular. Inheritance tax is regularly named in polls as Britain's most disliked levy even though only about 5% of wealthy estates pay the levy.
At its current level, the tax is expected to raise about £14.7 billion by 2030/2031, as rising property prices, particularly in London, mean a greater proportion of people are liable to pay it, according to research by the House of Commons.
In the speech, Badenoch cast herself as a champion of lower taxes and government spending compared to the [USN:L8N43N0JB TEXT:"state-directed economic plans"] of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's Labour Party.
Badenoch said Burnham's policies would make Britain "poorer" and accused him of wanting to spend "money we don’t have on things we can't afford".
She also proposed to cut employer National Insurance social security contributions from the current rate of 15% to 7.5% for 21- to 24-year-olds to help them find work.
Badenoch admitted there was "still a lot of work to do" to restore public trust in her party.
"People are looking through the shop window, they like what they see, but not enough of them are buying yet," she said. "We need to fix that."
($1 = 0.7560 pounds)

DURBAN, Oct 7 : Australia opener Travis Head has taken to task former test players turned critics whom he accused on Wednesday of “putting a bullet” through the current team, who start the first test against South Africa in Durban on Friday.
Head did not single out any pundit directly, but his strong remarks at a press conference came the day after Matthew Hayden, one-time holder of the record for the most runs in a test innings, accused selectors of “promoting the greatest pile of mediocrity that we've seen in a generation of cricket”. 
The reference, made in a podcast, was about the recall of Nic Maddinson, who has been out of test cricket for nearly 10 years, but who joined the squad in South Africa after Josh Inglis fractured his finger and Cameron Green suffered a stomach injury.
“I think it’s unfairly judged a fair bit from a group of past players, pretty much that put the bullet through a lot of players, which I think is unfair,” Head said.

“But that’s what they’re paid to do. Some of them need a job, so they go after us, and that’s totally fine.
“This group is strong enough to deal with those sorts of things. That’s how it is. It’s unfortunate sometimes to have some of that feedback from a generation of players that we have huge respect for, but that’s the caper.”
SELECTORS ACCUSED OF DISRESPECTING CRICKET
Hayden accused the selectors of "disrespecting first-class cricket”, asserting that batsmen should have an average of 45 runs or more before being considered for test selection.
But Head praised Maddinson’s abilities and the benefits of choosing experienced players for test cricket despite the 34-year-old replacement having a first-class average of 37.11.
“We need mature guys that know what they need to be doing,” Head said. “And I think that revolves back to why we’ve been so good over a period of time, and why Australian cricket was so good back then in that era, because you’d bring in the Mike Husseys of the world, who are 30, who are tried and tested and know what they need to do.”
Former Australia captain Allan Border suggested that the 32-year-old Head would face his toughest test as an opener against the South African bowling attack and would perhaps be better batting at number five. 
“I have laughed at a fair bit of it because if a traditional opening batter had pushed out the same sort of numbers in his first 20 innings, I think he’d be pretty safe and not talked about in the way that it has been talked about,” Head said. "It’s a lot of headline stuff."

Source: Reuters

items.title: QatarEnergy's LNG expansion project poised to start operations in November, sources say
items.author: Marwa Rashad
items.creator: Marwa Rashad
items.summary: The first liquefied natural gas train under QatarEnergy's North Field East expansion project will be ready to start operation in November, two people aware of the company's plans said, offering Qatar a path to restoring some output lost to Iranian attacks.
items.body:
The first liquefied natural gas train under QatarEnergy's North Field East expansion project will be ready to start operation in November, two people aware of the company's plans said, offering Qatar a path to restoring some output lost to Iranian attacks.
Launching the train would be a major milestone for the world's largest LNG expansion project at a time when Qatar is still recovering from the damage caused by attacks on Ras Laffan, which [USN:L6N407161 TEXT:"wiped out"] 17% of the country's LNG capacity.
LNG production from the train is expected to start in the first quarter of 2027, the people said.
QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.
QatarEnergy Chief Executive Saad al-Kaabi [USN:L1N45D0BX TEXT:"said"] last month that the project was expected to begin production in the first half of 2027 despite the US-Israeli war against Iran and the resulting disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Mehdy Touil — lead LNG specialist at Calypso Commodities, which develops AI solutions for LNG — said the next major step will be the introduction of feed gas followed by a gradual progression over several weeks towards the first LNG production.
"A sustained ramp-up will ultimately require the resumption of unrestricted transit through the Strait of Hormuz, but I expect QatarEnergy to have the first (North Field East) train ready regardless," he added.
Iranian attacks in March on Qatar's Ras Laffan facility damaged two LNG trains, repairs to which could take three years to complete, and one gas-to-liquids plant that will complete repairs in the first quarter of 2027.
Despite the damage, Qatar would be able to resume normal gas operations within weeks once the strait reopens, Kaabi said last month, adding that QatarEnergy is currently producing very little LNG.

items.title: Rahul Gandhi, Indian opposition lawmakers detained over election chief protest for second day
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Indian police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several lawmakers for the third time in two days on Wednesday as they launched an unannounced protest demanding the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.
items.body:
Indian police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several lawmakers for the third time in two days on Wednesday as they launched an unannounced protest demanding the resignation of the election chief over a [USN:L4N45K0E7 TEXT:"controversial revision"] of voter lists.
Opposition parties, their student units, and the "cockroach" youth movement have been staging [USN:L1N45O03D TEXT:"almost daily demonstrations"] seeking Chief Election Commissioner [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar's"] resignation, after the Indian Express newspaper last month reported disagreements within the poll panel over updating voter lists, stoking concerns over its neutrality.
Opposition lawmakers led by Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi [USN:L1N45S047 TEXT:"protested"] on Tuesday as well, seeking a meeting with Kumar and his deputies, before police broke up their gathering and briefly detained them.
Wednesday's protest began after a lunch meeting of lawmakers that Congress organised at a restaurant in central Delhi, close to the Jantar Mantar site where authorities permit demonstrations.
"Yesterday...Delhi Police stopped us and said you cannot protest here...so today...we will go to the designated protest site, sit there, and tell the country that, for us, Gyanesh Kumar is not the legitimate commissioner," Gandhi told reporters, referring to Jantar Mantar.
"The people who have done this (vote theft) are traitors...Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," he said, before boarding a bus that was to take the lawmakers to Jantar Mantar.
NEW POLITICAL CHALLENGE TO MODI Lawmakers in the bus held posters against the windows that said, "no vote theft, no democracy theft", and "election commission, not BJP commission", referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.
Hundreds of Congress members accompanied the bus on foot amid heavy deployment of police and paramilitary personnel in riot gear. Police also closed the road leading to Jantar Mantar, forcing the bus to take detour.
Gandhi later stepped out of the bus, with a live feed on his party's YouTube channel showing him standing at the centre of a crowd of protesters and security personnel, while his sister Priyanka Vadra and other lawmakers sprawled out on the road.
Visuals showed security personnel hauling Gandhi and Vadra into separate vehicles and taking them away.
There was no immediate comment from the police on the detentions.
The demonstrations present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term, just months after similar protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) youth movement forced the [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"resignation of his education minister"] over exam paper leaks.
Kumar has not commented on the voter lists issue but the election commission and BJP have denied accusations of wrongdoing.
items.raw_description: Indian police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several lawmakers for the third time in two days on Wednesday as they launched an unannounced protest demanding the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.

items.title: Ellison’s New Skydance Seeks to Wring More Profits From Movies
items.author: Thomas Buckley

LONDON, Oct 7 : Spanish Grand Prix organisers are planning to make changes to the Madring after complaints about the absence of overtaking and on-track thrills at this year's debut event, a spokeswoman for Formula One's newest circuit said on Wednesday.
The grand prix hype ultimately turned into a procession that even some drivers said had risked sending them to sleep, despite the banked 'La Monumental' curve promising to deliver as a standout feature, after earlier fears of crashes and safety cars.
Discussing the event at the Leaders Week London sports business conference at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge stadium, Juanco recognised there was work to do.
"The complaints about the lack of action on track, that's something we're working on," she said.

"It's not a difficult thing to change, because it's just a small modification in certain corners, but as you know it's not in our hands. We need FIA approval, but we are working on it."
Juanco said some pedestrian bridges would have to be moved after problems with visibility for some spectators sitting in certain grandstands. There were also gripes about the amount of time spent queuing for food and beverages in the fan zone.
McLaren's reigning world champion Lando Norris, who lost a likely win after an early virtual safety car period, said after the race that the circuit needed to "get rid of" turns 18 and 19 and have more of a straight into the hairpin to allow overtaking.
"I’m excited to come back here next year if they can make these changes because I think it’s a track that is good fun to drive and it can be a great racetrack. To me, it’s not a great racetrack," he added.
Juanco felt the situation had been exacerbated by an excess of caution by teams and drivers after a spate of crashes in junior series races, both in testing and early in the race weekend, that triggered red flags and safety cars.
There were also concerns about energy management with the new crop of hybrid cars, with engine tweaks already approved for next year. 
"Finally, we had nothing, just a virtual safety car. And so I think we can improve the show on track next year where we are working on it," she said.

Oct 7 : Former Spain forward Pedro Rodriguez announced his retirement on Wednesday at the age of 39, bringing the curtain down on a glittering 20-year career that yielded 25 major trophies.
Pedro, who became a free agent after leaving Lazio when his contract expired in July, was a key member of Spain's 2010 World Cup-winning squad and started in the final as they beat the Netherlands. He also helped Spain win Euro 2012.
"I feel it is time. The time to take a step forward and begin a new chapter in my life," Pedro said in a statement on social media.
"I leave proud of having lived my dream and of all the people who stood by my side to make it a reality. Thank you, football, for making me so happy."

Pedro broke into Barcelona's first team in 2008 and flourished under Pep Guardiola, winning 20 major trophies with the Catalan club.
The Tenerife-born forward scored in Barcelona's 3-1 victory over Manchester United in the 2011 Champions League final before joining Chelsea in 2015.
He won the Premier League title in his second season at Stamford Bridge and later spent a season at AS Roma before crossing the city to join Lazio, where he spent the final five years of his career.
Pedro made 794 appearances at club level, scoring 197 goals, while he netted 17 times in 65 appearances for Spain.

items.title: Tech companies tap debt, equity to fund AI and cloud expansion
items.author: Reuters Staff
items.summary: The world’s largest technology companies are tapping debt markets and raising equity to bolster AI infrastructure, marking a shift for Silicon Valley firms that typically relied on cash to fund their ...
items.body: The world’s largest technology companies are tapping debt markets and raising equity to bolster AI infrastructure, marking a shift for Silicon Valley firms that typically relied on cash to fund their investments. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta signalled in April that spending on AI would not slow down. Tech giants’ combined spending is now set to exceed US$730 billion this year, up from about US$700 billion previously. The AI boom has entered a “more dangerous phase,” marked by exponentially rising investments in physical infrastructure and growing reliance on outside capital, according to an analysis by Bridgewater Associates in February. SpaceX SpaceX is looking to raise about US$10 billion in bank loans and US$30 billion in investment-grade debt to buy Nvidia chips, the Financial Times reported. Apollo Global Management is expected to lead the deal and help place the debt with a broad range of investors, with bond fund Pimco among a small group of lenders in talks to provide financing, the report said. CEO Elon Musk said during SpaceX’s August earnings call that the company would exclusively build on Nvidia going forward because “we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best.” Amazon Amazon.com is looking to raise at least US$25 billion from the U.S. bond market, Bloomberg News reported in July, citing people familiar with the matter. The tech giant filed for an eight-part offering of floating and fixed-rate notes, according to a regulatory filing. Amazon is issuing senior unsecured bonds, with maturities ranging from three to 40 years, as per a term sheet seen by Reuters. In June, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing that it has issued $14 billion of Canadian dollar-denominated notes, marking a record size for the Canadian corporate bond market. It is also preparing to issue a six-part bond offering in Swiss franc denomination for the first time, a person familiar with the matter had told Reuters in May. Separately, the e-commerce giant is looking to raise about US$37 billion in an 11-part bond sale, according to a term sheet seen by Reuters in March. Nvidia Nvidia in June said it would raise US$25 billion through a U.S. bond issuance, as it taps the debt market to increase liquidity for the first time since 2021. The bond consists of seven tranches of notes, maturing as late as 2056, according to a term sheet seen by Reuters. Salesforce Cloud software provider Salesforce in March said it has priced a US$25 billion debt offering to help fund a major share buyback. The company announced a US$50 billion repurchase program and lifted its dividend by 5.8 per cent in February. The company had last issued U.S. bonds in 2021, securing US$8 billion to support its acquisition of communication platform Slack. Oracle Oracle in February said it expects to raise US$45 billion to US$50 billion in 2026 in a combination of debt and stock to build additional capacity for its cloud infrastructure. The cloud company was sued in January by bondholders who said they suffered losses because the company failed to disclose it needed to sell significant additional debt to build out its AI infrastructure. In September 2025, the company, chaired by Larry Ellison, filed to raise about US$18 billion in debt in a six-part offering to fund AI infrastructure, after investing billions in 2025. Alphabet Alphabet is looking to raise between US$20 billion and US$25 billion from its latest U.S. bond offering, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters. The company is offering notes in as many as 10 parts, a regulatory filing showed. The offering comes two weeks after the Google parent raised its 2026 spending forecast and highlighted plans for increased AI-related investments amid growing investor scrutiny of returns on such spending. In June, the company said it was looking to raise US$80 billion in equity offerings, including an investment from Berkshire Hathaway. It increased the size of its equity offerings to US$84.75 billion after seeing strong investor demand. The deal brings in Warren Buffett’s diversified holding company as a major new investor, adding a high-profile endorsement of Alphabet’s long-term AI and cloud strategy. Alphabet also plans to sell Japanese yen-denominated bonds for the first time, it disclosed in a filing in May. The issuance is expected to total several hundred billion yen, a source with direct knowledge of the deal said. The tech giant sold a rare, 100-year bond worth 1 billion pounds (US$1.35 billion) in February, as part of a global US$31.51 billion debt raise. The company sold 5.5 billion pounds worth of sterling bonds in a five-part deal, according to the final term sheet seen by Reuters. It had in November last year filed to raise US$17.50 billion in debt in the U.S. and 6.5 billion euros (US$7.50 billion) in Europe, for general corporate purposes, including the payment of outstanding debt. Verizon The U.S. carrier had in November last year filed to raise about US$11 billion in the corporate bond market to help fund its US$20 billion acquisition of fiber-optic internet provider Frontier Communications, which it closed in January. Meta platforms The Facebook owner had in October last year filed for its largest bond offering ever, of up to US$30 billion, to finance a costly AI infrastructure expansion. Meta has been navigating significant cost pressures from AI investments, boosting its capital spending plans by 73 per cent this year to offer personalized AI to its large social media user base. SOURCE: Data compiled by LSEG; SEC filings (Reporting by Anhata Rooprai, Zaheer Kachwala, Johann M Cherian, Harshita Mary Varghese and Prathik Jayaprakash in Bengaluru; Editing by Leroy Leo, Arun Koyyur, Anil D’Silva, Sahal Muhammed, Shilpi Majumdar and Jonathan Ananda)

items.title: Lower US Treasury yield view persists despite biggest quarterly surge since 1994: Reuters poll
items.author: Sarupya Ganguly
items.creator: Sarupya Ganguly
items.summary: US Treasury yields are forecast to fall over coming months, according to fixed income strategists in a Reuters poll who clung to their long-held view despite the benchmark 10-year yield recording its biggest quarterly jump since 1994.
items.body:
US Treasury yields are forecast to fall over coming months, according to fixed income strategists in a Reuters poll who clung to their long-held view despite the benchmark 10-year yield recording its biggest quarterly jump since 1994.
However, conviction behind calls for lower yields, which strategists have been [USN:L6N4520Y7 TEXT:"consistently wrong"] about over the past nine months, appears to be wavering.
Some strategists are basing their views on the position that financial markets have overdone pricing in a series of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and policymakers may end up doing less.
Meanwhile, government borrowing costs have hit [USN:L1N45N082 TEXT:"multi-decade peaks"] in many developed economies in recent weeks on fears of inflation from the US-Israeli war with Iran and rising central bank policy rates.
[USN:L6N45N0Q6 TEXT:"Heavy borrowing"] by tech giants to fund the AI buildout, coinciding with increased Treasury issuance, is only adding to rising yield pressure.
FED OUTLOOK GUIDING YIELD VIEW Median views from nearly 60 strategists polled October 5-7 showed the benchmark yield easing around 30 basis points to 5.00% by year-end, 4.90% in six months and 4.75% in a year.
The 10-year yield has risen almost 120 basis points this year and is trading a whisker away from the 5.34% it hit last week, the [USN:L8N45N0EQ TEXT:"highest since 2002"].
"Unless the Federal Reserve hikes a lot more aggressively than we expect, yields are probably a little too high," said Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research. He said his models pointed to yields being more fairly valued between 4.50% and 5.00%.
Interest rate futures are pricing in at least three more Fed rate rises over the coming months. The latest set of Fed [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"policymaker forecasts"] implied at least one more was coming this year.
That speculation has pushed up the rate-sensitive two-year yield roughly 40 basis points in the last month. According to the poll, it was forecast to fall about 10 basis points to 4.70% in three months, 4.60% in six and 4.25% in a year.
Still, all but 2 of a subset of 30 forecasters answering an additional question in the survey said the 10-year yield was more likely to land above their forecasts rather than below in the near term.
NINE MONTHS OF MISSES The recent US Treasury yield surge comes despite efforts from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in August to alter the schedule of debt issuance and attempt to increase long-end [USN:L1N44H0P5 TEXT:"buybacks"].
Reuters poll data show strategists have underestimated the 10-year yield's rise in nine straight monthly surveys this year, getting the direction mostly wrong in six of the most recent months.
Unexpected resilience in US growth is one reason. US GDP rose at a far-above-consensus [USN:L1N45L0XU TEXT:"2.2% annualised rate"] in the second quarter.
Foreign exchange strategists have also had a [USN:L6N45O04G TEXT:"bad run"], calling for dollar weakness on the 6-12 month horizon for at least half a decade and getting it wrong as a group most of the time over the last two years of monthly FX polls.
Three- and 6-month forecast ranges for the 10-year yield were also the widest since March.
Nordea, among the earliest in the surveys to correctly call higher yields, did so on the "stickiness of inflation pressures in the US", its chief analyst Jan von Gerich said.
There was "a straightforward case" that term premium, the additional compensation investors demand for holding longer-dated debt, "has been too low", he added.
Rates have entered "a different regime" from anything seen since the global financial crisis, said Meghan Swiber, director of US rates strategy at Bank of America.
"Long-end rates are really telling the Fed they should be doing more to tighten and rein in financial conditions — and a Fed not doing that is going to pay the consequence through higher longer-term rates," BofA's Swiber added.
"This is a divergence from how investors have been looking at rates over the past several decades. And there is inertia in investors' thinking about how high rates are going to go."

items.title: Francia suspende el uso de granadas aturdidoras para controlar las protestas estudiantiles
items.author: Nicolas Delame, Makini Brice
items.creator: Nicolas Delame, Makini Brice
items.summary: El Gobierno francés anunció el miércoles que suspenderá de forma temporal el uso de granadas aturdidoras en su actuación policial ante las protestas estudiantiles, después de que un joven de 15 años perdiera una mano durante un enfrentamiento con la policía antidisturbios.
items.body:
El Gobierno francés anunció el miércoles que suspenderá de forma temporal el uso de granadas aturdidoras en su actuación policial ante las protestas estudiantiles, después de que un joven de 15 años perdiera una mano durante un enfrentamiento con la policía antidisturbios.
Organizaciones de derechos humanos, estudiantes y algunos opositores políticos han acusado a la policía francesa de emplear una fuerza desproporcionada durante una ola de protestas estudiantiles que dura ya más de dos semanas y que ha puesto de manifiesto un profundo descontento social de cara a las elecciones del próximo año.
El ministro del Interior, Laurent Núñez, dijo que ordenó la suspensión del uso de granadas aturdidoras hasta que se aclaren los hechos ocurridos el lunes en la ciudad norteña de Lens. Asimismo, indicó que hay una "gran probabilidad" de que el disparo de una granada aturdidora no letal hubiera provocado la pérdida de la mano del joven.
"Suspendo su uso en el marco del movimiento de los estudiantes de secundaria hasta que se aclare lo ocurrido en este caso", declaró el ministro, quien añadió que se habían remitido un total de 18 investigaciones a la inspección de policía.
Los estudiantes de secundaria están indignados por el mal estado de las infraestructuras, la falta de profesores, los horarios sobrecargados y la falta de financiación en educación.
Atribuyen el empeoramiento de los resultados de Francia en el Programa para la Evaluación Internacional de Alumnos (PISA) de la OCDE a las malas condiciones de aprendizaje. Según las clasificaciones, estos resultados han caído más rápidamente que la media de la OCDE desde 2015.
Las protestas no daban señales de amainar el miércoles, con más de 500 centros educativos cerrados un día después de que las manifestaciones se extendieran por todo el país. Los sindicatos convocaron otra jornada de marchas callejeras para más adelante esta semana.
El primer ministro francés, Sébastien Lecornu, ha reconocido las reivindicaciones "legítimas" de los estudiantes franceses, pero también ha calificado los disturbios como las manifestaciones estudiantiles más violentas de las últimas décadas.

FAST

LONDON, Oct 7 : Manchester City should own up to their breaches of the Premier League's financial rules and accept their punishment, former England captain Gary Lineker said on Wednesday, adding he would not be surprised if they were ultimately stripped of titles.
City were found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the league's financial rules over nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as three out of four charges concerning failures to cooperate with the investigation.
The league said that City had used "sham" commercial contracts as part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than £900 million ($1.19 billion) over nearly a decade, during which time they won multiple trophies. City have appealed the ruling and insist they are innocent.
Former Everton, Tottenham Hotspur and Barcelona forward Lineker said the whole debacle was damaging for the club and the English game, but that City admitting their guilt would go some way to draw a line under the saga.

"Obviously it looks really bad for Manchester City, it really does. And bad for the game... I'd love to see Man City now just own it and just say, 'OK, we got it wrong'," Lineker told reporters at the Leaders Week sports industry conference at Stamford Bridge.
"'But for the good of the game, we'll accept it, we'll accept whatever punishment comes our way and we'll carry on'. I think that would be a blessing and save their face a little bit at the moment, though that doesn't look very likely," he added.
"But it is damaging... and I feel for their fans and I feel for their players." 
Asked if City should be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won in the disputed period, Lineker said: "I wouldn't be surprised if it goes down that route. But again, ultimately, who suffers from that? The players and the fans."
The appeal will take place in private. It remains unclear whether sanctions will be announced before the appeal is heard, and whether they would take effect immediately.
City top the Premier League standings on 15 points from five games and seek a sixth straight win at Liverpool on Sunday.

Oct 7 : Global stocks and the euro pulled back on Wednesday as oil prices rose above $100 amid renewed Middle East tensions while concerns France's fiscal woes could affect broader debt markets continued to weigh on overall sentiment.
The S&P 500 slid 0.6 per cent, a day after it hit a new record. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 0.85 per cent, also pulling back from a fresh all-time high.
MSCI's main world stocks index fell 0.9 per cent, while Europe's STOXX 600 was down 1.1 per cent, near its lowest level since June.
“In the very early stages of the fourth quarter, typically the best quarter of the year for equity returns, markets are being driven by a confusing ‘stocks up, US breadth down, yields up, oil down and up, and down...’ narrative,” said Jeremy Batstone-Carr, an economist at Raymond James.

Brent crude rose 1.65 per cent to $102.24 per barrel as the market weighed supply constraints from a storm heading for US oil-producing regions and attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia. US crude increased 1.34 per cent to $90.64 a barrel.
Aneeka Gupta, director of research at WisdomTree, credited still "really strong" earnings expectations for the stock market's relative resilience in the face of rallying oil prices.
"That's what's really holding up the market so far," Gupta said.
The French yield spread against safe-haven German Bunds — a market gauge of the risk premium investors demand to hold French debt — was about 11 basis points (bps) wider after narrowing for two days. It was last at 140 bps, and reached almost 160 bps last week.
French bonds have been under pressure as expectations of higher European Central Bank rates and political uncertainty before the 2027 election raise doubts over France's ability to fix its finances.
"Clearly the market is punishing France on its level of debt," WisdomTree's Gupta said.
EURO DOWN ON RATE DIVERGENCE, FISCAL CONCERNS
The rekindling of investor concerns weighed on the euro, which slipped 0.7 per cent to $1.118. It slid to a 17-month low against the dollar at $1.1161 earlier this week.
Wider yield spreads in the euro area weigh on the single currency by boosting expectations of ECB monetary easing, reviving worries about fiscal sustainability and stoking fears of increasing fragmentation in the euro area.
Markets also closely watched the rate divergence between the US and the euro area as they priced in a more hawkish Federal Reserve after the mid-September policy meeting.
"The interest rate spread between Germany and the US became more negative, which provided support to the US dollar against the euro," Georgette Boele, senior currency and oil strategist at ABN AMRO, said.
"We continue to believe that financial markets are pricing in too many rate increases by the Fed and the ECB," she said.
US TREASURY AUCTIONS, FED MINUTES IN FOCUS
Market participants will closely watch a 10-year Treasury bond auction later in the day and a 30-year auction on Thursday, which will show the depth of investor demand for US debt, analysts said.
US longer-dated yields hit a 24-year high on Monday amid a persistent selloff since late August due to concerns over inflation and the fiscal outlook.
The dollar index, which measures its performance against a basket of currencies, rose about 0.5 per cent, following a 0.27 per cent slide in the prior session. 
The Federal Reserve on Wednesday will publish the minutes of its September 15 to 16 policy meeting, which will be scrutinised for clues about potential rate moves over the next few months.
Traders cut the odds of a Fed rate hike in October to 19 per cent from about 50 per cent a week earlier.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Titan Mining signs preliminary deal with U.S. Army for Alabama graphite facility
items.author: Reuters Staff
items.summary: Titan Mining said on Wednesday its subsidiary signed a preliminary agreement with the U.S. Department of the Army outlining commercial terms for a proposed graphite processing facility in Alabama.
items.body: Titan Mining said on Wednesday its subsidiary signed a preliminary agreement with the U.S. Department of the Army outlining commercial terms for a proposed graphite processing facility in Alabama. The agreement comes as the United States moves to expand domestic processing capacity for critical minerals used in defense, battery and industrial applications. Here are more details: The proposed facility would be developed on about 97 acres of underutilized Army property at Anniston Army Depot in the state. Under the term sheet, Titan’s unit Empire State Mines would develop, finance, build, own and operate the graphite processing facility. The Canadian company said the facility would produce Purified Micronized Graphite — used in industrial, defence and battery applications — and later Coated Spherical Purified Graphite, a key material in lithium-ion battery anodes. The proposed lease framework includes an initial 50-year term with two 25-year renewal options, providing potential operating tenure of up to 100 years. The Army would have a right of first offer on certain uncommitted PMG and CSPG output, capped at 10 per cent of annual facility production. (Reporting by Varun Sahay in Bengaluru; Editing by Vijay Kishore)

items.title: India's Jubilant FoodWorks posts higher quarterly revenue as Domino's sales pick up
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: India's Jubilant FoodWorks said on Wednesday its consolidated revenue for the second quarter rose 11.9% on-year, driven by healthy sales at its Domino's pizza outlets.
items.body:
India's Jubilant FoodWorks (JUBI.NS) said on Wednesday its consolidated revenue for the second quarter rose 11.9% on-year, driven by healthy sales at its Domino's pizza outlets.
Quick-service restaurant operators are seeing demand recover after a sluggish start to the year. Motilal Oswal analysts expect growth to accelerate in the second quarter from the previous three months, although elevated fuel and raw material costs continue to weigh on margins.
The company, which operates Domino's Pizza (DPZ.O) outlets in India, reported a consolidated revenue of 26.09 billion rupees ($269.89 million) for the three months ended September 30, it said in a pre-earnings quarterly update. Standalone revenue rose 11.6% to 18.86 billion rupees.
Domino's India recorded like-for-like growth of 4.1% during the quarter, up from 2.5% in the June quarter. Jubilant did not provide like-for-like sales figures for its other brands.
In August, the company said its fried chicken brand Popeyes was emerging as a second growth engine, while efforts to revive dine-in and takeaway sales at Domino's, which have lagged its stronger delivery business, were showing signs of success.
Jubilant said it added a net 108 stores across its brands during the quarter, taking the total group network to 3,820 stores as of September 30.
($1 = 96.7750 Indian rupees)

Oct 7 : Life sciences company Danaher said on Wednesday it plans to launch its first AI-powered autonomous research lab early next year to make drug discovery and development faster and more efficient.
Here are more details:
• The lab, projected to operate at scale in early 2027, will combine AI, robotics and technologies from several Danaher operating companies in one connected workflow to develop custom antibodies and other molecular tools
• It is expected to make discovering molecules eight times faster and unlock a tenfold increase in generating target-binding molecules annually

items.title: Empleados de mina de cobre Centinela en Chile anuncian huelga tras fracasar negociación salarial
items.author: James Attwood
items.summary: El paro se produce en un momento en que aumentan las tensiones laborales en la industria del cobre chilena, en un contexto de precios casi récord.
items.body: Bloomberg — Los trabajadores de la mina de cobre Centinela, propiedad de Antofagasta Plc, en Chile, tienen previsto iniciar una huelga el miércoles tras el fracaso de las negociaciones salariales, lo que agrava las tensiones laborales en el mayor país productor de cobre del mundo. Los sindicatos Minera Esperanza y Distrito Centinela anunciaron en un comunicado que la huelga comenzará a las 8:00 a. m. hora local, luego de que la mediación obligatoria supervisada por la Inspección de Trabajo de Chile no lograra resolver el conflicto. Los sindicatos representan a más de 700 trabajadores. El paro se produce en un momento en que aumentan las tensiones laborales en la industria del cobre chilena, en un contexto de precios casi récord. Los supervisores de Escondida, del Grupo BHP —la mayor mina de cobre del mundo—, también han votado a favor de la huelga y se encuentran en negociaciones con la empresa, con la mediación del Gobierno. Ver más: Los venezolanos están abandonando Chile: tasa de desempleo entre extranjeros se reduce Cualquier interrupción prolongada agravaría las preocupaciones sobre el suministro en Chile, donde la producción de cobre ya se ha visto afectada este año por accidentes, condiciones meteorológicas adversas y contratiempos operativos. La huelga será la primera en Centinela, una de las cuatro explotaciones de Antofagasta en Chile. La mina produjo 240.400 toneladas métricas de cobre el año pasado. El principal punto de conflicto son las diferencias salariales y de beneficios entre empleados que desempeñan las mismas funciones pero pertenecen a distintos sindicatos. Los sindicatos afirmaron que la empresa rechazó un mecanismo propuesto para eliminar esas disparidades sin ofrecer una alternativa. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Funcionario iraní dice que pronto se bloquearán "rutas ilegales" del estrecho de Ormuz
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Las rutas de tránsito en el estrecho de Ormuz que Irán considera ilegales se cerrarán en breve, dijo el miércoles un asesor del comandante de la Guardia Revolucionaria (CGRI) a la agencia de noticias semioficial Fars, refiriéndose a la ruta sur que bordea la costa de Omán.
items.body:
Las rutas de tránsito en el estrecho de Ormuz que Irán considera ilegales se cerrarán en breve, dijo el miércoles un asesor del comandante de la Guardia Revolucionaria (CGRI) a la agencia de noticias semioficial Fars, refiriéndose a la ruta sur que bordea la costa de Omán.
Mohammadreza Naqdi dijo que estas "pocas rutas" se crearon mediante voladuras y dañando algunos de los pasos rocosos de esta vía navegable estratégica, y que eran utilizadas por "pequeñas embarcaciones que contrabandeaban petróleo y lo transferían a petroleros".
Esto contradice la narrativa de que las exportaciones de petróleo del golfo Pérsico están recuperando los niveles previos a la guerra.
"El estrecho de Ormuz está cerrado y las fuerzas armadas de la República Islámica de Irán tienen pleno control sobre él. Esta situación se mantendrá hasta que se satisfagan las demandas legítimas de Irán", añadió.
El promedio móvil de siete días de las exportaciones de crudo de la región fue de 18,3 millones de barriles al 30 de septiembre, según datos provisionales de Kpler, y los volúmenes superaron los niveles previos a la guerra durante 14 días en septiembre.
Esto incluía el petróleo del golfo Pérsico enviado a través de Ormuz, el mar Rojo y desde terminales y trasvases de barco a barco en el golfo de Omán.
El CGRI ha negado de manera sistemática que los flujos de crudo en el estrecho se estén recuperando gracias a la ayuda de la Armada de Estados Unidos, y otro asesor del CGRI, Majid Mirahmadi, dijo el jueves que por la vía transitan un promedio diario de 10 buques, frente a los 125 de antes de la guerra que comenzó el 28 de febrero, cuando Estados Unidos e Israel mataron al líder supremo, el ayatolá Alí Jamenei, en un ataque aéreo en Teherán.
A pesar del aumento de los flujos de petróleo en septiembre, los ataques iraníes contra petroleros y las limitaciones logísticas han persistido y ponen en duda que el aumento de los flujos pueda mantenerse de forma permanente.

items.title: Gauff falls to Mertens at China Open after 'draining' few days
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Coco Gauff crashed out of the China Open in the last 16 on Wednesday, suffering a 6-3 6-3 defeat by Belgium's Elise Mertens in what the American third seed described as a "draining" few days.
items.body:
Coco Gauff crashed out of the China Open in the last 16 on Wednesday, suffering a 6-3 6-3 defeat by Belgium's Elise Mertens in what the American third seed described as a "draining" few days.
Gauff revealed after her victory over Chinese 16-year-old Sun Xinran on Monday that she had received an [USN:L4N45S06O TEXT:""insane" amount of racial abuse"] on social media following a match in which a replayed point sparked an online backlash.
Asked what the previous 36 hours had been like, the 22-year-old told a news conference: "It has been kind of draining, I'm not going to lie. I just turn off my phone and move on. There's nothing you can do."
Gauff beat Sun 7-5 6-1 to reach the fourth round, but was targeted online after stopping play during a key point in the first set, raising her hand to complain about a flickering advertising board just as Sun was about to put away a winner.
After a video review, the umpire ordered the point to be replayed. Gauff won the replayed point and held serve for 5-5 before going on to seal victory over Sun.
Gauff later said she had received a barrage of abusive messages on social media after the match.
The WTA condemned the abuse.
"There is no place for racism, discrimination, or abuse in tennis," the WTA told Reuters in a statement.
"We are appalled by the racial abuse directed at Coco Gauff and are in contact with her to offer our full support.
"As we do for all WTA players experiencing online abuse, our Threat Matrix team is monitoring the abusive messages, working with the athlete's team to report them to the relevant platforms and seeking action on the content and the accounts responsible."
The Threat Matrix service was launched in 2024 and uses AI and open-source data to help protect athletes from online abuse and harassment.
The defeat against Mertens capped a difficult few days for the two-times Grand Slam champion, who had beaten the 30-year-old Mertens in all five of their previous meetings.
The 13th seed reached her first Beijing quarter-final in her seventh appearance at the WTA 1000 tournament and will next face six-times Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek.
"My coach/boyfriend (Christopher Heyman), it's his birthday tomorrow," Mertens said in her on-court interview. "So for me, this win is dedicated to him."
Gauff's challenge unravelled amid a barrage of errors, with the 2024 Beijing champion committing 34 unforced errors, including eight double faults, during the 78-minute defeat.
Gauff struggled to find her rhythm throughout the contest and, trailing 4-1 in the second set, told her team courtside that she had "no energy" and felt as though she might pass out.
"I think I just didn't play well," Gauff said. "I think I wasn't moving well. There were a lot of things I didn't do well. I thought Elise played well on the big points, made me play a big ball, yeah."

Oct 7 : Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, who last season guided the club to their first Premier League title in 22 years, has signed a new contract until June 2030, the English champions announced on Wednesday.
Arteta, who took charge at a time of crisis in 2019, has been at the heart of a long-term turnaround plan that has restored the club's status as one of the best teams in Europe.
“It's a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal," Arteta said in a statement.
"This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue."

Arteta ended his playing career in 2016 after five years at Arsenal, and joined Pep Guardiola's backroom staff at Manchester City as an assistant coach.
But he returned to Arsenal three years later, taking over from Unai Emery with the club struggling in 10th place in the Premier League.
Under the Spaniard, Arsenal returned to the league's top-five in 2021-22, and finished second three times straight before finally being crowned champions last season.
They also reached the Champions League final, where they lost to Paris St Germain in penalties.
“This is an important time in Arsenal Football Club’s history. We want to create a winning era together with Mikel," club CEO Richard Garlick said.
The club management backed Arteta's plan to rebuild the team, reinforcing the defence and midfield with signings like Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard and Ben White, and goalkeeper David Raya.
The investment paid off, with Arteta delivering a 62.05 per cent win-percentage after 361 games in charge, the best among all full-time Arsenal managers.
“We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together," the 44-year-old Arteta added.
Arsenal, second in the league, will return from the international break with a home game against Leeds United on Saturday.

items.title: US 30-year mortgage rate hits highest in nearly three years
items.author: Ann Saphir
items.creator: Ann Saphir
items.summary: The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to to 7.49%, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if the Republicans keep control of Congress.
items.body:
The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to its highest in almost three years, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if President Donald Trump's Republicans keep control of Congress.
The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage surged 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association said on Wednesday. It was last higher in November 2023.
Mortgage rates are tied closely to the yield on US 10-year Treasury notes, which earlier this week hit a 24-year high, driven by worries over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth.
The cost of living is the top issue on Americans' minds as they decide how they will vote on November 3, a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday showed, and is one reason why Trump's [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"approval rating"] is at a record low of 32%.
Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, which topped 5.3% on Monday.
Inflation is also on the rise, registering 3.4% in August by a measure that the Federal Reserve targets at 2%.
Fed policymakers have signaled they expect to follow their September interest-rate increase with another rate hike by year's end, though markets are for now betting they will not move at their upcoming policy meeting at the end of October.
Mortgage loan applications fell 4.2% last week from the previous week, the MBA said on Wednesday, with refinancing applications dropping sharply. Overall application volumes are the lowest since February 2025 and have fallen nearly 50% since January.
"Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market," said Joel Kan, the MBA’s deputy chief economist.

items.title: ロシア当局「ペスト流行リスクなし」、研究職員死亡巡りメディア批判
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andrew Osborn　Jennifer Rigby

［モスクワ／ロンドン　７日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Andrew Osborn　Jennifer Rigby

［モスクワ／ロンドン　７日　ロイター］ - ロシアの衛生当局は７日、東部シベリアのペスト研究所の職員が死亡した事例について、同地域で流行が広がるリスクはないと表明した。一方、世界保健機関（ＷＨＯ）はロシア政府に対し、死因に関するさらなる情報の提供を求めている。

シベリア地方のイルクーツク州にある研究所の女性職員（２８）が２日、原因不明の肺炎で死亡した。この事例を巡っては、トランプ米大統領を含め国際的な懸念が広がり、当初は約２００人が隔離対象となった。 

ロシアの衛生監視機関である消費者権利保護・福祉監督庁（ロスポトレブナゾール）は声明で、流行のリスクはないと結論付けたとして予防措置を縮小しつつあると表明。ＷＨＯとも最新情報を共有したとした。死亡した職員と接触した人の中からペストの症例は確認されておらず、約５０００件の検査でも危険な病原体は検出されなかったため、隔離対象者の９０％が解除されたという。

また、同職員はワクチン接種を受けており、「業務で扱っていた危険な感染症に対する免疫を獲得していた」とした。ただし、死因となった肺炎の原因や感染経路については明らかにしなかった。 

＜大統領府、メディアの「虚偽情報」を批判＞

ロシア大統領府のペスコフ報道官は、所定の手続きに従って事件についてＷＨＯに適切に報告したと述べた。メディア報道を事態の根拠として用いることに慎重であるべきだとした上で、「報道は非常に多いが、メディアがこの件について伝えていることの大半は虚偽の情報だ」と批判した。

ペスコフ氏はメディアなどに対し、衛生当局の発表する情報に依拠するよう助言した。

米ＡＢＣニュースはこれに先立ち、「米国がこの死亡事例へのロシアの対応について正式な外交抗議を申し入れ、ロシアに対し同事例に関する透明性の向上を求めた」と報じていた。

ペスコフ氏はまた、現時点ではプーチン大統領とトランプ米大統領との間で電話会談の予定は入っていないと述べた。トランプ氏は６日、この件について「まもなく」プーチン氏と話し合うと述べていた。
