items.title: RBI MPC raises FY27 inflation forecast to 5.2%, projects GDP growth at 7.1%
items.author: Vrinda Goel
items.summary: At its policy meeting, held between October 5 and October 7, the committee changed the stance to 'caliberated tightening' ...
items.body: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in its October monetary policy review, raised the FY27 consumer price index (CPI)-based inflation forecast to 5.2 per cent from 5 per cent, while raising the real gross domestic product (GDP) growth projection to 7.1 per cent from 6.7 per cent. “In light of the available data, it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year,” RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said. The RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on Wednesday unanimously hiked the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent from 5.25 per cent and changed the stance to ‘calibrated tightening’. The RBI changed the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate to 5.25 per cent, while the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate and the bank rate were changed to 5.75 per cent. Inflation forecast raised The RBI raised its FY27 CPI inflation forecast to 5.2 per cent from 5 per cent in the October monetary policy review, announced RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra. The quarterly inflation projections are: Q2 FY27: 4.9 per centQ3 FY27: 6 per centQ4 FY27: 5.7 per centQ1 FY28: 5.6 per cent Explaining the forecast, the RBI governor said CPI-based inflation increased to 4.8 per cent in August 2026 from 4.5 per cent in July. While the increase has been predominantly on account of higher inflation in the food and fuel groups, core inflation has also picked up, indicating some signs of widening price pressures. Food price increases have become more broad-based, along with notable spikes in certain items such as sugar and onion. The uptick in fuel inflation in August largely reflected unfavourable base effects. Core inflation increased to 4.2 per cent, while core inflation excluding precious metals increased to 2.9 per cent in August. The weighted share of items in headline CPI recording inflation above 4 per cent increased steadily to about 37 per cent in August. The RBI governor further said that the near-term inflation outlook points towards continued supply-side pressures on account of the deficient monsoon, ongoing El Nino conditions and high energy and other commodity prices, the pass-through of which is still continuing. GDP growth forecast raised The RBI raised its FY27 real GDP growth forecast by 40 basis points to 7.1 per cent from 6.7 per cent in the August monetary policy review. The quarterly growth projections are: FY27: 7.1 per centQ2 FY27: 7.2 per centQ3 FY27: 6.9 per centQ4 FY27: 6.8 per cent Announcing the forecast hike, Malhotra said that since the last MPC meeting in August 2026, the re-escalation of the conflict in West Asia and the consequent sharp volatility in crude oil prices have kept the global economy in flux. Global growth has remained resilient. Notwithstanding these persisting global headwinds, the Indian economy has remained resilient. Strong private consumption and fixed investment, a rebound in merchandise exports and sustained buoyancy in services exports supported growth. On the supply side, the manufacturing sector grew at a robust pace. Services sector activity strengthened further, owing to buoyant domestic and external demand. Malhotra further said that, looking ahead, global economic uncertainty will continue to have some bearing on domestic economic activity. While energy prices and supply chain pressures have continued, their near-term trajectory remains uncertain amidst the lingering West Asia conflict. Their adverse impact is being contained with active diversification of supply sources. Deficient south-west monsoon and strong El Nino conditions pose risks to the agriculture sector’s outlook and rural demand, although healthy buffers of foodgrains and proactive policy interventions by the government are expected to mitigate the impact. The RBI governor said that continuing momentum in services and broadly stable employment conditions are likely to support urban demand. Strong capacity utilisation, robust credit flows and the government’s thrust on infrastructure are expected to sustain investment activity. While services exports are expected to remain buoyant, bilateral trade agreements should boost merchandise exports.

items.title: インド中銀、約4年ぶり利上げ　追加引き締めも示唆
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jaspreet Kalra　Abinaya V

[ムンバイ ７日 ロイター] - インド準備銀行（中央銀行）は７日、主要政策金利のレポ金利を２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）引き上げ、５．５％とした。インフレ圧力が強まり、経済成長が堅調に推移する中、約４年ぶりの利上げに踏み切った。

金融政策スタンスを「中立」から「調整された引き締め（calibrated
items.body:
Jaspreet Kalra　Abinaya V

[ムンバイ ７日 ロイター] - インド準備銀行（中央銀行）は７日、主要政策金利のレポ金利を２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）引き上げ、５．５％とした。インフレ圧力が強まり、経済成長が堅調に推移する中、約４年ぶりの利上げに踏み切った。

金融政策スタンスを「中立」から「調整された引き締め（calibrated tightening）」に変更し、追加利上げを示唆した。ただ、マルホトラ総裁は、追加利上げの幅や時期は実際のインフレと成長の動向次第になると述べた。

中東紛争に伴う原油高がインフレを加速させ、購買力の圧迫や通貨安を招く中、インドも主要中央銀行に続いて利上げに動いた。インドではエルニーニョ現象に伴うモンスーン期の降雨不足も物価上昇圧力を強めている。

金融政策委員会の委員６人は全会一致で利上げを決定。ロイター調査では、エコノミストの６割近くが２５ｂｐの利上げを予想していた。

マルホトラ総裁は「インド経済は堅調で、成長の勢いは引き続き幅広い分野に及んでいる」と述べる一方、前回の政策会合以降、インフレ見通しが悪化したと指摘した。

インフレ期待の高まりや物価上昇圧力の広がりを示す兆候が一部に見られると説明し、「インフレの現状と見通しが、２０２５年のように良好ではないことは明らかだ」と述べた。

中銀はインフレ率見通しを従来の５％から５．２％へと小幅に引き上げた。コアインフレ率の予想も従来の４．３％から４．４％に引き上げた。

中銀がどこまで利上げを進めるかについては、アナリストの見方が分かれている。ＨＤＦＣ銀行のエコノミスト、サクシ・グプタ氏は「今後数カ月でさらに５０─７５ｂｐの利上げを予想している」とし、「中東紛争が長引き、原油価格が高止まりすれば、インフレリスクが一段と高まり、より積極的な引き締めが必要になる可能性がある」と語った。

インド１０年債利回りは７．２２６９％と小幅に上昇。ルピーは１米ドル＝９６．４３ルピーと、前日終値付近で推移した。

主要株価指数のＮＳＥ指数は０．３％下落したが、この日の安値からは持ち直した。

＜インフレ加速、成長は底堅く＞

８月の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）上昇率は前年同月比４．８２％に加速し、中銀の中期目標である４％を３カ月連続で上回った。燃料と食品の値上がりが経済全体に波及し、ＣＰＩ構成品目の半数近くで上昇率が４％を超えた。

マルホトラ総裁は「総合ＣＰＩの伸びは、今後３四半期に平均でほぼ５．８％になると予想される」とし、「こうした状況では、政策金利の調整が不可欠だ」と語った。

一方、経済成長は引き続き堅調で、中銀が消費者や企業の借り入れコストを引き上げる余地を広げている。

中銀は今年度の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）伸び率を７．１％と予想、従来見通しを０．４％ポイント引き上げた。

４─６月期のＧＤＰ伸び率は前年同期比７．８％で、中銀予想の７％を大幅に上回った。

マルホトラ氏は、これまでのところ需要面からのインフレ圧力を示す証拠は限定的だが、「通貨供給量や信用総量の力強い伸びを踏まえると」リスクはあると述べた。

＜中銀総裁「ルピーは過小評価」＞

マルホトラ総裁は政策発表後の記者会見で、金融市場は短期的には非合理的になる可能性があり、いくつかの指標はルピーが過小評価されていることを示唆していると述べた。

同氏は、インドが海外からの資金を誘致できているにもかかわらず、通貨予測やヘッジ行動がルピーのさらなる下落を示唆し続けている理由についての質問に「長期的に見てようやく適正な価値を見出すことができる」と述べ、「実質実効為替レート（ＲＥＥＲ）を含む多くの試算によると、ルピーは過小評価されている可能性がある」と語った。

同氏はその後、中銀はルピーが安定し、適正な価値を見つけ、秩序ある動きをするよう努めると述べた。

ルピーは７日、一時１ドル＝９６．８４５０ルピーまで下落し、５月に記録した過去最低値の９６．９６ルピーに迫った。

インド中銀は、原油価格の高騰、米国債利回りの上昇、海外からのポートフォリオ投資の流出などがルピーの下落圧力となっていることから、ルピーを下支えするためにスポット市場で定期的にドルを売却している。

同氏は、インドが海外からの資金を誘致できているにもかかわらず、通貨予測やヘッジ行動がルピーのさらなる下落を示唆し続けている理由についての質問に「長期的に見てようやく適正な価値を見出すことができる」と述べ、「実質実効為替レート（ＲＥＥＲ）を含む多くの試算によると、ルピーは過小評価されている可能性がある」と語った。

同氏はその後、中銀はルピーが安定し、適正な価値を見つけ、秩序ある動きをするよう努めると述べた。

ルピーは７日、一時１ドル＝９６．８４５０ルピーまで下落し、５月に記録した過去最低値の９６．９６ルピーに迫った。

インド中銀は、原油価格の高騰、米国債利回りの上昇、海外からのポートフォリオ投資の流出などがルピーの下落圧力となっていることから、ルピーを下支えするためにスポット市場で定期的にドルを売却している。

items.title: サッカー＝メッシ、代表引退試合で1得点2アシスト　「非常につらい」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ブエノスアイレス　６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ブエノスアイレス　６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのアルゼンチン代表主将リオネル・メッシ（３９）が６日、代表最後の試合となったベナンとの親善試合で１得点２アシストを記録し、３─０の勝利に貢献。２１年間に及ぶ代表キャリアに幕を下ろした。

スタジアムには８万５０００人を超える観客が詰めかけ、首都各地のランドマークも代表カラーの空色と白にライトアップされた。メッシの家族や、１９７８年、８６年、２０２２年のワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）優勝メンバーらも試合を見守った。

メッシは「話すのは難しい。いろいろな感情があり、さまざまなことが頭をよぎっている。最初に思い浮かぶのは父のこと」と最近亡くなった父親に言及。「２０年以上、このユニホームを着続けられたことは大きな誇りだった」と振り返った。

さらに「もうここに来られなくなるのは非常につらい。できることなら一生ここに来続けたい。アルゼンチン代表でプレーすることは人生で起こり得る最も素晴らしいことだから」と述べた。

試合前には、故郷ロサリオで「Ｇｒａｃｉａｓ（ありがとう）」と記された巨大な背番号１０のユニホームが掲げられた。チームバスがメッシの名を冠したトレーニングセンターを出発すると、沿道には数千人のファンが集まり、メッシが涙を拭う場面もあった。

試合はメッシのアシストからニコラス・オタメンディが先制。メッシは続いてニコ・パスの追加点を演出し、さらにＰＫを決めて代表通算１２６得点とした。オタメンディもこの試合を最後に代表を引退した。

試合後にはチームメートや相手選手らがメッシと抱擁を交わし、スタジアムではドローンショーも行われた。

メッシはいずれも代表歴代最多の２０８試合出場、１２６得点を記録。アルゼンチンを２０２２年Ｗ杯優勝に導いたほか、南米選手権でも２度の優勝を果たした。

items.author: ロイター

Duncan Miriri

items.body:
アフリカ大陸初の格付け機関発足、大手3社に代わる選択肢提供
13:32 配信

2021年11月、エチオピアの首都アジスアベバにあるアフリカ連合（AU）本部ビル。 REUTERS/Tiksa Negeri

Duncan Miriri

[ナイロビ ７日 ロイター] - アフリカ連合（ＡＵ）は７日、アフリカ大陸初の信用格付け機関を発足させる。多くのアフリカ諸国で債務負担が経済の重しとなる中、世界の格付け大手３社に代わる選択肢を提供することを目指す。

アフリカ信用格付け機関（ＡｆＣＲＡ）はモーリシャスの首都ポートルイスに本拠を置く。同機関の設立は、アフリカ各国の首脳が２０１８年に承認していた。

ＡＵは声明で「ＡｆＣＲＡはアフリカのデータ、専門知識、実情に根差した視点を提供することで、既存の世界的な信用格付け機関を補完する」と表明した。

アフリカの指導者は以前から、３大格付け会社がアフリカ諸国への融資リスクを公正に評価しておらず、紛争やパンデミック（世界的大流行）などの危機時にアフリカの格付けを性急に引き下げていると批判してきた。

ＡＵによると、ＡｆＣＲＡは国や金融機関、民間企業を格付け対象とし、独立して運営される。株主からの出資と事業収入で資金を賄う。ＡＵは株主の詳細を明らかにしなかった。

items.title: US forces face curfew, alcohol ban in Japan's Okinawa after murder case
items.author: CNA
items.summary: The presence of US forces has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents in Okinawa over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of its troops.

US forces face curfew, alcohol ban in Japan's Okinawa after murder case

The presence of US forces has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents in Okinawa over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of its troops.

Demonstrators take part in a protest outside the Prime Minister's office following the killing of a Japanese woman in Okinawa, for which a US Marine is a suspect, in Tokyo, Japan, on Oct 5, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Kim Kyung-Hoon)

FAST

TOKYO: US soldiers stationed on Japan's Okinawa have been given a month-long curfew and banned from drinking alcohol while they undergo discipline training after a Marine was alleged to have murdered and robbed a local woman .
Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in Naha, the capital of the southernmost prefecture, on Saturday (Oct 3) and taking her wallet and backpack. Ballard denied the allegations, police said.
The case is the latest in a string of incidents stretching back years that have fuelled unease over the large US troop presence on the island chain near Taiwan and China, with US officials warning it could undermine ties vital to security in East Asia.
"Every interaction with our neighbours either builds or undermines the trust that is essential to our team. When that trust is damaged, it affects the strength of our alliance and the security of this region," Lt Gen Benjamin Watson said in a statement on Tuesday ordering the measures.

Loading

All US military operations on Okinawa will be paused for 48 hours while troops undergo training on standards and discipline, Watson added.
"BRUTAL AND HEINOUS" Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called Saturday's killing "extremely brutal and heinous". She said she had strongly protested to the United States and demanded measures to prevent such incidents in the future.
Yagi died of asphyxiation after Ballard allegedly "pressed on her neck," police told the Stars and Stripes newspaper. 

Devin Jacob Ballard, a U.S. Marine who has been in custody in an alleged robbery and murder of a woman on Japan's southern island of Okinawa, is sent over to the Naha prosecutors' office in Japan, Monday, Oct. 5, 2026. (Kotaro Ueda/Kyodo News via AP)

Hotel staff found the woman unconscious in her room in the early hours of Saturday after she failed to check out. About 200 officers were involved in a search for the man earlier caught on CCTV entering the hotel with the victim, local media reported. 
Okinawa Governor Genta Koja will meet Takaichi on Wednesday to discuss the response to the crime, which sparked protests in Naha and Tokyo.
Japan hosts the largest overseas contingent of US forces globally. Most of the 18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War II until 1972.
That presence has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of its troops.
The 1995 rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen sparked mass demonstrations.
Saturday's killing could complicate Takaichi's efforts to relocate some Marines from the busy Futenma air base to a more remote facility at Henoko. Opponents want the troops moved out of the prefecture.
Okinawa, which is 100km from Taiwan at the closest point, is viewed by Tokyo and Washington as key in deterring potential military aggression from China.

items.title: African Union to launch continent's first credit rating agency
items.author: Duncan Miriri
items.creator: Duncan Miriri
items.summary: The African Union will launch the continent's first credit rating agency on Wednesday, seeking to provide an alternative to the "big three" global ratings agencies as debt burdens weigh on many African economies.
items.body:
The African Union will launch the continent's first credit rating agency on Wednesday, seeking to provide an alternative to the "big three" global ratings agencies as debt burdens weigh on many African economies.
The Africa Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA) — the creation of which African leaders endorsed in 2018 — will be launched in Port Louis, the capital of Mauritius, where it will be based.
"AfCRA complements existing global credit rating agencies by offering a perspective rooted in African data, expertise and realities," the AU said in a statement.
African leaders have long accused Western ratings agencies including S&P, Moody's and Fitch of failing to [USN:L6N41N01Z TEXT:"fairly assess"] the risk of lending to African countries and of moving too quickly to downgrade them during crises such as conflicts and pandemics.
The agencies reject that criticism, saying they apply the same methodologies globally.
A 2024 Reuters investigation into Africa's debt crisis found no evidence of systemic bias in the sovereign ratings assigned to the region by the three major global credit rating agencies.
CREDIBILITY TEST IN TIMES OF CRISIS Rating experts said the success of the initiative will hinge on the perceived credibility of the new agency, especially in times of crisis.
"A new rating agency begins with a promise while investors ultimately require a track record," said Dennis Shen, a lecturer in finance at the International School of Management in Berlin and former sovereign analyst at Scope Ratings.
"The hardest test, however, will come when markets are under stress, because a rating agency’s credibility is tested most severely when its conclusions are uncomfortable rather than when it is highly convenient."
AfCRA may provide a counterweight to established rating agencies, but it must meet global standards, former Nigerian Vice President Yemi Osinbajo said.
"It can't just be a chauvinistic or nationalistic agency," he said.
BORROWING COSTS IN FOCUS AfCRA, which will rate sovereign borrowers, financial institutions and private companies, will operate independently and be funded through shareholder capital and its operations, the AU said. It did not provide details about the
shareholders.
The AU says the agency should help improve African countries' access to capital markets and provide investors with more balanced and context-specific assessments of economies across the continent.
It noted that African economies are currently rated B to B-minus on average, compared with BB for other emerging regions, a gap the AU says can limit some investors' participation and raise borrowing costs.
The drive to improve borrowing terms for the continent has become more urgent following years of increased government borrowing, pushing some countries into debt distress in recent years.
"The stakes are significant," the AU said, adding that the continent's annual external debt service surged to $163 billion in 2024, from $61 billion in 2010.
In many countries, interest payments have exceeded the annual budgets for key social sectors such as health and education.
AfCRA is also expected to boost coverage, with 23 economies on the continent lacking a rating from the three big agencies, the AU said.

items.title: 仏ミストラル、一部中国勢上回る新ＡＩモデル発表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Elizabeth Howcroft　Leo Marchandon

[パリ ６日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）を手...
items.body:
仏ミストラル、一部中国勢上回る新ＡＩモデル発表
12:46 配信

Elizabeth Howcroft　Leo Marchandon

[パリ ６日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）を手がけるフランスの新興企業ミストラルは６日、新たなＡＩモデル「ミストラルＬａｒｇｅ４（ラージ４）」を発表した。同モデルは多くの競合するオープンウェイトモデルを上回る性能を発揮すると主張している。

設立から３年目となる同社は、米国や中国の競合他社に対して欧州で最も強力なＡＩ挑戦者と見なされているが、５月以来、新しいモデルを発表していなかった。

ミストラルのアルチュール・メンシュ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）はアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）の首都アブダビでの発表イベントで「本日発表するモデルは、サイバーセキュリティーを含む特定の側面において、中国のモデルを上回っている。したがって『欧州は（中国や米国と）競争できない』という説は事実ではない」と述べた。具体的な中国のモデルについては言及しなかった。

メンシュ氏は、ラージ４を今月２７日に一般公開すると明らかにした。一般公開に先立ち、サイバーセキュリティーの専門家や政府当局に安全上の制限を緩和したバージョンを提供し、性能をテストしてもらうという。

ミストラルの科学担当副社長、ピエール・ストック氏はロイターに対し、ラージ４は利用できるオープンウェイト型システムで最強の部類に属すると強調。ラージ４がテスト環境の外に出ようとしたことがあったが、予想されていたことで阻止できたと語った。

オープンウェイトとはユーザーがプラットフォームからモデルをダウンロードし、自身のハードウエア上で実行できることを意味する。多くの中国製モデルはオープンウェイトである一方、米国のトップクラスのモデルはクローズド型で、開発者のインフラを通じてのみアクセス可能となっている。

ミストラルによると、ラージ４はコーディング、金融、地理空間分析、製造、製品設計などの分野で「最先端モデルとの差を縮めている」という。同社は自社のインフラ上でラージ４に学習させた。

中国人民銀行、9月も金購入　23カ月連続
12:31 配信

銀行の金庫に保管されている金塊。2014年11月20日にチューリッヒで撮影。 REUTERS/Arnd Wiegmann

[北京 ７日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）が７日に公表した公式データによると、９月末の金保有量は７７４７万トロイオンスと、前月末の７６７３万トロイオンスから増加した。２３カ月連続の増加となる。

中国は今年、価格が大きく変動する中でも金の積み増しを続けている。 

９月末時点の金準備の評価額は３２３５億２０００万ドルと、前月末の３５００億８０００万ドルから減少した。  

金価格は９月に６％以上下落した。

７日０２４４ＧＭＴ（日本時間午前１１時４４分）時点で、金現物価格は１オンス＝４１４７．４７ドル付近で取引されていた。

FAST

TOKYO, Oct 7 : Shares of major Japanese beer makers fell nearly 4 per cent on Wednesday after Japan's Fair Trade Commission said it raided the country's four major beer makers on suspicion of collusion in sales of beer and other products to wholesalers. 
The beer divisions of Kirin Holdings Co, Asahi Group Holdings, unlisted Suntory Holdings as well as Sapporo Breweries,  which together control more than 90 per cent of Japan's domestic beer market, are suspected of coordinating prices over several years.
Public broadcaster NHK said the Fair Trade Commission was probing whether the companies formed a cartel when they raised prices in April last year and October 2022, citing factors including rising raw material costs.
The anti-trust watchdog is expected to continue its investigation and could file a criminal complaint, a source familiar with the matter said, declining to be named because the person was not authorised to talk to the press. The Commission declined to elaborate on the investigation.

Shares in Sapporo fell as much as 3.73 per cent, while Kirin briefly shed a little over 3 per cent to hit its lowest level in more than three months. Asahi dropped nearly 2.5 per cent before recouping some losses.
In statements, the four beer makers separately confirmed the raids and said they intend to cooperate with the investigation.
The Fair Trade Commission has carried out similar probes into well-known Japanese companies in recent months. In June, it raided six Japanese ice-cream makers, including Morinaga Milk Industry  and Meiji Holdings, over allegations of operating a cartel.

items.author: ロイター

items.summary:
Atsuko Aoyama

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 午前のドルは１５８円半ばで、約２週間ぶりの高値を付けた。明...
items.body:
午前のドルは158円半ば、約2週間ぶり高値　上値は重い
12:25 配信

日本円の為替レートを表示する電子スクリーンの前で2026年5月12日撮影　REUTERS/Issei Kato

Atsuko Aoyama

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 午前のドルは１５８円半ばで、約２週間ぶりの高値を付けた。明確な材料は見当たらないものの、堅調な原油価格や株価動向などを背景にドル買い／円売りが進んだ。２００日移動平均線の近辺となっており、一段高となるには材料不足との声もあった。

・ドルは１５８．５１円まで上値伸ばす、９月２５日以来の高値

・２００日移動平均線近辺に、上値重いとの声も

・堅調な原油先物価格がドル買いを支援

・仲値では輸入のドル買い観測も

・佐藤綾野日銀審議委員の発言は材料視されず、前回決定会合での反対票の火消しとの見方も

・第２次補正予算の検討報道は円の重しとの声

・ユーロ／円は１７８円前半で強含んだ後、１７７円台に下落

＜りそなホールディングス　シニアストラテジスト　井口慶一氏＞

「ドル買い／円売りが進む材料は特段見当たらない」

「２００日移動平均線が近づき、さらに上抜けするにはもう少し材料が必要」

「円安が進まないよう日米が共にけん制姿勢を示しており、ドル／円は動きにくい。ただ、円高方向の材料があった場合は素直に反応する可能性がある」

「佐藤日銀審議委員はもともとハト派とみられており、今回の発言をもって円売りを仕掛けることはないのではないか」

items.body:
午前の日経平均は反落、利益確定売り優勢　ＴＯＰＩＸも下落
11:59 配信

東京証券取引所。都内で４月撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Hiroko Hamada

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 前場の東京株式市場で日経平均は反落し、前営業日比０．８６％（６０９円８５銭）安の７万００７４円１３銭となった。前日までの続伸の反動で利益確定売りが優勢となった。指数寄与度の大きい半導体関連株や電子部品関連株が軟調で相場の重しとなり、日経平均は一時６６６円安となる場面があった。ＴＯＰＩＸも下落した。

・日経平均は前営業日比０．１４％安でスタートした後、一時プラス転換したが、すぐにマイナス圏に沈んだ。

・前場終盤にかけて売りが強まる。節目の７万円は維持。

・ＴＯＰＩＸは８月１４日に付けた終値ベース高値を上回ったが、上昇一服後は小幅安に転じた。

・物色面では、前日に引き続き一部のサイバーセキュリティ関連が高い。決算発表など個別材料を手掛かりにした物色も活発。

・ＴＯＰＩＸは０．５９％安の４１５８．８９ポイントで午前の取引を終了。東証プライム市場の売買代金は３兆８８１９億０２００万円。

・東証３３業種では、ゴム製品、電気・ガス、不動産など８業種が値上がり。非鉄金属、銀行、鉄鋼など２５業種は値下がりした。

・東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが４５４銘柄（２９％）、値下がりは１０４７銘柄（６７％）、変わらずは５１銘柄（３％）。

＜内藤証券　投資調査部長　田部井美彦氏＞

「今月下旬から始まる企業の決算シーズンを前に業績を確認したいという思惑も強い。決算シーズンに入るまでは日経平均は上下動を繰り返す展開を想定」

「個別では、今週決算を発表する安川電機に注目。内容が良ければ来週以降の日本株の支えに」

「半導体関連企業は好業績が見込まれる反面、それ以外の業種では金利上昇やコスト高にどう対応するかが焦点になりそうだ」

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 国内ビール大手４社が、ビールなどを卸売業者に出荷する価...
items.body:
公取委、ビール大手4社にカルテル疑いで強制調査　刑事告発視野＝関係者
11:42 配信

写真は2015年10月、都内のビール売り場で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 国内ビール大手４社が、ビールなどを卸売業者に出荷する価格についてカルテルを結んだ疑いがあるとして、公正取引委員会が７日、強制調査を行ったことが関係者の話で分かった。刑事告発も視野に調査を進めるとみられる。

４社はアサヒビール、キリンビール、サントリー、サッポロビール。関係者によると、各社の担当者らが集まるなどし、数年にわたって価格を調整していた疑いがあるという。

公取委の岩成博夫事務総長は７日の定例会見で、このタイミングでの調査開始について、犯則事件として調査を始めるに足る証拠が得られたためと説明。調査はスタートしたばかりだとして、詳細に関する言及は控えた。

４社は独占禁止法（独禁法）に基づき公取委の調査を受けたことを認め、全面的に協力するとのコメントを発表した。

items.title: World shares, euro slide as energy shock, fiscal worries bite
items.author: Lawrence Delevingne, Stefano Rebaudo
items.creator: Lawrence Delevingne, Stefano Rebaudo
items.summary: Global stocks and the euro pulled back on Wednesday as oil prices rose above $100 amid renewed Middle East tensions while concerns France's fiscal woes could affect broader debt markets continued to weigh on overall sentiment.
items.body:
Global stocks and the euro pulled back on Wednesday as oil prices rose above $100 amid renewed Middle East tensions while concerns France's fiscal woes could affect broader debt markets continued to weigh on overall sentiment.
The S&P 500 (.SPX) slid 0.6%, a day after it hit a new [USN:L6N45S16W TEXT:"record."] The tech-heavy Nasdaq (.IXIC) fell 0.85%, also pulling back from a fresh all-time high.
MSCI's main world stocks index (.MIWD00000PUS) fell 0.9%, while Europe's STOXX 600 (.STOXX) was [USN:L4N45T0JA TEXT:"down"] 1.1%, near its lowest level since June.
“In the very early stages of the fourth quarter, typically the best quarter of the year for equity returns, markets are being driven by a confusing ‘stocks up, US breadth down, yields up, oil down and up, and down...’ narrative,” said Jeremy Batstone-Carr, an economist at Raymond James.
Brent crude [USN:L1N45T02U TEXT:"rose"] 1.65% to $102.24 per barrel as the market weighed supply constraints from a storm heading for US oil-producing regions and attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia. US crude increased 1.34% to $90.64 a barrel.
Aneeka Gupta, director of research at WisdomTree, credited still "really strong" earnings expectations for the stock market's relative resilience in the face of rallying oil prices.
"That's what's really holding up the market so far," Gupta said.
The French yield spread against safe-haven German Bunds — a market gauge of the risk premium investors demand to hold French debt — was about 11 basis points (bps) wider after narrowing for two days. It was last at 140 bps, and reached almost 160 bps last week.
French bonds have been under pressure as expectations of higher European Central Bank rates and political uncertainty before the 2027 election raise doubts over France's ability to fix its finances.
"Clearly the market is punishing France on its level of debt," WisdomTree's Gupta said.
EURO DOWN ON RATE DIVERGENCE, FISCAL CONCERNS The rekindling of investor concerns [USN:L6N45T0MX TEXT:"weighed"] on the euro , which slipped 0.7% to $1.118. It slid to a 17-month low against the dollar at $1.1161 earlier this week.
Wider yield spreads in the euro area weigh on the single currency by boosting expectations of ECB monetary easing, reviving worries about fiscal sustainability and stoking fears of increasing fragmentation in the euro area.
Markets also closely watched the rate divergence between the US and the euro area as they priced in a more hawkish Federal Reserve after the mid-September policy meeting.
"The interest rate spread between Germany and the US became more negative, which provided support to the US dollar against the euro," Georgette Boele, senior currency and oil strategist at ABN AMRO, said.
"We continue to believe that financial markets are pricing in too many rate increases by the Fed and the ECB," she said.
US TREASURY AUCTIONS, FED MINUTES IN FOCUS Market participants will closely watch a 10-year Treasury bond auction later in the day and a 30-year auction on Thursday, which will show the depth of investor demand for US debt, analysts said.
US longer-dated yields hit a 24-year high on Monday amid a persistent selloff since late August due to concerns over inflation and the fiscal outlook.
The dollar index , which measures its performance against a basket of currencies, rose about 0.5%, following a 0.27% slide in the prior session.
The Federal Reserve on Wednesday will publish the minutes of its September 15 to 16 policy meeting, which will be scrutinised for clues about potential rate moves over the next few months.
Traders cut the odds of a Fed rate hike in October to 19% from about 50% a week earlier.

items.body:
ビングループ、仏アルストムから鉄道技術　ハノイに車両供給で合意
11:37 配信

ビングループ本社。ベトナム・ハノイで２月撮影。REUTERS/Khanh Vu

[ハノイ ６日 ロイター] - ベトナムのビングループと仏アルストムは６日、ハノイの都市鉄道網拡張に向け、車両２００編成の供給と関連技術移転で合意したと発表した。

• 合意に基づき、最初の８３編成はアルストムの仏施設で設計・製造する。いずれも５両編成で、完全自動無人運転に対応する。

• 残る１１７編成はビングループがベトナムで製造・組み立てを行い、アルストムが技術的な専門知識、製造設備面の支援、主要部品を提供する。

• 納入時期は明らかにされていない。

• 都市鉄道はベトナムの鉄道市場で最も急成長している分野の一つで、主要都市のハノイとホーチミンでは１２路線が計画されている。

• ハノイの都市鉄道網は２０４５年までに１８路線、総延長９７９キロに拡張する計画だ。

items.title: US EIA raises Q4 oil price forecast to USD 105 amid Middle East supply risks, diesel market tightness
items.summary: The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) has raised its forecast for Brent crude oil prices for the fourth quarter of 2026 to an average of USD 105 per barrel, citing continued constraints on ...
items.body:
US EIA raises Q4 oil price forecast to USD 105 amid Middle East supply risks, diesel market tightness The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) has raised its forecast for Brent crude oil prices for the fourth quarter of 2026 to an average of USD 105 per barrel, citing continued constraints on Middle East oil flows, attacks on energy infrastructure and tight diesel markets.
ANI | Updated: 07-10-2026 15:02 IST | Created: 07-10-2026 15:02 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) has raised its forecast for Brent crude oil prices for the fourth quarter of 2026 to an average of USD 105 per barrel, citing continued constraints on Middle East oil flows, attacks on energy infrastructure and tight diesel markets. The US EIA raised the Q4 Brent forecast by USD 14 per barrel from the previous month's outlook. The EIA said oil flows from the Middle East are expected to remain constrained through the fourth quarter, although regional shut-in production in September was the lowest since hostilities began.
The agency expects production and exports from the region to gradually increase as convoys through the Strait of Hormuz, bypass routes and increased ship-to-ship transfers help restore oil flows. However, it warned that attacks on the East-West pipeline in Saudi Arabia highlight the potential for continued volatility in physical oil supplies and crude prices. The EIA also pointed to tightness in diesel markets as an additional source of upward pressure on crude oil prices, as refiners increase crude processing to meet demand for diesel.
Despite the near-term price pressure, the EIA expects the oil market to ease next year, forecasting Brent crude to average USD 84 per barrel in 2027. US retail fuel prices also rose sharply in September. Average gasoline prices reached USD 4.35 per gallon, while diesel prices averaged USD 6.29 per gallon, driven by higher crude oil prices and rising refining margins. The EIA expects US diesel prices to average about USD 4.50 per gallon in 2027, while gasoline prices are projected to average just below USD 3.60 per gallon.
The outlook also highlighted persistent weakness in US distillate inventories. East Coast distillate inventories were 32 per cent below their five-year seasonal average in September and are expected to remain around 20 per cent below the 2021-2025 average through the upcoming winter. Meanwhile, the EIA expects Henry Hub natural gas prices to average USD 3.16 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) in 2027, down 9 per cent from 2026. The decline is expected to be driven by higher-than-average inventories, supported by rising production that offsets increased liquefied natural gas exports.
The EIA said the forecast was finalised using market inputs available as of October 1 and does not incorporate developments announced after that date, including additional energy supplies following the G7's October 2 announcement. (ANI)

items.title: Gold slides to two-month low as robust dollar, yields add pressure
items.author: Pablo Sinha
items.creator: Pablo Sinha
items.summary: Gold declined to a two-month low on Wednesday, pressured by a strong US dollar and Treasury yields, while investors awaited the minutes of the Federal Reserve's September meeting to gauge the implications for the central bank's next policy steps.
items.body:
Gold declined to a two-month low on Wednesday, pressured by a strong US dollar and Treasury yields, while investors awaited [USN:L6N45S0TH TEXT:"the minutes"] of the Federal Reserve's September meeting to gauge the implications for the central bank's next policy steps.
Spot gold fell 1.6% to $4,096.13 per ounce by 9:20 a.m. EDT (1320 GMT), touching its lowest level since August 5. US gold futures for December delivery declined 1.6% to $4,121.70.
The US dollar index (.DXY) climbed 0.7%, making greenback-denominated gold more expensive for holders of other currencies, and 10-year US Treasury yields were at an over two-decade high.
"The market is still pricing in at least one rate hike before year end. So I think the message is rates are going to continue to be higher for longer, and that's keeping yields and the dollar underpinned," said Peter Grant, vice president and senior metals strategist at Zaner Metals.
Markets are largely expecting the Fed to keep interest rates on hold later this month, but are still pricing an 84% chance of a hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch tool.
Kansas City Fed President [USN:S0N3XI00P TEXT:"Jeff Schmid"] said further interest rate increases may be needed to curb inflation, while San Francisco Fed President [USN:L6N45S13A TEXT:"Mary Daly"] said the future policy path would depend on whether inflationary pressures continue.
Higher interest rates diminish the attractiveness of non-yielding gold.
The minutes of the Fed's September meeting are due at 2:00 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT).
Meanwhile, oil prices rose on continued Middle East supply risks and a storm heading for oil-producing regions in the United States.
"Official gold demand is the main supporting factor. I think we could see one more test to the downside, perhaps as low as $4,000, and then a recovery into year-end with potential to reach $4,400," Grant added.
[USN:L1N45T01W TEXT:"China's central bank"] stepped up its gold purchases in September, extending its buying streak to a 23rd consecutive month, official data showed.
Spot silver eased 2.9% to $59.89 per ounce, platinum fell 4.8% to $1,620.38, and palladium lost 4.2% to $1,122.75.

items.title: Californians blast Trump remark that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles, San Diego
items.author: CNA
items.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom denounced the Republican Trump as "deranged and dangerous".
items.body:

World

Californians blast Trump remark that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles, San Diego

California Governor Gavin Newsom denounced the Republican Trump as "deranged and dangerous".

US President Donald Trump speaks to reporters after arriving aboard the Marine One helicopter on his South Lawn helipad at the White House in Washington, DC, on Oct 6, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst)

07 Oct 2026 10:06AM
(Updated: 07 Oct 2026 10:19AM)

FAST

LOS ANGELES: President Donald Trump suggested to a crowd of his supporters in Nebraska that Iran could "take out" a major US city like Los Angeles or San Diego , drawing a swift rebuke from California's Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans.
Trump, speaking at a political rally in the state's farm belt on Monday (Oct 5), discussed American wartime economic sacrifices and said he was determined to "see a tremendous victory, because it verifies all the things we did."
"And again, remember, with the war, it's just artificial, it's a little bit high, it's a small price to pay," he told the crowd in Grand Island, Nebraska, apparently referring to rising prices of fuel, fertiliser and other products attributed to energy market disruptions from the war.
"It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let 'em take out Los Angeles, let 'em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it's going to be over with very soon," he said.

"It's essentially almost over with," Trump went on. "But it's going to end very soon, and it's going to end one way or the other."
On Tuesday, the White House dismissed criticism of the remark. "The media freakout over President Trump’s comments is not rooted in reality. He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped," White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung said in a social media post. 
"America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money."
Trump has shrugged off cost-of-living concerns stemming from the Iran conflict before, and he previously downplayed his concerns about the potential for Iran or its allies to launch an attack on US soil.
EARLY VOTING UNDERWAY IN CALIFORNIA The comment in rural Nebraska, a state Trump won with more than 55 per cent of the vote in the 2024 presidential election, targeted Democratic-run cities in California, a solidly Democratic state the president often criticises.
Monday's comments prompted a backlash from California officials.
California Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, denounced the Republican president as "deranged and dangerous".
"After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego," he wrote on X.
Newsom, who has positioned himself as a major political foil to Trump and is seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, juxtaposed a video clip of Trump in Nebraska with mention of the president's previous rhetoric to justify deploying US military troops to Los Angeles and other cities to fight crime and enforce immigration.

Related:

Commentary: Why a booming economy is not helping Trump

Commentary: Who in Iran can make a deal with the US – and make it stick?

California's early voting for the November midterm elections started on Monday. The president's Republican Party has hoped to win more races in the state in recent years, including this year's gubernatorial election.
Newsom championed the redrawing of California's congressional map last year to favour Democrats in this year's election after Trump pushed for conservative-led Texas to redraw its map to boost Republicans.
One of the Republicans running in a competitive race in a redrawn California district near San Diego, Jim Desmond, distanced himself from Trump's remarks.
"I vehemently disagree with President Trump’s comments. America must stand up to Iran and defend our interests, but the first responsibility of our Commander in Chief is to protect the American people and our homeland," he wrote on X. 
"No American city is expendable, and no American family should ever be treated as collateral damage."
US Representative Kevin Kiley, an independent who caucuses with Republicans and is running for re-election in a competitive race in northern California, said in a statement that Trump's comment was "unhelpful".
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, a Democrat, said in a statement that Trump's comment "could potentially compromise our safety".
Appearing on MS Now on Tuesday, Bass disputed Cheung's assertion that Trump's comments were being misinterpreted by a "freaked out" media.
"Well, I'm not sure that he understands that we can hear what the president said," Bass countered, adding that Cheung's defence of Trump's remarks "has no connection to the words that came out of the president's mouth".
Los Angeles and San Diego rank as the largest and second-largest cities in California by population.
More than 115,000 active-duty service members are also stationed in San Diego, including Naval Base San Diego, the largest on the US West Coast.
"My constituents - including many active duty service members, veterans, and their families - are not acceptable collateral damage in Trump’s stupid war," US Representative Sara Jacobs, a Democrat, said in a social media post.

Related:

In reversal, Trump to pay for political ads about himself

Source: Reuters/ec

items.title: エネルギー業界、代替輸送ルート巡る投資検討強化　資金負担が課題
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Shadia Nasralla　Stephanie Kelly　Robert Harvey

[ロンドン ６日 ロイター...
items.body:
エネルギー業界、代替輸送ルート巡る投資検討強化　資金負担が課題
11:05 配信

オマーンのムサンダムから見たホルムズ海峡。１０月２日撮影（２０２６年　ロイター）

Shadia Nasralla　Stephanie Kelly　Robert Harvey

[ロンドン ６日 ロイター] - イランでの戦争による混乱を受け、エネルギー業界では効率性を重視した「ジャスト・イン・タイム」のサプライチェーン戦略を見直し、ペルシャ湾や紅海を迂回する代替輸送ルートへの投資を検討する動きが強まっている。ただ具体的な資金負担が課題だ。

フランスのトタルエナジーズのパトリック・プヤンヌ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「今回の危機から得られた最大の教訓は、生産だけでなく輸出についても考える必要があるということだ」と述べ、業界は「ジャスト・イン・タイム」から「ジャスト・イン・ケース（万一に備える）」への発想転換が必要だとの認識を示した。

プヤンヌ氏は、イラクからシリアへ通じるパイプライン計画への参画や、ホルムズ海峡を迂回してアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）のフジャイラ港へ原油を輸送するパイプライン網の輸送能力倍増に向けた投資計画を改めて表明。「こうしたインフラ整備に参加する必要があることは明らかだ」と強調した。

英ＢＰのメグ・オニールＣＥＯは、米コノコフィリップスおよびトルコ国営ＴＰＡＯと進めるキルクーク油田再開発により、新たな北部輸出ルートの選択肢が広がったと指摘した。

オニール氏は「イラク政府が代替輸出ルートの確保に非常に積極的に取り組んでいることは承知している」と述べた。しかしそれがＢＰ株主の資金を投じるべき案件かどうかについては慎重な見方を示して「他の投資家には適しているかもしれない」とだけ語った。

米シェブロンのマイク・ワースＣＥＯは、イラク政府との間で西クルナ２油田およびナシリヤ油田への参入交渉の進展を楽観視した。同社は今年初め、原油をトルコのジェイハン港またはシリアのバニヤス港へ輸送する新規パイプライン建設の可能性を調査するため、イラク政府と初期合意を締結している。

もっともワース氏は、資金の大部分は他の投資家が負担する必要があるとくぎを刺した上で「こうした案件に自社資本を大量投入することは一般的ではない。実現する場合は複数企業によるコンソーシアムの一員として参加することになるだろう」と付け加えた。

またクウェート石油公社（ＫＰＣ）のシャイフ・ナワフ・アルサバＣＥＯは、サウジアラビアおよびＵＡＥと、それぞれの港湾へつながる新たなパイプラインについて協議していることを明らかにした一方で、産油国だけでなく輸入国も費用負担を担うべきだと訴えた。「生産国に全ての責任を負わせて『必要な投資を全て行い、全てを供給可能にしなければならない』と言うことはできない。これは共同の責任だ」と主張している。

items.author: CNA

In interview, US Vice President Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war

Vance said any agreement would require Iran to reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity, rather than offer assurances of future drawdowns.

US Vice President JD Vance is interviewed by Reuters reporter Jacob Bogage before a campaign rally at Fairbanks International Airport in Fairbanks, Alaska, on Oct 5, 2026. (Photo: Jacquelyn Martin/Pool via REUTERS)

FAST

FAIRBANKS: US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries’ seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how Tehran makes decisions in negotiations.
Vance, a longtime sceptic of US involvement in foreign wars, has taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in September that quickly fell apart. The war has jolted global energy markets and become a political liability for President Donald Trump and fellow Republicans ahead of November midterm elections. 
Speaking on Monday after a campaign trip in Alaska, Vance said any agreement would require Iran to reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity, rather than offer assurances of future nuclear drawdowns.
"If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60 per cent enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don't build highly enriched fuel. That's a very basic threshold issue," Vance said.
"I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their enrichment capacity."
Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz , a vital global energy shipping route. Trump rejected Tehran's latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterms.
Vance said the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions.
"We're not going to trade words for actions," Vance said. 
UNCLEAR HOW IRAN MAKES DECISIONS: VANCE Complicating matters, Vance said Washington is uncertain who makes decisions in Tehran.
Vance said the US was in talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. But it was unclear how much authority they wield within Iran's power structure, he said, after joint US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. 
"One of the things we picked up on is it's not totally clear how their country makes decisions," Vance said. Separately, Trump said on Tuesday his "biggest problem" is no one knows who is running Iran. 
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Sunday that US officials are well aware of who their Iranian counterparts are and how Iran's decision-making system works.
"The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials," Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference.

Related:

Commentary: Who in Iran can make a deal with the US – and make it stick?

White House denies Trump suggested Iran should 'take out' US cities

Vance told Reuters he has held personal conversations with field commanders to gauge battlefield conditions. He dismissed concerns over critical munitions shortages and added that while Iranian troops are periodically able to strike commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, they are largely unable to prevent energy exports through the waterway.
The war - and its US$3 billion monthly price tag - has become a key issue on the campaign trail. Higher energy prices have put Trump and Republicans on the defensive in competitive states that will decide control of Congress. 
Vance has sought to temper criticism of Trump’s handling of the conflict, telling voters they should not let that issue keep them from backing Republicans in next month's elections.
In Alaska, Vance rallied for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is locked in a tight reelection battle with Democratic challenger Mary Peltola. Trump carried Alaska by 13 percentage points in 2024, but rising everyday costs have put the state in play.
Before speaking with Reuters, Vance focused much of his speech on affordability concerns, especially around energy. Alaska's remote locale makes consumer goods more expensive, and energy production is a key industry.
Rally attendees roared when Sullivan nearly introduced Vance as the president of the US, rather than the vice president. Vance is seen as a leading Republican contender to succeed Trump in the White House. 
Vance told Reuters afterward that he had not decided whether to seek the presidency in 2028.
"I'm inherently a procrastinator," he said. "I really haven't thought about it much."

Related:

Commentary: Why a booming economy is not helping Trump

Trump moves to cut diesel costs with order on tax-free fuel

Source: Reuters/ec

items.title: Houthis attack Aden airport as fighting intensifies in Yemen
items.author: Enas Alashray, Mohammed Ghobari, Timour Azhari
items.creator: Enas Alashray, Mohammed Ghobari, Timour Azhari
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis attacked Aden's international airport with ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones.
items.body:
Yemen's Houthis attacked Aden's international airport with ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones on Wednesday, the country's Transport Ministry said, as fighting between the Iran-aligned group and Saudi-backed government forces intensified.
Battles have focused in recent days on areas around the [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"], a shipping route that has become more crucial for energy exports since the conflict between the US and Iran restricted trade through the Strait of Hormuz.
This week, Yemeni government forces with Saudi-led coalition air support [USN:L8N45M1W0 TEXT:"launched a counter-offensive"] to recapture strategic territory near the strait and around the town of Mocha that the Houthis had captured in September, but it is unclear if their advance will hold.
The fighting, a spillover from the wider US-Iran conflict , has revived a [USN:L6N45S0PX TEXT:"complex 12-year war"] in Yemen that led to one of the worst humanitarian crises globally and fragmented the Arab world's most impoverished country. The number of people displaced since the latest round of fighting began has risen to more than 200,000, the International Organization for Migration [USN:L6N45T0PU TEXT:"said on Wednesday"].
"People are running for their lives and finding nowhere safe to go," said IOM Director General Amy Pope, who called for more funding amid rising needs for food and shelter. Both sides allege that hundreds of people have been killed in fighting, without providing details. The UN says three in four families are going hungry in parts of Yemen.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted infrastructure including airports, oil refineries and pipelines in Saudi Arabia, a US ally.
On Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile north of the Saudi capital Riyadh. It said it was tracking the launch platform over Houthi-controlled Sanaa and would destroy it, but gave no details of casualties or damage.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a statement that the group had targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with several drones. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of an attack on the airport.
BATTLES OVER THE STRAIT Any Houthi stranglehold on the Strait could threaten shipping or global oil flows, and Saudi Arabia has been seeking international assistance to repel the Houthis. Turkey is sending mainly [USN:L6N45T0IX TEXT:"defensive and technical support"], two officials said on Wednesday, after the NATO member and Pakistan pledged to implement a collective defence commitment under their [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"newly formed alliance"].
Fighting on the western front remains concentrated in the Dhubab district overlooking Bab el-Mandeb, with pro-government forces attempting an advance in the strategic hills to the east of that coastal plain, Yemeni military and government sources said. Fierce clashes have taken place, with the Houthis claiming they have repelled attacks.
On Monday the Yemeni government said it had reached Mocha, which sits at a junction with a supply route to the critical battleground of Taiz, but the claim had been premature, according to Yemeni military officials on the ground and analysts.
Hussam Radman, a researcher at the Sanaa Center, a Yemen-focused think tank, said [USN:L1N45S0Y9 TEXT:"pro-government forces"] including the Giants Brigade, a conservative Sunni Salafi group that has led the counter-offensive, are trying to take control of Dhubab and to advance in the mountains to its east.
Control of those highlands would allow for government forces to more easily advance up the rest of the coast, he said.
AIRPORT STRUCK Along Yemen's coast to the east, one missile landed near the runway at Aden International Airport minutes before a flight from Cairo was due to land, the Transport Ministry said. Authorities cancelled the landing and diverted the aircraft to Jeddah, while two planes on the runway were moved away from the area over fears of further strikes, it added. There was no immediate comment from the Houthis.
Aden International Airport is the main international gateway for parts of Yemen outside Houthi control.
The Houthis, who control much of Yemen's north, seized the capital Sanaa in 2014, prompting a military coalition led by Saudi Arabia, fearful of rival Iran's influence in Yemen and chaos on its borders, to intervene. A UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted heavy fighting, but it did not lead to a lasting settlement.
The Saudi-led coalition accuses Iran of arming, training and funding the Houthis. The group, mountain fighters who have emerged as a force of tens of thousands with missiles and drones that threatens the region, denies being part of Iran's Middle East proxy network, and says it develops its own weapons. Tehran also rejects the allegations.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched towards the southwestern Saudi city of Khamis Mushait, Saudi state television reported.
In a separate statement, Saree said the Houthis had attacked Abha International Airport and an airbase in Khamis Mushait with ballistic missiles and drones. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm an attack on Abha airport.

items.title: In interview, US Vice President Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war
items.author: Jacob Bogage
items.creator: Jacob Bogage
items.summary: US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries’ seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how Tehran makes decisions in negotiations.
items.body:
US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries’ seven-month war , even as Washington was unsure how Tehran makes decisions in negotiations.
Vance, a longtime skeptic of US involvement in foreign wars, has [USN:L8N42P1PE TEXT:"taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement"] to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in June that quickly fell apart. The war has jolted global energy markets and become a political liability for US President Donald Trump and fellow Republicans ahead of November midterm elections.
Vance said on Monday after a campaign trip in Alaska that any agreement would require Iran to reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity, rather than offer assurances of future nuclear drawdowns.
"If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don't build highly enriched fuel. That's a very basic threshold issue," Vance said.
"I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their enrichment capacity."
Washington's "requests and ideas" about Iran's nuclear program are at odds with Tehran's demands, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday when asked about Vance's comment that Tehran must cut enrichment to end the war.
Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. Trump rejected Tehran's latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterms.
Vance said the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions.
"We're not going to trade words for actions," Vance said.
Trump and administration officials have consistently called for blocking Iran's path to building a nuclear weapon, including the destruction or removal of its highly enriched uranium stockpile that can be used for a nuclear bomb.
The message has been less clear on whether Iran, under a possible peace deal, might be permitted to maintain some enriched uranium, at levels below what would be necessary to quickly build a weapon.
TEHRAN'S RED LINE The senior Iranian official said no negotiations had taken place with the US about Iran's nuclear program, and Washington must first meet Tehran's conditions before nuclear talks can start.
The official said US recognition of Iran's right to nuclear enrichment is Tehran's red line, which he said "it will not show flexibility on in any way." However, he said details of enrichment can be discussed later.
"Vance's comments are Washington's ideas and requests. ... Americans are free to make requests and have ideas, but they are at odds with Iran's demands," said the senior Iranian official, who is involved in indirect negotiations with the US.
Israel, the US and other Western states have long accused Iran of seeking nuclear weapons, including pointing to its move to enrich uranium to 60%, far higher than needed for civilian uses and closer to the 90% needed for a weapon. Iran denies seeking nuclear weapons; Iranian authorities have said that Tehran could agree to dilute its most highly enriched uranium.
UNCLEAR HOW IRAN MAKES DECISIONS: VANCE Complicating matters, Vance said Washington is uncertain who makes decisions in Tehran.
Vance said the US was in talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. But it was unclear how much authority they wield within Iran's power structure, he said, after joint US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
"One of the things we picked up on is it's not totally clear how their country makes decisions," Vance said. Separately, Trump said on Tuesday that his "[USN:S0N44P02O TEXT:"biggest problem"]" is no one knows who is running Iran.
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Sunday that US officials are well aware of who their Iranian counterparts are and how Iran's decision-making system works.
"The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials," Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference.
Vance told Reuters he has held personal conversations with field commanders to gauge battlefield conditions. He dismissed concerns over critical munitions shortages and added that while Iranian troops are periodically able to strike commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, they are largely unable to prevent energy exports through the waterway.
Vance declined to say whether he was leading peace talks, though he is frequently cited as the White House's top negotiator.
"We're certainly involved," he said. "Ultimately, the president of the United States is driving things."
The war — [USN:L6N4530XO TEXT:"and its $3 billion monthly price tag"] — has become a key issue on the campaign trail. Higher energy prices have put Trump and Republicans on the defensive in competitive states that will decide control of Congress.
Vance has sought to temper criticism of Trump’s handling of the conflict, telling voters they should not let that issue keep them from backing Republicans in next month's elections.
In Alaska , [USN:L6N45R01A TEXT:"Vance rallied for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan"], who is locked in a tight reelection battle with Democratic challenger Mary Peltola. Trump carried Alaska by 13 percentage points in 2024, but rising everyday costs have put the state in play.
Before speaking with Reuters, Vance focused much of his speech on affordability concerns, especially around energy. Alaska's remote locale makes consumer goods more expensive, and energy production is a key industry.
Rally attendees roared when Sullivan nearly introduced Vance as US president, rather than vice president. Vance is seen as a leading Republican contender to succeed Trump.
Vance told Reuters afterward that he had not decided whether to seek the presidency in 2028.
"I'm inherently a procrastinator," he said. "I really haven't thought about it much."

items.title: Kotak, IndusInd, Axis Bank shares jump on strong Q2 business updates
items.author: Subrata Panda
items.summary: Lenders report strong credit and deposit growth aided by FCNR(B) inflows, though analysts flag concerns over CASA momentum ...
items.body: Shares of Kotak Mahindra Bank, IndusInd Bank and Axis Bank rose sharply on Tuesday after the lenders reported robust growth in advances and deposits in their quarterly business updates. This growth was aided by healthy mobilisation of FCNR(B) deposits. Kotak Mahindra Bank’s shares jumped 3.59 per cent to close at ₹431.25 on the BSE, while IndusInd Bank gained 2.79 per cent to end at ₹906.95. Axis Bank’s shares rose 2.01 per cent to ₹1,248.50. However, RBL Bank’s shares closed 0.72 per cent lower at ₹414 on the BSE compared with the previous day’s close. On Monday, Kotak Mahindra Bank reported robust net advances (period-end) growth of 25 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) and 13 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q). Excluding advances linked to FCNR(B) deposits, loan growth remained firm at around 21 per cent Y-o-Y and 10 per cent Q-o-Q. Deposits grew 23 per cent Y-o-Y and 14 per cent Q-o-Q, aided by FCNR(B) inflows. Excluding these, deposit growth was more measured at 13 per cent Y-o-Y and 4 per cent Q-o-Q. Current account savings account (CASA) balances grew 11 per cent Y-o-Y and 8 per cent Q-o-Q. The bank mobilised $5.78 billion through FCNR(B) deposits during the quarter. Axis Bank, India’s third-largest private sector lender, said its deposits grew 5.8 per cent sequentially and 20.7 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹14.52 trillion as of September 30, while gross advances rose 8.8 per cent Q-o-Q and 22.7 per cent YoY to ₹13.85 trillion. The lender mobilised $10.62 billion (₹1.02 trillion) in FCNR(B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India’s swap facility introduced earlier this year.   “While the outcome is good on the loan growth front, the question is sustainability plus core deposit growth around 12-13 per cent for Kotak (Mahindra Bank) and Axis (Bank) isn’t that great. That goes to show that eventually loan growth will have to come down from current levels. CASA growth is also 10 to 11 per cent similar to HDFC Bank showing the pressure that exists in CASA across the system. CASA ratios continue to decline even on core deposit growth basis”, said Suresh Ganapathy, MD&Head - Financial Services Research, Macquarie Capital.  Meanwhile, IndusInd Bank’s net advances grew 11.2 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹3.62 trillion as of September 30, 2026, outpacing the 10.1 per cent growth in deposits to ₹4.29 trillion. IndusInd Bank’s CASA ratio declined to 28 per cent from 30.7 per cent a year earlier and 29.4 per cent in June. The lender mobilised $3.51 billion in FCNR(B) deposits under the RBI’s deposit swap facility, with outstanding loans of about ₹16,564 crore extended from its GIFT City branch against these deposits as of September-end. And, RBL Bank’s total deposits rose 34 per cent Y-o-Y to around ₹1.56 trillion in the quarter ended September 30 (Q2FY27), while gross advances grew 40 per cent to around ₹1.43 trillion. (Disclosure: Entities controlled by the Kotak family have a significant holding in Business Standard Pvt Ltd)

US and China discuss reciprocal visits to nuclear sites: Reports

The idea of reciprocal visits was initially raised by China in meetings with US officials this year and visits to US Department of Energy national laboratories and equivalent Chinese facilities were discussed, CNN said, citing a source familiar with the matter.

FAST

The United States has discussed starting reciprocal visits to nuclear sites with China, and plans to continue pushing in meetings in the coming months, CNN reported on Tuesday (Oct 6), citing sources familiar with the matter.

The idea of reciprocal visits was initially raised by China in meetings with US officials this year and visits to US Department of Energy national laboratories and equivalent Chinese facilities were discussed, CNN said, citing a source.

The discussions between US and Chinese officials have mainly been on the sidelines of gatherings by the UN Security Council's five veto-wielding permanent members, CNN reported.

Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The White House and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment outside business hours.

US President Donald Trump called for trilateral arms control negotiations between the US, China and Russia when he met President Xi Jinping last month. However, the two leaders did not discuss the possibility of nuclear site visits during their talks, the CNN report said, citing a US official.

Beijing has said its nuclear arsenal is far smaller than those of Russia and the US, something it says makes its participation in such talks unnecessary.

Another meeting between Trump and Xi is widely considered likely this year, potentially at November's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China or during Group of 20 meetings in the US in December.

By the time the two leaders meet again, it is expected that further lower-level discussions on possible nuclear site visits will have taken place, CNN said.

items.author: CNA

Francis Halzen wins Nobel physics prize for Antarctic 'ghost particle' hunt

FAST

STOCKHOLM: The Belgian-American Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work creating an Antarctic observatory of ice to detect high-energy neutrinos, elusive subatomic particles that can reveal otherwise inaccessible information about the cosmos.
Halzen, 82, realised that pristine ice at the South Pole could be used to track such neutrinos, sometimes known as "ghost particles" for the way they pass through the Earth without a trace, only interacting with matter extremely rarely.
"The messengers bring information from the cosmos," Eva Olsson, of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, told a press conference. "They open the door to distant galaxies and tell us about the processes of exploding stars."
HALZEN HAILED FOR DETECTING "MESSENGERS FROM THE COSMOS" The interactions registered by the IceCube observatory provide information about how high-energy neutrinos are created and may even reveal previously unknown phenomena, the Academy said.

In 2014, the US-based Smithsonian magazine dubbed Halzen "Neutrino Man" when giving him one of its Ingenuity Awards, acclaiming him for an "amazing experiment (that) heralds the beginning of a new era in astronomy".
It even published a comic illustrating his life: "How One Physicist’s Pursuit of the Cosmos Took Off in Antarctica".
The observatory - in effect a telescope that shows neutrinos instead of light - is set in a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice, which extends to a depth of 2,500 metres below the surface near the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station.
More than 5,000 sensors await blips from the nearly massless high-energy neutrinos, which unlike other particles do not lose energy or change direction, in the hope of tracing their paths back to exploding stars, gamma-ray bursts, and cataclysmic phenomena involving black holes and neutron stars. They can expect to register about one per day.
Halzen, a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in the United States, first presented his idea in 1988 for capturing neutrino traces at the South Pole, but the project was not completed until 2011.
"I have to emphasise how lucky I was because, when we started this project, everybody realised this was maybe a good idea, but very few thought it would work, including myself," Halzen told the press conference by telephone.
Neutrinos are electrically neutral, undisturbed by any magnetic field, which means that, in contrast to electromagnetic waves such as visible light, the direction from which they arrive points directly back to their source.

Related:

Medicine Nobel goes to US-German trio for pioneering light-based control of cells

FRUITS OF HALZEN'S RESEARCH YET TO COME The observatory has determined that high-energy neutrinos originate within but also far outside our own Milky Way galaxy, setting in motion an interstellar quest to find the objects and processes that create them.
Through the long winter at the South Pole, when bringing anything in or out is difficult as temperatures below minus 50°C (minus 58 Fahrenheit) preclude even aircraft landing, a skeleton crew of "winterovers" has to maintain the observatory.
The station, home to many other activities, can house as many as 150 people and has an industrial kitchen, dining room, gym and even a greenhouse. Last week it celebrated the sun's return above the horizon after six months of night with a six-hole ice-golf tournament.
An extension, IceCube-Gen2, encompassing 8 cubic kilometres of ice, is planned to become operational in 2033 and will be able to detect 10 times as many neutrinos, including much weaker ones.
Halzen said the main fruits of his work were yet to be seen and that it was too early to say exactly what it could reveal about the universe.
"The real excitement is that I cannot answer that question yet," he said. "This is just an introduction to the science, the astronomy is still to come."
WINNERS FROM EINSTEIN TO BOHR AND THE CURIES Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever congratulated Halzen on the recognition of "a life dedicated to unraveling the greatest secrets of the cosmos through its most minuscule manifestations".
The physics laureate receives an award of 12 million Swedish crowns (US$1.2 million). Past winners include several other neutrino research pioneers, for instance Japan's Takaaki Kajita and Arthur McDonald from Canada in 2015.
The Nobel Prizes were established under the will of Swedish inventor and entrepreneur Alfred Nobel, whose fortune was built in part on the invention of dynamite.
Physics was prominent in Nobel's will and the prize remains one of the discipline's highest distinctions. Over the decades, it has recognised discoveries that have fundamentally reshaped humanity's understanding of the universe.
Among past laureates are some of the most celebrated figures in science, including Albert Einstein, Marie and Pierre Curie, Max Planck and Niels Bohr, whose work helped establish the foundations of modern physics.
The prize is presented in Stockholm on Dec 10, the anniversary of Nobel's death.

Source: Reuters/fh

items.title: Police fire teargas as French school protests cause 'heaviest toll in decades'
items.author: Tilman Blasshofer, Cecile Mantovani, Lucien Libert
items.creator: Tilman Blasshofer, Cecile Mantovani, Lucien Libert
items.summary: Police fired tear gas at protesters outside French high schools on Tuesday as students, teachers and parents took to the streets on the biggest day of what Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu described as the most violent school protests in decades.
items.body:
Police fired tear gas at protesters outside French high schools on Tuesday as students, teachers and parents took to the streets on the biggest day of what Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu described as the most violent school protests in decades.
The protests, in which a teenager lost a hand on Monday, were the latest manifestation of public anger in a country where the far right and far left are surging ahead of a presidential election in the spring.
The government is under pressure to tame public debt amid weak growth, and has struggled with basic tasks such as passing a budget since President Emmanuel Macron's allies lost their majority in a 2024 parliamentary vote.
Lecornu told lawmakers at least 215 teenagers and 85 school staff had so far been injured in clashes, "the heaviest toll in decades paid by the school system". His office said more than 700 police officers were also hurt.
Macron has convened Lecornu and other senior ministers at an emergency meeting on Tuesday, broadcaster BFM reported.
In Marseille and Nantes, protesters held up signs reading "The state has killed national education". In Toulouse, parents linked arms at the front of a march through the city.
In Strasbourg, Lyon, Rennes and Paris, the demonstrations at times turned violent, with police firing tear gas and protesters lighting fires in the streets and hurling projectiles.
The Paris police said the clashes there had come about when some 300 people attempted to face off against security forces, adding that the protest was generally unfolding well elsewhere.
By late afternoon they said they were still clashing with a small contingent of people. Three storefronts had been damaged.
The protests began in September in the deprived suburbs of Paris, before spreading nationwide.
"There is such a gap between the elites and us," said Hugo Vetzel, a recent high-school graduate in Strasbourg.
The High School Students Union said more than half of France's high schools were blockaded or would close for the day. Some local education authorities have tried to move classes online.
Students complain about schools facing basic maintenance problems, from water leaks to rat infestations.
THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS Rights groups, students and parent groups have accused authorities of using disproportionate force against minors. The government says the protest movement has been hijacked by outsiders and in some places deteriorated into urban violence.
France's interior ministry said 6,100 people have been arrested since the protests began, the overwhelming majority of them minors. More than 1,800 people are being prosecuted for unspecified crimes, including 1,483 minors, the justice ministry said.
A teenager's hand was blown off as high-school protesters clashed with riot police in northern France on Monday. The regional newspaper La Voix du Nord said the 15-year-old lost his hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police grenade intended to be non-lethal.
"They want to divide the young people into good and bad protesters," said Omar Slaouti, a high-school teacher in Argenteuil, a northwestern suburb of Paris.
Young people were torching things to make their voices heard, he said, including those angry about being excluded from the education system.
"If there were no trash cans on fire, the government would not have stepped back and become aware of the issues at stake. I would add that one can of course regret this but the government alone is responsible for this."
Six months before an election to replace Macron, his government and far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally party have accused hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) lawmakers and mayors of stoking the unrest. LFI denies the accusation.
"All the young people are in the streets. Everywhere there aren't police, everything is going smoothly," said Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's presidential candidate.
PRIME MINISTER PROMISES A RESPONSE Lecornu has ordered his ministers to tackle the students' leading demands. Those include ensuring absent teachers are replaced, reviewing the length of the 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. school day and the need for longer lunch breaks.
The government will also look at repairs needed to ageing school buildings, said Lecornu, who demanded ministers send in their first proposals by the end of October.
Parent Emilie Lhomme said at a protest outside the Helene Boucher school in Paris that the government's words were not enough: "That's all fine and dandy, but that's not what's going to change the daily lives of our children," she said.
Finding spare cash to implement educational reforms will be difficult.
The government is under pressure to try to narrow a ballooning budget deficit as investor concerns about France's growing debt, weak growth and reluctance to rein in spending push the cost of borrowing higher. The yield on [USN:L8N45O0YO TEXT:"France's 10-year bonds"] briefly hit a 24-year high of over 5% last week.
The surge in French borrowing costs has started to spill into the broader euro area, with the [USN:L6N45S0D2 TEXT:"sliding euro currency"] the latest alarm bell for policy makers. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said on Tuesday there was no need for the [USN:S8N3XB0C2 TEXT:"European Central Bank"] to step in.
Le Pen, the far-right euro-sceptic populist leading the presidential race ahead of next spring's election, set out [USN:L1N45S0C4 TEXT:"plans to slash public spending if elected"], seeking to establish her fiscal credibility as the bond market crisis deepens.
French spending on education has lagged inflation and the country's students are trailing their OECD peers in overall performance, data from the href="nL8N44Z0XI" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> PISA 2025 assessment shows.

items.title: Barrick secures 15-year North Mara mining licences in Tanzania
items.author: Northern Miner Staff
items.creator: Northern Miner Staff
items.summary: The latest approval removes tenure risk, leaving Barrick to reverse a sharp first-half production decline.
items.body:
Barrick secures 15-year North Mara mining licences in Tanzania

Henry Lazenby | October 5, 2026 | 12:10 pm
Top Companies   Africa   Canada   Gold  

( Image by Twiga Partnership, Facebook. )

Tanzania has renewed Barrick Mining’s (TSX: ABX; NYSE: B) licences for the North Mara gold mine for 15 years, securing its operating tenure as the company weighs an expansion.

North Mara is a combined open-pit and underground operation about 540 km northwest of Dodoma and 20 km south of the Kenyan border. Barrick owns 84% and Tanzania holds the remaining 16%. The mine produced 249,000 attributable oz. last year.

“Relations at North Mara mine have strengthened since Barrick took over,” Tarime district commissioner Maj. Edward Gowele said in Barrick’s Monday release. “Residents now really view the mine as a community partner.”

North Mara’s two special mining licences were last renewed for 15 years in 2012. The latest approval removes that separate tenure risk, leaving Barrick to reverse a sharp first-half production decline, meet North Mara’s attributable 2026 guidance of 200,000 to 230,000 oz. and decide whether to expand the North Mara-Bulyanhulu complex.

Barrick’s Toronto-traded shares were down 1% at $56.84 (US$39.87) apiece by mid-Monday, after tracking 20% higher over the past 12 months. Bids have tested $42.62 and $74.00 over the same period.

Production test

Attributable output fell 47% to 68,000 oz. in the first half from 129,000 oz. a year earlier. All-in sustaining costs rose 79% to US$2,283 per oz. from US$1,272 per ounce. Barrick cited lower grades at North Mara among the factors raising company-wide second-quarter costs.

Barrick maintained North Mara’s guidance at 200,000 to 230,000 oz. and all-in sustaining costs of US$1,520-US$1,680 per oz. The mine must produce 132,000 to 162,000 oz. in the second half to reach that range.

North Mara output is expected to rise next year. Barrick is studying upgrades to remove processing bottlenecks and expand the North Mara-Bulyanhulu complex.

North Mara held attributable proven and probable reserves of 43 million tonnes grading 2.32 grams gold per tonne for 3.2 million oz. at the end of 2025, Barrick reported.

State reset

Barrick bought the 36% of Acacia Mining it didn’t already own in September 2019 and took direct control of North Mara. Under then-CEO Mark Bristow, it reached a settlement with Tanzania the following month and formalized it in January 2020, agreeing to pay $300 million, give the state a 16% free-carried interest in the mines and split their economic benefits equally.

The accord created Twiga Minerals to manage North Mara and Bulyanhulu. Since 2019, Barrick says its Tanzanian operations have contributed about $5.3 billion to the country, including $1.2 billion last year.

LBMA trial

The renewal comes as the London Bullion Market Association prepares for a six-week High Court trial beginning Wednesday over the deaths of two 23-year-old artisanal miners at North Mara in 2019. Their families allege Tanzanian police, private guards or both killed the men in separate incidents that July and December.

Barrick took operational control in September, between the incidents. It isn’t a defendant in the London case and declined to comment to Reuters , the news outlet reported Monday.

The claim alleges the LBMA negligently kept India-based refiner MMTC-PAMP that processed North Mara gold on its ‘good delivery list’ despite reports of abuses at the mine. The list determines which refiners’ bars are accepted in London’s wholesale bullion market.

The LBMA denies liability, saying it certifies refiners rather than mines and had no control over North Mara or Tanzanian police.

The association held about £1.4 million ($1.8 million) in reserves at the end of 2025 and could face £3 million in claimants’ legal costs before damages if it loses, Bloomberg reported on Monday.

A ruling holding the LBMA responsible could set a precedent for compensation over abuses at supplying mines and threaten its role in global gold trading, John Meyer, a mining analyst at SP Angel, said in a note on Monday. The court has stayed another 26 claims and five potential claims until after the trial, according to the LBMA.
